Keeps concrete damage away from the faces you marked as Avoid.
Off: patches may land on protected faces too.
On: protected faces stay untouched.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_detail:
Octaves of the relief noise (1 to 8, default 3). Each octave adds finer grain.
Low (1): soft, large ripples.
High (8): more fine grain on top; the change from 3 is small.
Allowed range: 0.05 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_amount:
Number of patches (0 to 500, default 5). Placement may give fewer where there is no free space.
Low (1): one patch.
High (15): the wall is covered with spalls, many of them on the edges.
Allowed range: 0 to 500.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_size_min:
Smallest size of a broken-out patch, in cm.
Low: some patches are tiny chips.
High: even the smallest patch is big.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_size_max:
Largest size of a broken-out patch, in cm.
Low: all patches stay small.
High: some patches grow large.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_lobes:
Number of overlapping blobs that make one patch outline (1 to 8, default 4).
Low (1): one rounded patch.
High (8): a large cloud-like patch with several bays.
Allowed range: 1 to 8.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_stretch:
Largest elongation of a patch (default 1.6; 1 is about round).
Low (1): a compact patch.
High (4): a long patch, like a strip of spalled cover.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_edge_bias:
How strongly the patches are pulled toward sharp edges and corners (0 to 4, default 0.25). The images use Amount 8.
Low (0): patches spread over the whole face.
High (1): nearly every patch sits on an edge or a corner.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_paint_radius:
Half-width of the damage along an open stroke (default 6 cm). Closed strokes fill their own outline instead.
Low (3 cm): a narrow groove.
High (15 cm): a wide band with a full grid of bars.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_paint_snap:
How far a stroke point may be from the surface to count (default 5 cm). The images use a stroke drawn 3 cm in front of the face.
Low (1 cm): the stroke is too far away and makes no damage.
High (5 cm): the stroke is used.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_paint_close:
A stroke whose ends are closer than this share of its length is treated as closed and filled (default 0.15; 0 = only cyclic strokes). The images use a rectangle with a gap of 9 cm in a 2 m stroke.
Low (0): the open stroke is swept as a band; the middle stays whole.
High (0.15 and more): the outline is closed and the whole area is spalled.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_depth_min:
Shallowest depth of a broken-out patch, in cm.
Low: some patches only skim the surface.
High: even the shallowest patch is deep.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_depth_max:
Deepest depth of a broken-out patch, in cm.
Low: all patches stay shallow.
High: some patches go deep; watch thin walls.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_jagged:
How ragged the outline is (Jagged, default 0.6). Resolution must be high enough to show fine raggedness.
Low (0): smooth, round lobes.
High (2): a torn outline with loose islands round the patch.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_outline_scal:
Feature size of the coarse noise that bends the outline (default 1).
Low (0.3): many small bites along the rim.
High (3): broad, smooth bulges.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_terraces:
Number of stepped layers at the rim (1 to 4, default 2): plaster skin, cover, core. The images have the bars off.
Low (1): one step from the surface to the floor.
High (4): several thin ledges; the deepest layer covers only the middle.
Allowed range: 1 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_terrace_skin:
Share of the depth taken by the outermost layer (default 0.3).
Low (0.1): a thin skin, most of the depth in the core.
High (0.8): a thick first step; the core is shallow.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_terrace_inse:
How far inside the patch each deeper layer starts, times the patch size (default 0.18).
Low (0): all layers start at the rim; one steep wall.
High (0.5): the deeper layers shrink to a small pit in the middle.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_wall_soft:
Width of the sloping transition into the cavity (default 0.35). Hidden for the Wooden wall type.
Low (0): sheer, broken walls.
High (1.5): soft, bowl-like slopes; the patch looks smaller and shallower.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_roughness:
Blend of broad ripples and fine aggregate pits (0 to 100 %, default 45 %).
Low (0 %): a smooth, wavy floor.
High (100 %): a pitted, gritty floor.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_aggregate_si:
Size of the aggregate pits and stones on the floor (default 0.8 cm).
Low (0.3 cm): fine sand-like grain.
High (3 cm): large lumps.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_thickness_ca:
Largest cut depth as a share of the local wall thickness, outside holes (default 0.45; 0 turns the cap off). The images use a 5 cm thick wall and Depth 6 to 9 cm.
Low (0.2): the cut stops at 1 cm.
High (0, off): the cut goes through the thin wall and opens a hole.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_surf_mode:
Choose Spall Surface. Procedural: Roughness / Aggregate only; Texture: Image displacement on top of the procedural spall, like the Boolean break surface.
Procedural: Roughness / Aggregate only.
Texture: Image displacement on top of the procedural spall, like the Boolean break surface.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_tex_path:
A black and white image that roughens the broken concrete. White sticks out, black sinks in.
Empty: the built-in gravel image is used.
Assigned: your own image shapes the break.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_tex_scale:
How big one repeat of the image is on the surface, in cm.
Low: small, busy texture detail.
High: large, stretched-out texture detail.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_tex_strength:
How deep the image presses into the broken concrete, in cm.
0: the image is ignored, only the built-in bumps remain.
High: deep, rough relief from the image.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_tex_edge:
Triangle size on the spall surface. 0 uses Texture Scale / 60. Increase for faster updates.
Minimum: At zero use the automatic size described above; small positive sizes produce fine, heavier geometry.
Maximum: Larger cells or edges: coarser, faster geometry that may lose small features.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_tex_offset_x:
X translation of the procedural pattern in local coordinates.
Minimum: Move the pattern toward negative X.
Maximum: Move the pattern toward positive X. Feature size is unchanged.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_tex_offset_y:
Y translation of the procedural pattern in local coordinates.
Minimum: Move the pattern toward negative Y.
Maximum: Move the pattern toward positive Y. Feature size is unchanged.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_tex_offset_z:
Z translation of the procedural pattern in local coordinates.
Minimum: Move the pattern toward negative Z.
Maximum: Move the pattern toward positive Z. Feature size is unchanged.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_hole_enable:
Enable this feature for the current source. Disable to omit it without losing its stored settings.
Off: omit hole enable while keeping its stored settings.
On: use hole enable with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_hole_chance:
Share of the patches (or painted strokes) that break through (default 0.6). The images use Amount 6.
Low (0): no holes.
High (1): every patch has a hole.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_hole_size:
Share of the patch interior that is open (default 0.45).
Low (0.2): a small opening between the bars.
High (0.9): most of the patch is open.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_hole_jagged:
How ragged the rim of the hole is (default 0.5).
Low (0): a smooth opening.
High (2): a torn, notched rim.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_crack_enable:
Enable this feature for the current source. Disable to omit it without losing its stored settings.
Off: omit crack enable while keeping its stored settings.
On: use crack enable with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_crack_amount:
Cracks from each patch (0 to 32, default 4; painted damage: per stroke section).
Low (0): no cracks.
High (12): a star of cracks round the patch.
Allowed range: 0 to 32.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_crack_length:
Shortest crack running out of a patch, in cm.
Low: some cracks are very short.
High: even the shortest crack is long.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.

Longest crack running out of a patch, in cm.
Low: all cracks stay short.
High: some cracks run far across the surface.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_crack_width:
Opening of the crack at the surface (default 0.35 cm). Narrow cracks need enough Resolution.
Low (0.1 cm): barely visible lines.
High (1.2 cm): open, dark cracks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_crack_depth:
Depth of the crack grooves (default 1 cm).
Low (0.2 cm): shallow scratches.
High (3 cm): deep, dark slots.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_crack_meande:
Side-to-side wandering of the crack path (default 0.45).
Low (0): straight cracks.
High (1.5): kinked, wandering cracks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_crack_branch:
Chance of one fork per crack (default 0.35).
Low (0): single lines.
High (1): every crack forks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_crack_interi:
Share of the cracks that start inside the spall floor instead of at the rim (default 0.3). The images use Crack Amount 8; cracks on the rough floor hardly show, so the cracks outside thin out.
Low (0): every crack starts at the rim and runs outward.
High (1): the cracks are inside the patch; none run out over the wall.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_enable:
Enable this feature for the current source. Disable to omit it without losing its stored settings.
Off: omit rebar enable while keeping its stored settings.
On: use rebar enable with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_amount:
Share of the grid lines that carry a bar (0 to 1 in use, default 0.85).
Low (0.3): most lines are empty; here only one vertical bar is left.
High (1): every grid line has a bar.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_densit:
Multiplies the number of bars by dividing both spacings (default 1).
Low (0.5): bars twice as far apart; here no full crossing is left.
High (2): a dense mesh.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_radius:
Radius of the bars (default 0.6 cm, a 12 mm bar).
Low (0.3 cm): thin wire.
High (1.2 cm): heavy bars; the dug-out channels round them get wider too.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_scale:
Multiplies radius, spacing, cover and ribs together (default 1).
Low (0.5): a fine, shallow mesh.
High (2): a coarse, deep grid; few bars fall inside one patch.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_spacin:
Distance between the vertical bars, measured along X (default 10 cm).
Low (5 cm): vertical bars close together.
High (25 cm): only one vertical bar crosses the patch.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.

Distance between the horizontal bars, measured along Y (default 12 cm).
Low (6 cm): many horizontal bars.
High (30 cm): a single horizontal bar.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_bars_x:
Local-space X component of rebar bars. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Off: omit rebar bars x while keeping its stored settings.
On: use rebar bars x with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_bars_y:
Local-space Y component of rebar bars. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Off: omit rebar bars y while keeping its stored settings.
On: use rebar bars y with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_outer:
Which family lies in front, nearer the surface: Horizontal (default) or Vertical.
Horizontal: the horizontal bars pass in front of the vertical ones.
Vertical: the vertical bars are in front.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_angle:
Rotation of the grid about the surface normal, in degrees (default 0). The patch frame turns with it, so the patch outline changes too.
Low (0°): horizontal and vertical bars.
High (45°): a diagonal grid.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_cover:
Concrete cover: the depth from the surface to the front of the outer bars (default 2 cm).
Low (0.5 cm): bars right under the surface; more of them show.
High (3.5 cm): bars deep in the core; only the deepest part of the patch reaches them.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_expose:
How far the core is dug out round the bars (0 to 1, default 0.7).
Low (0): the bars stay buried; only a trace shows.
High (1): the bars stand free in deep channels.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_embed:
How far the bars continue into the intact concrete past the cavity (default 4 cm). The hidden part is not visible from outside, so there is no image; it matters when the wall is cut open or the bars are used on their own.
Low (0): the bars end at the cavity wall.
High (12 cm): long bars under the surface.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_ribs:
Rib height, times the bar radius (default 0.15; 0 = a smooth bar).
Low (0): smooth round bars.
High (0.6): coarse, deep ribs.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_sides:
Segments round the bar (4 to 16, default 8).
Low (4): square-looking bars.
High (16): round bars, more polygons.
Allowed range: 4 to 16.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_jitter:
Random offset of each bar off the even grid (0 to 1 in use, default 0.3).
Low (0): a perfectly even grid.
High (1): irregular gaps between the bars.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_wobble:
Waviness along each bar, times its radius (default 0.2). It is small next to the patch size.
Low (0): straight bars.
High (1): slightly wavy bars.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_bend:
Outward bow of exposed bars and bend of broken ends (default 0.3). The images have Through Holes on (Hole Chance 1, Hole Size 0.7).
Low (0): the bars stay in their plane.
High (1.5): bars over the hole bow out toward the viewer.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_broken:
Chance that a bar crossing a hole is snapped (default 0.35). The images have Through Holes on.
Low (0): every bar spans the hole.
High (1): the bars are snapped at the hole and their ends bent.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_up_x:
X component of the local up direction used to orient courses or strips. Use a nonzero direction vector, usually (0, 0, 1).
Minimum: Point this direction component toward negative X.
Maximum: Point toward positive X. Only the vector direction matters; avoid a zero vector.
Allowed range: -100 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_up_y:
Y component of the local up direction used to orient courses or strips. Together with X and Z defines the orientation.
Minimum: Point this direction component toward negative Y.
Maximum: Point toward positive Y. Only the vector direction matters; avoid a zero vector.
Allowed range: -100 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_up_z:
Z component of the local up direction used to orient courses or strips. 1 with X/Y at 0 uses local Z-up.
Minimum: Point this direction component toward negative Z.
Maximum: Point toward positive Z. Only the vector direction matters; avoid a zero vector.
Allowed range: -100 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_group:
Optional weight-painted region; empty means the whole cloth.
Empty: no vertex-group restriction.
Assigned: use the named group weights on this object.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve that shows where the concrete breaks out. Draw close to the surface.
Empty: patches are placed automatically.
Assigned: patches follow your strokes.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_mode:
Choose Rust Mode. Paint Contours: Rust inside closed Grease Pencil contours; Procedural: Uniform rust or edge/bottom biases.
Paint Contours: Rust inside closed Grease Pencil contours.
Procedural: Uniform rust or edge/bottom biases.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve that shows where the rust starts. Draw close to the surface.
Empty: rust is placed automatically.
Assigned: rust grows from your strokes.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve that shows where the paint peels. Draw close to the surface.
Empty: peeling is placed automatically.
Assigned: paint peels along your strokes.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_materials:
Blend rust into copies of result materials; original materials remain unchanged.
Off: omit rust shader while keeping its stored settings.
On: use rust shader with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_enable:
Corrode the metal (crust, pits, perforation) and its paint (front, crazing, blisters, flakes).
Off: omit rust while keeping its stored settings.
On: use rust with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_mask_source:
Choose Mask. Vertex Paint: Paint the rust into a Color Attribute (Vertex Paint mode); Vertex Group: Use a weight-painted vertex group; None: No mask: uniform Intensity, or only the Edge/Bottom tendencies.
Vertex Paint: Paint the rust into a Color Attribute (Vertex Paint mode).
Vertex Group: Use a weight-painted vertex group.
None: No mask: uniform Intensity, or only the Edge/Bottom tendencies.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_color_attr:
Name of the colour layer that the rust is painted into.
Empty: the active colour layer of the object is used.
Assigned: rust is painted into the layer with this name.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_color_channel:
Choose Channel. Luminance; Red; Green; Blue; Alpha.
Luminance: select this channel variant.
Red: select this channel variant.
Green: select this channel variant.
Blue: select this channel variant.
Alpha: select this channel variant.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_mask_invert:
Enable Invert for this object.
Off: omit invert while keeping its stored settings.
On: use invert with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_group:
Choose Vertex Group.
Empty: no vertex-group restriction.
Assigned: use the named group weights on this object.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_seed:
Shuffles where rust appears and how it looks, without changing its amount.
Every number gives a different random arrangement.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_intensity:
Overall amount of rust on the object. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0%: clean metal, no rust.
High (150%): rust takes over almost the whole surface.
Allowed range: 0% to 150%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_edge_bias:
How strongly rust gathers along edges and creases. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0%: edges rust no more than flat areas.
High (150%): edges and creases rust first and hardest.
Allowed range: 0% to 150%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_bottom_bias:
How strongly rust gathers at the bottom, where water collects. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0%: top and bottom rust the same.
High (150%): sills and lower rims are heavily rusted.
Allowed range: 0% to 150%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_world_gravity:
Gravity is the world -Z (follows the object's rotation).
Off: omit world down while keeping its stored settings.
On: use world down with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_gravity:
The direction that counts as down for this object when World Down is off. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Each number is one axis of the direction.
Only the direction matters, not the length.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_noise:
How ragged the border between rust and clean paint is. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0%: a smooth, even border.
100%: a torn, blotchy border.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_noise_scale:
Size of the blotches along the rust border, in cm.
Low: fine, speckled border.
High: big rounded tongues of rust.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_detail:
Sampling resolution for this effect. Higher values resolve smaller features but increase mesh density and processing cost; start low for previews.
Minimum: Coarser, faster geometry with less small detail.
Maximum: Finer, heavier geometry; the active geometry budget may limit the requested detail.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_crust_start:
How much rust an area needs before thick scaly crust forms. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: crust appears almost everywhere there is rust.
High (150%): crust only in the very worst spots.
Allowed range: 0% to 150%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_crust_height:
How deep the scaly crust eats into the metal, in cm.
0: rust is only a colour, the surface stays flat.
High: deep, layered scale.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_crust_rough:
How rough the crust surface is.
0%: smooth, even crust.
100%: lumpy, crumbling crust.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_pits:
Number of small rust pits. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0: no pits.
High (5000): the surface is peppered with pits.
Allowed range: 0 to 5000.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_pit_start:
How much rust an area needs before pits appear. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: pits appear even in light rust.
High (150%): pits only in the heaviest rust.
Allowed range: 0% to 150%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_pit_size:
Size of one rust pit, in cm.
Low: pin-point pits.
High: wide craters.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_pit_depth:
Depth of the rust pits, in cm.
0: flat spots without depth.
High: deep pits; watch thin sheet metal.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_hole_start:
How much rust an area needs before the metal rusts right through. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: holes appear easily.
High (140% and more): the metal never rusts through.
Allowed range: 0% to 150%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_hole_depth:
Thickest metal that can still rust through, in cm. Thicker metal only gets a pit this deep.
Low: only very thin sheet gets holes.
High: even thick walls are eaten through.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_flakes:
Thin sheets of rust lifting around the holes. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0%: clean hole rims.
100%: every hole is ringed by lifted rust sheets.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_flake_size:
Size of one lifted rust sheet, in cm.
Low: small crumbs.
High: big peeling plates.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_paint:
Rust drives the paint (the coating object, Coating Thickness).
Off: omit paint layer while keeping its stored settings.
On: use paint layer with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_paint_start:
How much rust an area needs before the paint is gone. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: paint is lost even over light rust.
High (150%): paint holds on until the rust is severe.
Allowed range: 0% to 150%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_band:
Width of the zone just ahead of the rust where the paint cracks and bubbles.
0%: paint is perfect right up to the rust.
100%: a wide belt of damaged paint around the rust.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_paint_flakes:
Loose paint flakes along the rust border. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0%: no flakes.
100%: the whole border is lined with lifted flakes.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_craze:
Fine network of cracks in the paint near the rust. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0%: no cracks.
100%: densely cracked paint.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_craze_cell:
Size of one cell in the paint crack network, in cm. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: a fine, dense mesh of cracks.
High: big plates between the cracks.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_blisters:
Number of paint bubbles pushed up by rust underneath. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0: no bubbles.
High (3000): the paint is covered in bubbles.
Allowed range: 0 to 3000.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_blister_size:
Size of one paint bubble, in cm.
Low: tiny pimples.
High: big swollen bubbles.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_streak:
Rusty water streaks running down from the rust. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0%: no streaks.
100%: strong streaks under every rusty spot.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.rust_streak_length:
How far the rusty streaks run down, in cm.
0: no streaks.
High: long runs down the surface.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_enable:
Enable this feature for the current source. Disable to omit it without losing its stored settings.
Off: omit enable heat damage while keeping its stored settings.
On: use enable heat damage with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_seed:
Shuffles the burn pattern, cracks and bubbles without changing their amount.
Every number gives a different random arrangement.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: -2.14748e+09 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_intensity:
How hot the fire was. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0: no burn at all.
High: everything near the source is deeply charred.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_diffuse:
Enable Diffuse Heat for this object.
Off: omit diffuse heat while keeping its stored settings.
On: use diffuse heat with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_spread:
How far the heat travels from its source, in cm. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0: only the source spot is burnt.
High: the burn reaches far across the object.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_duration:
How long the fire burned. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: a quick scorch on the surface.
High: a long burn that chars deep and wide.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_steps:
How carefully the spreading of the heat is calculated. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low (1): quick, rough burn border.
High (64): smooth, natural border but slower.
Allowed range: 1 to 64.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_char_start:
How hot an area must get before it turns to char. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0%: everything touched by heat chars.
100%: only the very hottest core chars.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_shrink_depth:
How far the charred surface sinks in, in cm.
0: the charred surface keeps its shape.
High: burnt areas are clearly eaten away.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_detail:
Sampling resolution for this effect. Higher values resolve smaller features but increase mesh density and processing cost; start low for previews.
Minimum: Coarser, faster geometry with less small detail.
Maximum: Finer, heavier geometry; the active geometry budget may limit the requested detail.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_block_round:
How rounded the charred blocks are, like burnt wood. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0%: sharp-edged blocks.
100%: soft, pillow-like blocks.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_cell_min:
Smallest charred block, in cm. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: some blocks are tiny.
High: even the smallest block is big.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_cell_max:
Largest charred block, in cm. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: all blocks stay small.
High: some blocks are large.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_crack_cells:
Number of blocks the char tries to crack into. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0: no cracks between blocks.
High (5000): a dense alligator-skin pattern.
Allowed range: 0 to 5000.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_crack_width:
Width of the cracks between charred blocks, in cm.
0: no visible cracks.
High: wide open gaps.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_crack_depth:
Depth of the cracks between charred blocks, in cm.
0: no depth.
High: deep gaps; careful with thin walls.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_blisters:
Number of heat bubbles the surface tries to form. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0: no bubbles.
High (2000): a surface covered in bubbles.
Allowed range: 0 to 2000.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_blister_min:
Smallest heat bubble, in cm. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: some bubbles are tiny.
High: even the smallest bubble is big.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_blister_max:
Largest heat bubble, in cm. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: all bubbles stay small.
High: some bubbles are large.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_blister_low:
The mildest heat at which bubbles start to appear. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: bubbles appear even in barely warmed areas.
High: bubbles need strong heat.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_blister_high:
The heat above which bubbles no longer form because the surface is burnt away. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: bubbles only in a thin warm belt.
High: bubbles reach right into the hottest zone.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_blister_burst:
Share of heat bubbles that have popped open. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0%: all bubbles are whole.
100%: every bubble has burst into a small crater.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_char_layer:
Thickness of the charred layer, in cm. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0: char is only on the surface.
High: a thick black crust.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_group:
Empty heats the whole mesh; a named group supplies per-vertex exposure weights.
Empty: no vertex-group restriction.
Assigned: use the named group weights on this object.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_zone_enable:
Enable this feature for the current source. Disable to omit it without losing its stored settings.
Off: omit painted contour zone while keeping its stored settings.
On: use painted contour zone with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_zone_threshol:
How strong the painted weight must be for an area to count as peeling zone. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: even lightly painted areas peel.
High: only fully painted areas peel.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_zone_smooth:
Set Zone Smoothing (cm) for this generated feature.
Minimum: Retain sharper local changes.
Maximum: Round or average more local variation.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_zone_inset:
Pulls the border of the peeling zone inward, in cm. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0: the zone ends exactly where you painted it.
High: the zone shrinks away from its painted border.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_zone_detail:
Set Zone Detail (cm) for this generated feature.
Minimum: Coarser, faster geometry with less small detail.
Maximum: Finer, heavier geometry; the active geometry budget may limit the requested detail.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_flake_side:
Choose Flake Side. All: All island rims; Upper: Rims along the local side axis; Lower: Rims opposite the local side axis.
All: All island rims.
Upper: Rims along the local side axis.
Lower: Rims opposite the local side axis.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_flake_side_x:
Local-space X component of flake side. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Minimum: Lower the local X component.
Maximum: Raise the local X component.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_flake_side_y:
Local-space Y component of flake side. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Minimum: Lower the local Y component.
Maximum: Raise the local Y component.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_flake_side_z:
Local-space Z component of flake side. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Minimum: Lower the local Z component.
Maximum: Raise the local Z component.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_zone_group:
Choose Coating Vertex Group.
Empty: no vertex-group restriction.
Assigned: use the named group weights on this object.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_enable:
Enable this feature for the current source. Disable to omit it without losing its stored settings.
Off: omit coating peeling while keeping its stored settings.
On: use coating peeling with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_amount:
Number of peeled patches the paint tries to form.
0: the paint stays whole.
High (1000): the paint is peeled all over.
Allowed range: 0 to 1000.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_thickness:
Thickness of the paint layer, in cm.
Low: a thin film with barely visible edges.
High: a thick crust with clear steps at the edges.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_patch_min:
Smallest peeled patch, in cm. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: some patches are tiny chips.
High: even the smallest patch is big.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_patch_max:
Largest peeled patch, in cm. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: all patches stay small.
High: some patches are large.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_jagged:
How ragged the border of a peeled patch is.
0%: smooth rounded borders.
100%: torn, chipped borders.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_flakes:
How much of the paint around the patches lifts up as flakes. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0%: the paint lies flat right up to the border.
100%: lifted flakes all around every patch.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_curl:
How strongly the lifted flakes curl away from the surface.
0%: flakes stay flat.
100%: flakes curl up tightly.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.coating_cracks:
Cracks in the paint running out from the peeled patches. Older effect, kept for old projects.
0%: no cracks.
100%: many cracks around every patch.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_type:
Pattern the cracks follow in Procedural mode. The typed assets (Concrete, Wood, Glass, Radial) fix it for you
Fracture: a free wandering network that closes into plates
Radial, Glass, Wood: stars, glass stars with rings, or splits along the grain
ProjectDamageProps.fract_impacts:
Legacy compatibility value; no longer used by network styles.
Minimum: Compatibility value; not an artistic intensity control in the current asset.
Maximum: Compatibility value; not an artistic intensity control in the current asset.
Allowed range: 1 to 64.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_grain_x:
X part of the wood grain direction, in the object's local axes. Only the ratio of X, Y and Z matters. All three at 0 turns the grain off
0: the grain has no X component
1: fibres run along X, use it for a beam lying along X. Mixing two axes gives diagonal spilts
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_grain_y:
Y part of the wood grain direction, in the object's local axes. Only the ratio of X, Y and Z matters
0: the grain has no Y component
1: fibres run along Y. Negative values point the same axis the other way and give the same splits
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_grain_z:
Z part of the wood grain direction, in the object's local axes. The default (0, 0, 1) is for upright posts
0: the grain has no Z component
1: fibres run along Z, upright like a post or a log standing on its end
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_grain_pull:
How strongly the cracks follow the wood grain.
0: the grain is ignored, cracks wander like in concrete.
1: cracks run straight along the grain as long splits.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_recipe:
which version of the crack generator is used
Legacy: the original network, gives exactly the same result as older files
Improved: more stable randomness, depth follows width, depth is limited by wall thickness, fallen bits are removed
ProjectDamageProps.fract_thickness_cap:
Improved recipe only. The deepest a crack may go, as a share of the wall thickness under it, so thin walls are not cut thorugh
0%: no cap, cracks keep their full Depth even in thin parts
100%: cracks may go as deep as the whole wall. Lower values keep them shallower in thin areas
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_prox_mode: Chooses how the points are used. Off: points are ignored. Default: the normal crack network is pulled toward the points. Radial: a radial impact pattern at each point. Glass: a glass impact pattern at each point.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_prox_collection: The collection whose objects (Empties) are the proximity points. Add Proximity Point creates an Empty at the 3D Cursor and creates the collection if needed.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_prox_use_size:
Takes the reach of each point from its Empty: display size multiplied by scale.
Off: every point uses Distance. On: each point has its own reach, set by scaling the Empty in the viewport.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_prox_radius:
Reach of a point when Radius from Empty Size is off: how far from the point cracks gather.
Low: cracks packed tightly around the point. High: cracks spread over a large area around it.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_prox_strength:
Share of the cracks of each level that start near the points instead of anywhere on the object. It concentrates cracks, it does not cut them off at the reach.
Low (0%): points have no effect. High (100%): almost all cracks start around the points.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_radial_spokes:
Number of straight spokes per star. The network uses half of this value plus one, so 14 gives 8 spokes.
Low (3): a few long spokes. High: a dense star of many spokes.
Allowed range: 3 to 32.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_radial_rings:
Number of concentric rings around each star. The network uses half of this value.
Low (0): spokes only, no rings. High: many rings, a spider-web look.
Allowed range: 0 to 12.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_radial_ring_fil:
Share of the ring pieces between neighbouring spokes that are actually cracked.
Low: broken, scattered ring pieces. High (100%): complete rings.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_radial_crush:
Size of the crushed zone at the impact point, as a share of the reach.
Low (0%): the cracks meet in a clean point. High (40%): a crushed hole area in the middle.
Allowed range: 0% to 60%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_glass_spokes:
Number of straight spokes per star. The network uses half of this value plus one, so 14 gives 8 spokes.
Low (3): a few long spokes. High: a dense star of many spokes.
Allowed range: 3 to 48.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_glass_rings:
Number of concentric rings around each star. The network uses half of this value.
Low (0): spokes only, no rings. High: many rings, a spider-web look.
Allowed range: 0 to 24.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_glass_branch:
Chance that each radial crack forks (up to two times) as it runs out.
Low (0%): straight, single cracks. High (100%): every crack forks, a tree-like pattern.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_glass_ring_fill:
Share of the ring pieces between neighbouring spokes that are actually cracked.
Low: broken, scattered ring pieces. High (100%): complete rings.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_glass_width:
Width of the crack lines at the surface, in cm.
Low: fine hairlines. High: wide, clearly visible cracks.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_glass_depth:
Depth of the crack lines, in cm. Keep it below the glass thickness.
Low: surface scratches. High: cracks that go deep into the pane.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_glass_crush:
Size of the crushed zone at the impact point, as a share of the reach.
Low (0%): the cracks meet in a clean point. High (40%): a crushed hole area in the middle.
Allowed range: 0% to 40%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_through_enable:
Alternative fracture asset sharing the Fracture settings; cuts cracks through the wall.
Off: omit fracture through while keeping its stored settings.
On: use fracture through with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_physics:
Close crack islands and detach shallow chunks while retaining the main body; geometry only, no Blender physics.
Off: omit non-through chunks (wip) while keeping its stored settings.
On: use non-through chunks (wip) with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_physics_depth:
How deep the loose chunks go into the object, in cm.
0: the depth is taken from the Level 1 crack depth.
High: thick chunks that reach deep into the object.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_physics_close:
How hard the addon tries to join open cracks into closed pieces.
0: only cracks that already meet make pieces.
High (32): many more pieces, slower to build.
Allowed range: 0 to 32.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_helper_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve with extra lines that close open cracks into pieces. Draw close to the surface.
Empty: no helper lines are used.
Assigned: your lines are added as extra cuts.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_helper_snap:
How far the end of a helper line may jump to reach a nearby crack or edge, in cm.
0: the distance is chosen automatically.
High: ends snap to cracks even far away.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_through:
Split the solid beneath closed crack regions into separate mesh islands; disable for ordinary shallow grooves.
Off: omit pass through while keeping its stored settings.
On: use pass through with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_through_min_pie:
Throws away pieces that are too small, as a share of the whole object.
0%: every tiny piece is kept.
High (10%): only big pieces survive.
Allowed range: 0% to 10%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_volume_size:
Size of the pieces deep inside the object, in cm.
0: the size is guessed from the pieces on the surface.
Low: many small inner pieces, slow. High: a few big inner pieces.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_volume_rough:
How rough the hidden faces between inner pieces are.
0%: flat, clean break faces.
100%: lumpy, natural break faces.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_enable:
Turns the Fracture effect on for this obejct. Only one Fracture asset can be active, they all share the same settings
Off: no cracks are made
on: cracks are cut into the surface with the settings below
ProjectDamageProps.fract_scale:
Multiplies the width, depth, length and chip size of all cracks at once, keeping their proportions. Handy when the pattern already looks right and you just need everything bigger or smaller.
Low (10%): thin, shallow hairline cracks. High (400%): wide, deep, heavily broken cracks.
Allowed range: 10% to 400%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_detail:
Polygon density along each crack. Changes how smooth and finely broken the crack edges are and how fast the effect updates, not the size of the cracks.
Low (25%): few polygons, straight faceted crack edges, fast updates. High (400%): finely broken, rough edges, heavy mesh and slow updates. Keep it low while tuning and raise it at the end.
Allowed range: 25% to 400%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l1_amount:
Number of main cracks on the whole object.
0: this level is off.
High: a dense network of main cracks.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l1_subdiv:
Extra passes after the cracks of this level are finished. Each pass adds new cracks in the large uncracked areas between them, filling the gaps evenly.
Low (0): only the Amount cracks. High (4): four extra passes, a much denser and more even network.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l1_width:
Width of the main cracks at the surface, in cm.
Low: hairline cracks.
High: wide open cracks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l1_depth:
Depth of the main cracks, in cm.
Low: shallow surface cracks.
High: deep cracks into the object.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l1_length:
The longest a main crack can grow, in cm.
Low: short cracks.
High: cracks that run across the whole object.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_length:
The longest a second-level crack can grow, in cm.
Low: short side cracks.
High: long side cracks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_length:
The longest a finest-level crack can grow, in cm.
Low: tiny hairlines.
High: long fine cracks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l1_branches:
Average number of side branches that grow from each crack of this level. Fractions work: 0.5 means roughly every other crack gets one branch.
Low (0): no branches, the original pattern. High: every crack forks several times, a tree-like network.
Allowed range: 0 to 16.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_branches:
Average number of side branches that grow from each crack of this level. Fractions work: 0.5 means roughly every other crack gets one branch.
Low (0): no branches, the original pattern. High: every crack forks several times, a tree-like network.
Allowed range: 0 to 16.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_branches:
Average number of side branches that grow from each crack of this level. Fractions work: 0.5 means roughly every other crack gets one branch.
Low (0): no branches, the original pattern. High: every crack forks several times, a tree-like network.
Allowed range: 0 to 16.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l1_branch_lengt:
Length of a branch compared with the crack it grows from (1 = as long as the parent). Visible only when Branches is above 0. Also limited by Fracture Length when that is set.
Low: short stubs off the main crack. High: long branches that run as far as the parent.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_branch_lengt:
Length of a branch compared with the crack it grows from (1 = as long as the parent). Visible only when Branches is above 0. Also limited by Fracture Length when that is set.
Low: short stubs off the main crack. High: long branches that run as far as the parent.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_branch_lengt:
Length of a branch compared with the crack it grows from (1 = as long as the parent). Visible only when Branches is above 0. Also limited by Fracture Length when that is set.
Low: short stubs off the main crack. High: long branches that run as far as the parent.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l1_bias:
How many cracks start near corners instead of at random places. For Level 1 these are the corners of the object; for Level 2 and 3 they are the junctions and ends of the previous level's cracks.
Low (0%): cracks start anywhere along the edges. High (100%): cracks start from corners and junctions, like real stress cracks.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l1_chips:
Turns on chips (small spalls broken out of the rim) along the cracks of this level.
Off: clean grooves. On: chips along the rims, set by the three fields below.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l1_chip_amount:
How many chips are made per 100 cm of crack length.
Low (0): no chips. High (20): the rim is chipped almost all along the crack.
Allowed range: 0 to 20.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l1_chip_size:
Size of the chips broken off along the main cracks, in cm.
Low: small nicks.
High: big chunks missing along the crack.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l1_chip_depth:
How deep the chips along the main cracks go, in cm.
Low: shallow flakes.
High: deep bites.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_amount:
Number of second-level cracks on the whole object.
0: this level is off.
High: a dense network of side cracks.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_subdiv:
Extra passes after the cracks of this level are finished. Each pass adds new cracks in the large uncracked areas between them, filling the gaps evenly.
Low (0): only the Amount cracks. High (4): four extra passes, a much denser and more even network.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_width:
Width of the second-level cracks at the surface, in cm.
Low: hairline cracks.
High: wide open cracks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_depth:
Depth of the second-level cracks, in cm.
Low: shallow surface cracks.
High: deep cracks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_bias:
How many cracks start near corners instead of at random places. For Level 1 these are the corners of the object; for Level 2 and 3 they are the junctions and ends of the previous level's cracks.
Low (0%): cracks start anywhere along the edges. High (100%): cracks start from corners and junctions, like real stress cracks.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_chips:
Turns on chips (small spalls broken out of the rim) along the cracks of this level.
Off: clean grooves. On: chips along the rims, set by the three fields below.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_chip_amount:
How many chips are made per 100 cm of crack length.
Low (0): no chips. High (20): the rim is chipped almost all along the crack.
Allowed range: 0 to 20.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_chip_size:
Size of the chips broken off along the second-level cracks, in cm.
Low: small nicks.
High: big chunks missing along the crack.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_chip_depth:
How deep the chips along the second-level cracks go, in cm.
Low: shallow flakes.
High: deep bites.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_amount:
Number of finest cracks on the whole object.
0: this level is off.
High: a dense web of fine cracks.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_subdiv:
Extra passes after the cracks of this level are finished. Each pass adds new cracks in the large uncracked areas between them, filling the gaps evenly.
Low (0): only the Amount cracks. High (4): four extra passes, a much denser and more even network.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_width:
Width of the finest cracks at the surface, in cm.
Low: hairline cracks.
High: clearly visible cracks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_depth:
Depth of the finest cracks, in cm.
Low: shallow surface cracks.
High: deep cracks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_bias:
How many cracks start near corners instead of at random places. For Level 1 these are the corners of the object; for Level 2 and 3 they are the junctions and ends of the previous level's cracks.
Low (0%): cracks start anywhere along the edges. High (100%): cracks start from corners and junctions, like real stress cracks.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_chips:
Turns on chips (small spalls broken out of the rim) along the cracks of this level.
Off: clean grooves. On: chips along the rims, set by the three fields below.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_chip_amount:
How many chips are made per 100 cm of crack length.
Low (0): no chips. High (20): the rim is chipped almost all along the crack.
Allowed range: 0 to 20.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_chip_size:
Size of the chips broken off along the finest cracks, in cm.
Low: small nicks.
High: bigger bites along the crack.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_chip_depth:
How deep the chips along the finest cracks go, in cm.
Low: shallow flakes.
High: deep bites.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_disp_strength:
How strongly the crack line wanders and how much micro relief its walls get.
Low (0%): smooth, clean crack lines. High (300%): very jagged, rough crack lines.
Allowed range: 0% to 300%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_disp_scale:
Multiplies the width, depth, length and chip size of all cracks at once, keeping their proportions. Handy when the pattern already looks right and you just need everything bigger or smaller.
Low (10%): thin, shallow hairline cracks. High (400%): wide, deep, heavily broken cracks.
Allowed range: 25% to 400%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_tile_offset:
Raises or sinks the pieces (tiles) enclosed by cracks, like a cracked slab that has setled. Measured as a share of the crack depth around each tile, so a tile never sinks below its own crack. Shows best with Level 2 and 3
0%: all tiles stay flush with the surface
100%: tiles shift up and down by up to the full crack depth
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_tile_seed:
Reshuffles which tiles go up and which go down, without moving any crack. Chnage it when the offset pattern looks unlucky
Any number: one arrangement of raised and sunk tiles
another number: a different arrangement, there is no low or high, only variants
Allowed range: 0 to 999999.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_rim_jag:
Makes the two lips of a crack break unevenly, so one side is wider than the other and the width changes along the crack
0%: both lips are even, a clean groove
100%: strongly uneven, ragged lips
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_flare:
crumbles the opening of the crack: a wide broken lip at the surface over a narrow, deep slit
0%: straight walls, the crack is as wide at the top as at the bottom
100%: a wide crumbled mouth narrowing into a thin slit
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_shard_enable:
Move the broken pieces near the points in or out along their normal.
Off: omit shard displace while keeping its stored settings.
On: use shard displace with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_shard_collectio: The collection whose objects (Empties) are the proximity points. Add Proximity Point creates an Empty at the 3D Cursor and creates the collection if needed.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_shard_dir:
Choose Direction. Push In: Pieces sink into the surface; Lift Out: Pieces lift off the surface; Mixed: Each piece goes in or out at random.
Push In: Pieces sink into the surface.
Lift Out: Pieces lift off the surface.
Mixed: Each piece goes in or out at random.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_shard_amount:
How far the pieces are pushed away from a point, in cm.
0: pieces stay in place.
High: pieces are thrown far apart.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_shard_use_size:
Takes the reach of each point from its Empty: display size multiplied by scale.
Off: every point uses Distance. On: each point has its own reach, set by scaling the Empty in the viewport.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_shard_radius:
How far the push from a point reaches, in cm.
Low: only pieces right at the point move.
High: pieces far from the point move too.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_shard_falloff:
How quickly the push fades with distance from the point.
Low: almost every piece inside the radius moves equally.
High (6): only pieces right next to the point move.
Allowed range: 0.1 to 6.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_shard_tilt:
The side of a piece nearer the point moves more, so pieces tilt.
Minimum: Rotate or tilt toward the lower end of the permitted angle range.
Maximum: Rotate or tilt toward the upper end; angles are not a damage-strength multiplier.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_shard_random:
How much the push differs from piece to piece.
0%: neighbours move the same distance.
100%: every piece moves a different distance.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_shard_seed:
Shuffles the random differences between pieces.
Every number gives a different random arrangement.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 999999.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_depth_mult:
Scales the depth of the cracks of all three levels together, without changing their width. Use it to make the whole network shallower or deeper in one move.
Low (10%): shallow surface cracks. High (400%): deep grooves that cut far into the object.
Allowed range: 10% to 400%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_rim_soft:
Rounds the rim of the chips along the cracks outward into a soft fillet, like worn or weathered damage.
Low (0%): sharp, fresh chip rims. High (100%): rounded, smoothed rims. The difference is subtle and shows in close-up.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_enable:
Enables cuts at qualifying convex corner vertices.
Off: Off leaves corners intact.
On: On evaluates candidates and Probability.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_scale:
Multiplies corner footprint and depth dimensions together with Master Scale.
Minimum: 10% gives small corner losses.
Maximum: 400% enlarges the base dimensions fourfold before Master Scale.
Allowed range: 10% to 400%.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_detail:
Sampling detail of the corner cutters, combined with Master Quality.
Minimum: 25% uses coarse cutter facets.
Maximum: 400% resolves finer roughness at greater cost.
Allowed range: 25% to 400%.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_prob:
Independent chance of accepting each qualifying corner. It is not a target percentage of the object's area.
Minimum: 0% accepts none.
Maximum: 100% accepts every candidate that survives geometry and drawing checks.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_min_edges:
Minimum number of exposed convex edges meeting at a vertex. A concave incident edge disqualifies the vertex.
Minimum: 3 admits ordinary box corners.
Maximum: 8 requires unusually high-valence convex junctions; many meshes then have no candidates.
Allowed range: 3 to 8.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_size_min:
Lower bound of the corner footprint before scaling.
Minimum: Near zero admits small corner chips.
Maximum: A higher minimum removes more of every accepted corner.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_size_max:
Upper bound of the corner footprint before scaling.
Minimum: Small values constrain missing corner size.
Maximum: Larger values permit damage to spread farther onto adjacent faces.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_depth_min:
Lower bound of depth into the corner, measured along the cutter's outward-direction frame.
Minimum: Near zero admits shallow corner marks.
Maximum: Higher values make even small accepted cuts deeper.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_depth_max:
Upper bound of corner cut depth, before scaling.
Minimum: A small value keeps corner loss shallow.
Maximum: A large value permits deep missing chunks; keep the minimum no greater than this maximum.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_rim_soft:
Shoulder softness of Round Crater cutters and their secondary cuts.
Minimum: 0% keeps a sharper transition.
Maximum: 100% softens the bowl shoulder; it is not the Broken Corner roughness control.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_sec_amount:
Extra cuts on corner-damage rims after the primary Boolean pass.
Minimum: Zero disables secondary rim damage.
Maximum: More cuts roughen the primary corner boundary.
Allowed range: 0 to 50000.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_sec_size:
Secondary footprint relative to the primary corner size range.
Minimum: 1% makes tiny rim chips.
Maximum: 100% uses the primary footprint range.
Allowed range: 1% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_sec_depth:
Secondary cut depth relative to the primary corner depth range.
Minimum: 1% makes shallow rim marks.
Maximum: 100% uses the primary depth range.
Allowed range: 1% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_style:
Round Crater uses a bowl cutter. Broken Corner uses a tilted, rough fracture-face cutter.
Low / first state: Round Crater gives a rounded bite.
High / other state: Broken Corner gives a knocked-off face and enables Roughness, Tilt and Flakes.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_rough:
Amplitude of irregularity on a Broken Corner cutter's fracture face.
Minimum: 0% gives the simplest fracture plane.
Maximum: 100% produces the roughest supported broken face.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_tilt:
Random tilt of the fracture face around its base corner direction.
Minimum: 0% keeps the base orientation.
Maximum: 100% allows the strongest random slant.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_flakes:
Adds satellite cutters around the primary broken corner, using a separate shape random stream.
Minimum: 0% adds no satellite flakes.
Maximum: 100% adds the largest supported satellite population; these are cuts, not separate flake objects.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_mode:
Automatic evaluates all qualifying corners; Draw limits them by distance to the linked strokes.
Low / first state: Automatic has no drawing restriction.
High / other state: Draw requires a corner within Paint Radius; it cannot turn a flat-face point into a corner.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_drawing:
Linked Grease Pencil or supported curve paths, read at the current frame and transformed into source-local space. Use New Drawing to create an input, Draw / Edit to paint, and the trash button to remove it.
Low / first state: Empty supplies no drawing constraint or no drawn damage, according to the placement mode.
High / other state: Assigned visible strokes guide placement; geometry outside their eligible region is not made eligible merely by drawing there.
ProjectDamageProps.corner_paint_radius:
Distance within which a drawn stroke permits an existing convex corner candidate.
Minimum: A small radius needs strokes close to each corner.
Maximum: A large radius can admit multiple nearby corners, without increasing their cut size.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.guide_index:
Set guide_index for this generated feature.
Minimum: First entry or lowest enabled-axis bit pattern.
Maximum: Later entry or combined enabled-axis bits; this is a selector, not an intensity.
Allowed range: -2.14748e+09 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.breaker_index:
Set breaker_index for this generated feature.
Minimum: First entry or lowest enabled-axis bit pattern.
Maximum: Later entry or combined enabled-axis bits; this is a selector, not an intensity.
Allowed range: -2.14748e+09 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.break_scale:
Multiplies the surface noise Strength of every breaker (10 to 400 %, default 100 %). It does not change the size of the cut.
Low (50 %): a smoother break face.
High (200 %): a deeply broken face and a ragged rim.
Allowed range: 10% to 400%.
ProjectDamageProps.break_surf_dmg:
Adds Surface Damage craters on the break faces as well (off by default). The change is small on this break.
Off: only the chips on the rims.
On: a few craters on the break face too.
ProjectDamageProps.break_rim_enable:
Turns the rim chips on.
Off: clean rims.
On: chips bitten out along the rims.
ProjectDamageProps.break_rim_amount:
Edge Breakup fold, Plane and Strip only: how strongly the outline of the breaker is broken up (0 to 50 %, default 13 %).
Low (0 %): the ends of the cut are straight and clean.
High (40 %): the ends of the cut are torn and rounded.
Allowed range: 0 to 50000.
ProjectDamageProps.break_rim_size:
Chip size as a share of the Edge Damage size range (default 100 %).
Low (50 %): small nicks.
High (250 %): large chunks.
Allowed range: 1% to 400%.
ProjectDamageProps.break_rim_depth:
Chip depth as a share of the Edge Damage depth range (default 100 %).
Low (40 %): shallow chips.
High (250 %): deep chips.
Allowed range: 1% to 400%.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_enable:
Turns Bullet Impacts on: shot holes whose shape depends on the Material Type. Thin objects are shot through and get an exit wound
Off: no shots
On: holes with the settings below
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_seed:
Changes where the shots land without changing their number or size.
Every number gives a different arrangement.
There is no low or high, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_mode:
How the shots are placed
Automatic: shots and bursts spread over the object by the Distribute settings
Paint: shots follow your strokes, a tiny stroke or a dot gives a single shot
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_material:
The material the shots hit. It decides the shape of the wound and which settings box is shown at the bottom of the panel.
Metal: a clean hole with a torn crown. Wood: a crushed hole with splinters along the grain.
Concrete / Stone: a wide spall crater with a bore hole in the middle.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_avoid:
Keeps bullet marks away from the faces you marked as Avoid.
Off: bullets may hit protected faces too.
On: protected faces stay untouched.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_detail:
Polygon density of the holes and craters.
Low: faceted holes and craters, fast updates.
High: round holes and finely broken craters, heavy mesh.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_size_min:
Smallest hole, in cm. Keep it at or below Size Max
Low: small calibre holes are possible
High: every hole is large
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_size_max:
Largest hole, in cm. Keep it at or above Size Min
low: only small holes
High: large holes and craters are possible
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_size_bias:
Share of small holes within the size range (images use 0.3-2 cm).
Low (0): mostly large holes.
High (1): mostly small holes; 0.5 is an even spread.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_penetration:
A wall up to this thick is shot through. The images show the back of a 3 cm wall.
Low: shots stop in the wall, no exit wound.
High: shots go through and blow out an exit wound on the back.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_penetration_va:
Random variation of the penetration from shot to shot.
Low (0): every shot penetrates the same.
High (1): some shots go through and others stop.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_thickness_cap:
The deepest a shot that does not go through may cut, as a share of the local thickness. Protects thin walls from almost-holes.
Low: shallow craters on thin walls.
High: craters may cut almost through.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_shot_mode:
Random Slant gives every shot its own slanted direction. Fixed Direction fires all shots from Shot X / Y / Z.
Random Slant: holes elongated in many directions.
Fixed Direction: all holes elongated the same way, like fire from one position.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_oblique:
How slanted the random shots are (1 = up to about 70°).
Low (0): all shots hit straight on, round holes.
High (1): steep shots with long, stretched craters.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_shot_x:
X component of the direction the shots travel (Fixed Direction). Straight into the face gives round holes, slanted gives stretched holes, in object space. Set X, Y and Z together, they form one direction. Default (0, 1, 0)
0: no part of the direction along X
1: the direction points along X (mixed values give a diagonal)
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_shot_y:
Y component of the direction the shots travel (Fixed Direction). Straight into the face gives round holes, slanted gives stretched holes, in object space. Set X, Y and Z together, they form one direction. Default (0, 1, 0)
0: no part of the direction along Y
1: the direction points along Y (mixed values give a diagonal)
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_shot_z:
Z component of the direction the shots travel (Fixed Direction). Straight into the face gives round holes, slanted gives stretched holes, in object space. Set X, Y and Z together, they form one direction. Default (0, 1, 0)
0: no part of the direction along Z
1: the direction points along Z (mixed values give a diagonal)
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_elongate:
How much a slanted shot stretches its hole and crater (images use a fixed 45° shot).
Low (0): round holes even for slanted shots.
High: strongly stretched, teardrop holes.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_amount:
Number of shots on the whole object. Placement can give fewer where there is no room.
Low: a few hits.
High: a heavily shot-up surface.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_clusters:
Number of bursts the clustered shots are grouped into.
Low (0): no bursts, every shot is placed on its own.
High: many small bursts.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_cluster_share:
Share of the shots that belong to a burst.
Low (0): all shots scattered evenly.
High (1): all shots in bursts.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_cluster_spread:
Radius of a burst.
Low: tight groups of holes.
High: loose, wide groups.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_min_spacing:
Closest distance between two hole centres, x the sum of their radii.
Low (below 1): holes may overlap and merge.
High: holes keep a clear distance from each other.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_paint_spacing:
Distance between shots along a stroke.
Low: a dense line of shots, holes merge.
High: a sparse line of separate shots.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_paint_spread:
How far shots scatter sideways from the stroke.
Low (0): shots exactly on the stroke.
High: a wide band of shots around the stroke.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_paint_snap:
How far a stroke can be from the surface and still be projected onto it.
Low: only strokes drawn right on the surface are used.
High: strokes away from the surface are used too.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_paint_close:
Treats a nearly closed stroke as a filled area rather than a line.
Low: only exactly closed loops are filled.
High: loosely closed loops are filled with shots too.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_paint_single:
Strokes shorter than this become one single shot.
Low: even short strokes give a line of shots.
High: longer strokes still count as one shot.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_halo_enable:
Adds a very shallow ring of damaged surface around each hole
Off: the surface is untouched around the wound
on: a shallow damaged ring around every hole
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_halo_scale:
Radius of the halo, x size.
Low: a ring tight around the hole.
High: a wide ring.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_halo_depth:
Depth of the halo.
Low: only a trace on the surface, mostly for materials.
High: a visible shallow dish around the hole.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_halo_jagged:
Irregularity of the halo outline.
Low (0): a round halo.
High: a ragged halo.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_pit_amount:
Number of small pits per impact.
Low (0): no pits.
High: many pits around every hole.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_pit_size:
Size of a pit, x size.
Low: tiny dots.
High: large pits.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_pit_spread:
How far the pits scatter from the hole, x size.
Low: pits close to the hole.
High: pits spread far around it.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_metal_hole_jag:
Raggedness of the hole outline.
Low (0): a clean round hole.
High: a torn, ragged hole.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
