ProjectDamageProps.debris_enable:
Turns the removed material into separate loose chunks you can drop or scatter.
Off: removed material simply disappears.
On: every removed piece becomes its own object.
ProjectDamageProps.debris_seed:
Seed shared by the roughness field on neighbouring pieces.
Minimum: 0 is the first repeatable field.
Maximum: Other values give a different matching field; do not use different seeds for opposite sides of one boundary.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.debris_min_volume:
Throws away chunks smaller than this volume, in cubic cm.
0: even the tiniest crumbs are kept.
High: only big chunks are kept.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.debris_min_thickness:
Throws away paper-thin chunks, such as the slivers cut out by cracks.
0: thin films and dust are kept.
High: only solid, chunky pieces are kept.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.debris_chunk_size:
Breaks big removed pieces into chunks of about this size.
0: pieces are kept whole as they were removed.
Low: many small chunks. High: a few big chunks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.debris_chunk_jitter:
How irregular the breaks between chunks are.
0: straight, even splits.
1: crooked, random splits.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.debris_max_pieces:
The most chunks that may be created. The biggest ones are kept. Older effect, kept for old projects.
Low: only a handful of big chunks, light scene.
High (100000): every chunk is kept, can be very heavy.
Allowed range: 1 to 100000.
ProjectDamageProps.debris_inner_uv_scale:
World-length scale for UVs on generated inner faces, in centimetres.
Minimum: 0.001 produces many texture repeats over a face.
Maximum: 10000 gives very large texture features and fewer repeats; it does not change geometry.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.debris_smooth_angle:
Angle threshold used for shading piece surfaces. It changes normals, not the partition itself.
Minimum: 0 degrees preserves sharp boundaries between differing face normals.
Maximum: 180 degrees permits smoothing across the widest range of angles.
Allowed range: 0 to 180.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_enable:
Breaks the whole object into separate pieces ready for a physics simulation.
Off: the object stays in one piece.
On: the object is split into loose pieces.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_seed:
Seed shared by the roughness field on neighbouring pieces.
Minimum: 0 is the first repeatable field.
Maximum: Other values give a different matching field; do not use different seeds for opposite sides of one boundary.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_material:
Concrete chunks, Wood splinters, Fabric patches, Glass shards or Soil clods.
Concrete: Concrete.
Wood: Wood.
Fabric: Fabric.
Glass: Glass.
Soil: Soil.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_pieces:
Requested final number of closed pieces. The current wrapper merges excess pieces, then repeatedly splits large pieces to reach the requested count where valid solid cuts are possible.
Minimum: 1 keeps one piece.
Maximum: 2000 requests many smaller pieces and can be expensive; invalid solids or failed splits can prevent an exact count.
Allowed range: 1 to 1500.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_max_pieces:
The most pieces the object is broken into.
Low: a few big pieces.
High (10000): very many small pieces, slow.
Allowed range: 1 to 10000.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_gap:
Separates adjacent cell boundaries by removing material at the cut, rather than translating finished pieces.
Minimum: 0 keeps matching pieces tiled together.
Maximum: Large gaps remove more material and can erase small pieces.
Allowed range: 0 to 1000.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_size_variation:
Controls irregularity in cell size; -1 is a material-specific automatic value, not a negative variation.
Minimum: -1 uses the selected type's default; 0 gives the most even sizes.
Maximum: 1 gives strong size variation while retaining the requested final piece-count target.
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_min_piece:
Throws away pieces that are too small, as a share of the whole object.
0: every crumb is kept.
High (0.5): only huge pieces survive.
Allowed range: 0 to 0.5.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_cut_spacing:
Distance between break points along a cut you drew, in cm.
0: chosen automatically.
Low: the cut follows your line closely with many small pieces. High: a rough cut with big pieces.
Allowed range: 0 to 10000.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_impact_radius:
How far an impact point shatters the object when it has no size of its own, in cm.
Low: a small shattered spot.
High: a wide shattered zone.
Allowed range: 0.001 to 10000.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_impact_density:
How much finer the pieces are near an impact.
Low (1): the same piece size everywhere.
High (100): a cloud of tiny pieces at the impact.
Allowed range: 1 to 100.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_rubble:
Amount of small pieces near impact sources; -1 uses the material default.
Minimum: -1 is automatic; 0 adds no rubble population.
Maximum: 1 adds the strongest local rubble population before final count reconciliation.
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_grain_x:
X component of the local grain axis, normalised with Y and Z.
Minimum: -1 points the X contribution toward negative X.
Maximum: 1 points it toward positive X; the axis controls shape direction, not cell size by itself.
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_grain_y:
Y component of the normalised local grain axis.
Minimum: -1 points toward negative Y.
Maximum: 1 points toward positive Y; combine the three components to choose the grain axis.
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_grain_z:
Z component of the normalised local grain axis.
Minimum: -1 points toward negative Z.
Maximum: 1 points toward positive Z; Wood's stretching and splinter relief use this axis.
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_grain_stretch:
Anisotropic cell stretch along the grain; the partition is built in compressed coordinates and transformed back.
Minimum: 1 gives isotropic cells.
Maximum: 100 permits very long, thin grain-aligned pieces.
Allowed range: 1 to 100.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_weave_stretch:
How stretched the pieces are along the threads of a fabric.
Low (1): roundish pieces.
High (100): long strips along the threads.
Allowed range: 1 to 100.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_glass_spokes:
Number of primary radial directions in a planar glass impact network.
Minimum: 3 creates a few broad radial sectors.
Maximum: 64 creates many narrow radial sectors, subject to piece-count reconciliation.
Allowed range: 3 to 256.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_glass_ring_growth:
Multiplicative growth of successive ring distances from an impact.
Minimum: 1.15 keeps successive rings close together.
Maximum: 10 rapidly increases spacing between outer rings.
Allowed range: 1.01 to 10.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_inner_uv_scale:
World-length scale for UVs on generated inner faces, in centimetres.
Minimum: 0.001 produces many texture repeats over a face.
Maximum: 10000 gives very large texture features and fewer repeats; it does not change geometry.
Allowed range: 0.001 to 10000.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_smooth_angle:
Angle threshold used for shading piece surfaces. It changes normals, not the partition itself.
Minimum: 0 degrees preserves sharp boundaries between differing face normals.
Maximum: 180 degrees permits smoothing across the widest range of angles.
Allowed range: 0 to 180.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_enable:
Turns rusted-through holes on for this object.
Off: no holes are made, the settings are kept.
On: clusters of rust holes are added.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_seed:
Shuffles where the hole clusters sit and how they look, without changing their size.
Every number gives a different random arrangement.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_mode:
Automatic: the generator scatters the hole clusters; the Placement section is shown. Paint: holes are cut where you draw; a Drawing field with New Drawing, Draw / Edit and a delete button appears, and the Paint Settings section is shown instead. Draw dots, closed outlines and open trails.
Automatic: one cluster at a random place on the tile.
Paint: a dot (top left), a closed outline (right) and an open trail (bottom) drawn on the tile.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_avoid:
Keeps rust holes away from the faces you marked as Avoid.
Off: holes may appear on protected faces too.
On: protected faces stay whole.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_detail:
Outline resolution (0.05 to 4, default 0.8). Lower gives fewer faces, higher gives finer, lacier edges.
Low (0.3): coarse, polygonal outlines; small pits become simple shapes.
High (2): fine, ragged edges and more tiny pits; the mesh is heavier.
Allowed range: 0.05 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_amount:
Number of hole clusters (0 to 2000, default 5). Fewer are placed when there is no room left.
Low (1): one cluster.
High (20): the sheet is covered with corroded holes.
Allowed range: 0 to 2000.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_size_min:
Smallest main hole radius (default 1.5). The image uses Amount 8.
Low (0.5 cm): some clusters are very small.
High (4 cm): every cluster is at least 4 cm; the small ones are gone.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_size_max:
Largest main hole radius (default 5). The image uses Amount 8.
Low (2 cm): only small clusters.
High (12 cm): large holes that eat much of the sheet.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_size_bias:
Above 0.5 gives more small clusters, below more large ones (0 to 1, default 0.5). The image uses Amount 12 and Size Max 10 cm.
Low (0): most clusters are near Size Max; the sheet is badly eaten.
High (1): most clusters are near Size Min.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_min_spacing:
Closest distance between cluster centres, times the sum of their two radii (default 0.8); below 1 lets clusters run into each other. The image uses Amount 12 and Size Max 8 cm.
Low (0): clusters may overlap and merge into larger holes.
High (3): clusters keep well apart; fewer fit on the sheet.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_lobes:
Number of overlapping corrosion lobes that form each main hole (1 to 24, default 4). Automatic mode only.
Low (1): a single rounded main hole.
High (10): a larger, more cloud-like main hole.
Allowed range: 1 to 24.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_lobe_spread:
How far the lobes sit from the centre, times the size (0 to 2, default 0.55).
Low (0): all lobes on top of each other; a compact, round hole.
High (1.5): the lobes spread out into a wide, irregular hole.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_jagged:
Large-scale distortion of every outline (0 to 3, default 0.7).
Low (0): rounded outlines.
High (2.5): stretched, twisted outlines.
Allowed range: 0 to 3.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_roughness:
Fine ragged noise along the edges (0 to 4, default 0.5).
Low (0): clean edges.
High (2): the rim breaks up into many small eaten-through specks.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_scallop:
Eaten bites along the rim: scalloped edges with sharp cusps (0 to 5, default 1.4).
Low (0): a smooth rim.
High (4): a rim of many bites; the difference is small at this size.
Allowed range: 0 to 5.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_merge:
Fillet where pits and lobes join (0 to 2, default 0.35); 0 keeps hard cusps.
Low (0): sharp cusps where the discs meet.
High (1.5): pits near the hole fuse with it into one large rounded opening.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_lace:
Band of lacy, eaten-through metal round every hole (0 to 3, default 0.6); 0 = off.
Low (0): clean metal between the holes.
High (2): a wide band of small holes round the cluster.
Allowed range: 0 to 3.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_pit_amount:
Number of small holes round each cluster (0 to 2000, default 28).
Low (0): only the main hole.
High (100): many pits, some merging with the main hole.
Allowed range: 0 to 2000.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_pit_size:
Pit radius, times the cluster size; a few pits grow much larger (0 to 2, default 0.14).
Low (0.05): tiny pits.
High (0.4): large pits that merge into the main hole.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_pit_spread:
How far the pits reach, times the size (1 and up, default 2.4); they are denser near the hole.
Low (1): pits only right at the rim.
High (5): pits scattered far over the sheet.
Allowed range: 1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_crack_amount:
Number of thin cracks out of each rim (0 to 32, default 2).
Low (0): no cracks.
High (8): many short cracks round the hole.
Allowed range: 0 to 32.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_crack_length:
Crack length, times the cluster size (default 0.9).
Low (0.3): short notches in the rim.
High (3): long cracks running out over the sheet.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_crack_width:
Crack width at its root, tapering to the tip (default 0.15).
Low (0.05 cm): hairline cracks.
High (0.6 cm): wide slots that open the cluster up.
Allowed range: 0.0001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_crack_meander:
How much the cracks wander (0 to 2, default 0.7).
Low (0): straight cracks.
High (2): bent, wandering cracks.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_crack_fork:
Chance of side branches (0 to 1, default 0.25).
Low (0): single cracks.
High (1): the cracks fork into side branches.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_crack_pits:
Small holes strung along the cracks (0 to 1, default 0.35).
Low (0): clean cracks.
High (1): a row of small pits along each crack.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_flow:
Corrosion runs downhill: pits and cracks drift down the surface (0 to 1, default 0.4).
Low (0): pits all round the hole.
High (1): more pits below the hole and cracks running down.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_stretch:
Stretches the clusters downhill (0 to 3, default 0.25). Automatic mode only.
Low (0): round clusters.
High (2): the cluster and its pits are drawn out downward.
Allowed range: 0 to 3.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_down_x:
Local-space X component of down. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Minimum: Point this direction component toward negative X.
Maximum: Point toward positive X. Only the vector direction matters; avoid a zero vector.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_down_y:
Local-space Y component of down. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Minimum: Point this direction component toward negative Y.
Maximum: Point toward positive Y. Only the vector direction matters; avoid a zero vector.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_down_z:
Local-space Z component of down. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Minimum: Point this direction component toward negative Z.
Maximum: Point toward positive Z. Only the vector direction matters; avoid a zero vector.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_thickness:
Depth of the hole rim: holes are cut this far into the surface and open into the inside of the mesh; thinner walls are cut through (default 2). On sheet metal thinner than the value the holes simply go through. The image uses a solid steel block 5 cm thick.
Low (0.5 cm and 2 cm): on this solid 5 cm block nothing is cut at all.
High (6 cm): the value is more than the block thickness and the holes go through the block.
Allowed range: 0.0001 to 100.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_min_bridge:
Metal strips between holes narrower than this are eaten away (default 0.1).
Low (0 cm): even thin strips of metal stay.
High (1 cm): the hole and the pits round it merge into one large opening.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_paint_size:
Hole radius along open strokes (default 1.2).
Low (0.6 cm): a row of small holes along the trail.
High (2.5 cm): the holes are so large that they merge into one long opening.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_paint_spacing:
Spacing of the holes along open strokes, times Trail Size (0.2 and up, default 1.4).
Low (0.7): holes close together; the trail is almost one continuous slot.
High (3): separate round holes along the trail.
Allowed range: 0.2 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_paint_gaps:
Share of the trail spots left as metal (0 to 1, default 0.3).
Low (0): every spot is a hole.
High (0.8): most spots stay metal; only scattered holes and the crack are left.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_paint_crack:
Joins the trail holes with a thin crack along the stroke (default on).
Off: the trail holes are separate.
On: a hairline crack links them.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_paint_snap:
Largest distance of a stroke point from the surface (default 5). The image uses strokes drawn 3 cm in front of the tile.
Low (1 cm): the strokes are too far away; nothing is cut.
High (5 or 10 cm): the strokes are used. Keep it low so strokes do not reach other surfaces behind.
Allowed range: 0.0001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_paint_close:
Closes a stroke whose ends are this close, times its length (0 to 1, default 0.15); closed strokes are hole outlines. The image uses a ring drawn 330 degrees round, its ends 3 cm apart.
Low (0): the ring stays open and becomes a trail of holes.
High (0.15 and up): the ring is closed and cut as one large hole.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_paint_single:
Strokes shorter than this, and circles smaller than this, make one round cluster instead of a drawn outline or a trail (default 2).
Low (0 cm): every stroke is used as drawn; the outline on the right stays a drawn hole.
High (8 cm): the 10 cm outline on the right is small enough and becomes a round cluster.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_enable:
Dents the whole shape at the impact empties before any other damage is added.
Off: the shape is not dented.
On: the object is pushed in at every impact empty.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_collection:
Every empty is an impact: radius = its display size x scale, strength = its project_damage_deform_strength property (default 1).
Empty: no collection input.
Assigned: read supported helper objects from that collection.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_origin:
The point the dented parts are pushed toward.
Empty: parts are pushed toward the origin of the object.
Assigned: parts are pushed toward this object.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_protection:
A collection of cube empties that protect what is inside them from being dented.
Empty: everything may be dented.
Assigned: parts inside the cubes never move.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_strength:
Multiplies the strength of every impact (0 and up, default 1).
Low (0.3): a shallow dent with soft rings.
High (3): the dent is pushed as far as Maximum Deformation allows.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_max_deform:
How far toward the origin a vertex may be pushed, as a share of its distance (0 to 1, default 0.75). It also scales the push itself.
Low (0.2): the dent stops early; its floor is flat, as if pressed against a plate.
High (1): nothing limits the push; the centre is driven to the origin.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_total_amplitud:
Strength of the three noise layers (0 and up, default 1). The images use Noise Strength 1.
Low (0.3): only faint rings.
High (3): violent folds far past the dent.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_noise_factor:
Share of the noise in the dent (0 and up, default 0.3).
Low (0): a clean, round dent.
High (1.5): the dent breaks into sharp radial folds and its rim tears out.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_groups_x:
Vertex groups along this axis (search acceleration only).
Minimum: Lower the local X component.
Maximum: Raise the local X component.
Allowed range: 1 to 128.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_groups_y:
Vertex groups along this axis (search acceleration only).
Minimum: Lower the local Y component.
Maximum: Raise the local Y component.
Allowed range: 1 to 128.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_groups_z:
Vertex groups along this axis (search acceleration only).
Minimum: Lower the local Z component.
Maximum: Raise the local Z component.
Allowed range: 1 to 128.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_signature:
An internal number the addon uses to notice that the dent setup changed. You do not need to edit it.
Any value: no visible effect.
It is updated automatically.
Allowed range: -2.14748e+09 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_origin_mode:
Auto (default): each impact pushes straight into the surface under it, toward its own origin behind the surface. Empty: every vertex is pushed toward the Deformation Origin empty; Add Origin puts one at the volume centre of a closed mesh (Find Centre moves it there again). Without an empty Auto is used. Object Origin: every vertex is pushed toward the origin of the object.
Auto: a round dent straight into the side.
Empty at the body centre: the dent goes toward the middle of the body; here wider and deeper. Object Origin (here 10 cm below the body, on the floor): the dent is pushed down and in, skewed toward the floor.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_origin_depth:
Auto only: how far behind the surface each origin sits, times the impact radius (0.05 and up, default 1). The vertices move a share of their distance to the origin, so a deeper origin gives a deeper and wider push.
Low (0.3): a shallow dent.
High (3): a deep crater that pushes in the whole sphere of the impact.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_smoothness:
Blurs the dents along the surface after they are made: softer rims, calmer noise (0 to 1, default 0). It reaches about Smoothness x half the mean impact radius past the dents. Protected vertices stay put, so painted zones get a soft border.
Low (0): the original look, with sharp ripples and a crisp rim.
High (1): a smooth, shallow hollow; the ripples are gone.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_noise_scale:
Frequency of the noise (0 and up, default 1): higher gives more and finer ripples. The images use Noise Strength 1.
Low (0.3): broad concentric waves.
High (4): many fine, spiky folds.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_protect_group:
Vertex group painted with the protected areas: weight 1 never moves, 0.5 moves half.
Empty: no vertex-group restriction.
Assigned: use the named group weights on this object.
ProjectDamageProps.deform_protect_invert:
The button next to the group: the painted areas are the ones that may dent, the rest is protected.
Off: the painted area is protected.
On: only the painted area dents.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_enable:
Turns holes with material hanging from their edges on for this object.
Off: no such holes are made, the settings are kept.
On: the holes are added.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_seed:
Changes where the holes go and their shapes. The images use Amount 2.
Every number gives another arrangement.
There is no low or high, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_mode:
Auto (default): the generator makes its own holes. Breakers: the linked Boolean breakers make the holes; the Distribution box is replaced by a Breakers box with a Breakers Collection field and the breaker list. The image uses two sphere breakers of 22 and 30 cm radius on the face of the wall.
Auto: one hole of the Distribution settings.
Breakers: one opening per breaker, shaped by the breaker; the smaller one did not reach through the wall.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_avoid:
Keeps these holes away from the faces you marked as Avoid.
Off: holes may land on protected faces too.
On: protected faces stay whole.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_amount:
Cables per hole (default 3).
Low (1): a single cable.
High (10): many cables, some hanging across the opening.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_size_min:
Smallest hole, in cm.
Low: some holes are tiny.
High: even the smallest hole is big.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_size_max:
Largest hole, in cm.
Low: all holes stay small.
High: some holes are large.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_jagged:
How ragged the outline is (default 0.6).
Low (0): a round, clean opening.
High (2): a torn opening with deep notches.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_flare:
How much wider the hole is at the face it was hit from: a crater round the opening (default 0.35). The images look at the hole from the side.
Low (0): straight walls through the wall.
High (1.2): a wide crater narrowing to the opening.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_roughness:
How strong each finer octave is compared with the one before (0 to 0.95, default 0.5). The images use Detail 5.
Low (0.2): the fine octaves almost vanish.
High (0.9): sharp, jagged walls.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_surf_mode:
Choose Hole Surface. Procedural: Rough walls; Texture: Image displacement on top.
Procedural: Rough walls.
Texture: Image displacement on top.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_tex_path:
A black and white image that roughens the broken edge. White sticks out, black sinks in.
Empty: the built-in gravel image is used.
Assigned: your own image shapes the break.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_tex_scale:
How big one repeat of the image is on the surface, in cm.
Low: small, busy texture detail.
High: large, stretched-out texture detail.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_tex_strength:
How deep the image presses into the broken surface, in cm.
0: the image is ignored.
High: deep, rough relief from the image.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_tex_offset_x:
X translation of the procedural pattern in local coordinates.
Minimum: Move the pattern toward negative X.
Maximum: Move the pattern toward positive X. Feature size is unchanged.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_tex_offset_y:
Y translation of the procedural pattern in local coordinates.
Minimum: Move the pattern toward negative Y.
Maximum: Move the pattern toward positive Y. Feature size is unchanged.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_tex_offset_z:
Z translation of the procedural pattern in local coordinates.
Minimum: Move the pattern toward negative Z.
Maximum: Move the pattern toward positive Z. Feature size is unchanged.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_tex_edge:
mesh edge (cm), 0 = scale / 60.
Minimum: At zero use the automatic size described above; small positive sizes produce fine, heavier geometry.
Maximum: Larger cells or edges: coarser, faster geometry that may lose small features.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_bars_enable:
reinforcement bars.
Off: omit bars enable while keeping its stored settings.
On: use bars enable with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_bar_spacing:
Distance between the bars in cm (default 15).
Low (8 cm): a dense mesh.
High (30 cm): a few bars.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_bar_radius:
Cable radius in cm (default 0.18).
Low (0.1 cm): thin wires.
High (0.6 cm): thick cables.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_bar_depth:
Depth of the bar layer as a share of the wall thickness (default 0.5, the middle).
Low (0.15): bars near the front face.
High (0.85): bars near the back.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_bar_broken:
Chance that a bar crossing the opening is snapped (default 0.65).
Low (0): every bar spans the hole.
High (1): every bar is snapped; only stubs hang from the rim.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_droop:
How far the loose bar ends bend down (default 0.7).
Low (0): the ends stick straight out.
High (2): the ends hang down.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_bar_bow:
Sag of the bars that are still whole (default 0.6). The images use Broken 0.
Low (0): straight bars.
High (2): the bars sag in the opening.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_cables_enable:
cables.
Off: omit cables enable while keeping its stored settings.
On: use cables enable with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_cable_amount:
Cables per hole (default 3).
Low (1): a single cable.
High (10): many cables, some hanging across the opening.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_cable_radius:
Cable radius in cm (default 0.18).
Low (0.1 cm): thin wires.
High (0.6 cm): thick cables.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_cable_length:
Cable length, times the hole radius (default 1).
Low (0.3): short stubs.
High (3): long cables that reach across the hole.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_cable_sag:
How floppy the cables are (default 0.5).
Low (0): wide, stiff arcs.
High (2): the cables hang close and straight down.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_cable_loops:
Share of the cables slung as loops between two points instead of hanging free (default 0.35). The images use Amount 8.
Low (0): only loose hanging ends.
High (1): every cable is a loop across the opening.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_sides:
Number of sides of the bar and cable tubes (Sides, default 8). It does not change the hole.
Low (4): square bars.
High (16): round bars, more polygons.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_gravity_x:
Local-space X component of gravity. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Minimum: Point this direction component toward negative X.
Maximum: Point toward positive X. Only the vector direction matters; avoid a zero vector.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_gravity_y:
Local-space Y component of gravity. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Minimum: Point this direction component toward negative Y.
Maximum: Point toward positive Y. Only the vector direction matters; avoid a zero vector.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_gravity_z:
Local-space Z component of gravity. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Minimum: Point this direction component toward negative Z.
Maximum: Point toward positive Z. Only the vector direction matters; avoid a zero vector.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hit_through_enable:
Alternative to the ordinary asset, sharing its impact and material settings.
Off: omit through asset while keeping its stored settings.
On: use through asset with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.hit_through:
Detach impact plates or glass shards as loose mesh islands.
Off: omit pass through while keeping its stored settings.
On: use pass through with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.hit_through_gap:
Gap between pieces; for Glass, zero gives a hairline split so the shards fit together with no visible gap. Follows Master Scale.
Minimum: Small or closed gaps between neighbouring elements.
Maximum: Larger visible separation between neighbouring elements.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hit_through_min_piece:
Throws away slivers that are too small, as a share of the smallest part of the object.
0: every sliver is kept.
High (10): only solid pieces are kept.
Allowed range: 0 to 10.
ProjectDamageProps.glass_through_enable:
Alternative to the ordinary asset, sharing its impact and material settings.
Off: omit through asset while keeping its stored settings.
On: use through asset with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.glass_through:
Detach impact plates or glass shards as loose mesh islands.
Off: omit pass through while keeping its stored settings.
On: use pass through with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.glass_through_gap:
Gap between the pieces (default 0, a hairline split so the shards fit together with no visible gap). It follows Master Scale.
Low (0 cm): the shards touch.
High (1 cm): wide gaps between the shards.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.glass_through_min_pie:
Removes slivers smaller than this percentage of the smallest part of the source (default 0.02). No image.
Allowed range: 0 to 10.
ProjectDamageProps.hit_through_max_wall:
Thickest wall an impact still breaks right through, in cm. Thicker walls only lose a chunk from the surface.
0: nothing is broken through.
High: even thick walls are broken through.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hit_chunk_depth:
How deep the broken-out chunk goes on a thick wall, compared with the size of the impact.
Low: a shallow flake comes off.
High: a deep chunk is knocked out.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.hit_through_remove:
Fraction of hit-zone chunks removed entirely, from zero to one.
Minimum: Keep more of the original structure intact.
Maximum: Omit or break a larger share of eligible elements.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.glass_through_rings:
Make Pass Through only. Number of ring cracks that form rows of shards, limited by Ring Count; the last ring closes (default 2). The image uses Remove Shards 0.6.
Low (1): one row of shards round the opening.
High (4): four rows; the loose area grows.
Allowed range: 1 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.glass_through_fall:
Make Pass Through only. Share of the shards knocked out completely (0 to 1, default 0).
Low (0): every shard stays in place.
High (1): all loose shards are gone; a large hole is left.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.glass_pass_through:
The cracks round the opening cut through the pane, so the shards between them come apart as loose pieces (default off). The image uses Remove Shards 0.5.
Off: the cracks are grooves; the pane is one piece.
On: the shards are cut loose, and half of them are knocked out.
ProjectDamageProps.glass_fill_hole:
Fills the opening with loose shards, denser at the centre, for a simulation (default off). With Make Pass Through off, Piece Gap and Min Piece are shown under it. The images use Piece Gap 0.3 cm, so the shards can be seen.
Off: an open hole.
On: the hole is filled with shards.
ProjectDamageProps.glass_fill_count:
Fill Hole only. Number of shards filling one hole (2 to 500, default 40).
Low (10): a few large shards.
High (150): many small shards.
Allowed range: 2 to 500.
ProjectDamageProps.glass_fill_center:
Fill Hole only. 0 spreads the shards evenly; 1 packs small shards tightly round the impact centre (default 0.7).
Low (0): even shard sizes.
High (1): tiny shards in the middle, large ones at the rim.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_density:
How heavy the material is. It is used to work out the weight of every piece.
0: the weight is taken from the chosen material type.
High: heavy pieces that hit hard and are hard to push.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_physics:
Unused compatibility value; Rigid Body Fracture creates geometry only.
Off: omit legacy physics while keeping its stored settings.
On: use legacy physics with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_impact_collection:
Collection supplying this effect's helper objects. Only supported object types are read; the source mesh itself is not used as a helper.
Empty: no collection input.
Assigned: read supported helper objects from that collection.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_cuts_drawing:
Grease Pencil or supported curve input read at the current frame and transformed into the source's local coordinates.
Low / first state: Unassigned supplies no stroke constraints.
High / other state: Assigned visible paths influence the partition according to Stroke Mode.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_impacts_drawing:
Grease Pencil or supported curve input read at the current frame and transformed into the source's local coordinates.
Low / first state: Unassigned supplies no stroke constraints.
High / other state: Assigned visible paths influence the partition according to Stroke Mode.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_material:
Selects the partition recipe: stretched grain for Wood, an impact network for planar Glass, or material-specific cellular relief for Concrete, Rock and Soil. This is an algorithm selector, not a Blender material slot.
Low / first state: Choose the type that matches the source structure.
High / other state: Changing it also changes automatic roughness, size variation and rubble defaults when those values are -1.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_planar:
Auto uses principal-axis thickness and the material recipe; Volume uses a 3D partition; Planar extends a 2D partition through thickness.
Low / first state: Volume gives volumetric cells.
High / other state: Planar suits thin panels; Auto switches only when its thickness test and material recipe allow it.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_stroke_mode:
Crack Lines adds paired seeds along paths; Shatter Zone treats segments as density sources; Both combines these operations.
Low / first state: Crack Lines favours boundaries following the paths.
High / other state: Shatter Zone concentrates smaller cells near paths; Both combines line guidance and local density.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_enable:
Breaks the object into solid pieces with rough, natural break faces.
Off: the object stays in one piece.
On: the object is split into solid pieces.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_keep_remainder:
Groups the far, relatively intact region instead of treating it as independent background damage.
Off: Off partitions the entire source.
On: On keeps a larger remainder around the local impact region; final count reconciliation can still split or merge pieces.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_seed:
Rerolls the partition while combining this seed with the object's main Seed.
Minimum: 0 is the first repeatable layout.
Maximum: Other integers give other repeatable layouts; larger numbers are not stronger damage.
Allowed range: 0 to 100000.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_pieces:
Number of background pieces before drawn cuts. Guidance can add local pieces and Draw Cut can divide them further.
Minimum 1: begin with one cell.
Maximum 2000: request 2000 background cells; dense inputs take more time.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_max_pieces:
Safety cap for Cell Fracture output. Surplus cells merge into neighbours rather than disappear.
Minimum: very few large output pieces.
Maximum: permit a denser partition at higher processing cost.
Allowed range: 2 to 5000.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_glass_spokes:
Number of primary radial directions in a planar glass impact network.
Minimum: 3 creates a few broad radial sectors.
Maximum: 64 creates many narrow radial sectors, subject to piece-count reconciliation.
Allowed range: 3 to 64.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_gap:
Separates adjacent cell boundaries by removing material at the cut, rather than translating finished pieces.
Minimum: 0 keeps matching pieces tiled together.
Maximum: Large gaps remove more material and can erase small pieces.
Allowed range: 0 to 1000.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_size_variation:
Controls irregularity in cell size; -1 is a material-specific automatic value, not a negative variation.
Minimum: -1 uses the selected type's default; 0 gives the most even sizes.
Maximum: 1 gives strong size variation while retaining the requested final piece-count target.
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_roughness:
Amplitude of shared boundary relief. -1 selects the material default. The relief field deforms neighbouring partitions together.
Minimum: -1 is automatic; 0 disables this relief.
Maximum: 1.5 is strong relief. The source comments identify rare folds above about 1.25; Detail cannot remove folds caused by excessive amplitude.
Allowed range: -1 to 1.5.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_rough_scale:
Wavelength of the break-face relief relative to characteristic piece size. Amplitude is adjusted with wavelength to control field gradients.
Minimum: 0.05 gives small relief features.
Maximum: 10 gives broad features; increasing this is not the same as adding more octaves.
Allowed range: 0.05 to 10.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_detail:
Refinement used to resolve the relief field; the native builder also enforces an overall triangle budget.
Minimum: 0.01 is coarse and can miss small relief.
Maximum: 4 resolves finer relief at greater cost; budget clamping can limit the visible increase.
Allowed range: 0.01 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_planar_ratio:
Auto-planar threshold: smallest principal extent must be below this fraction of the middle extent.
Minimum: 0.01 restricts automatic planar treatment to extremely thin shapes.
Maximum: 1 admits much thicker shapes; it has no effect when Volume or Planar is forced.
Allowed range: 0.01 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_prox_radius:
Fallback influence radius for point sources. A per-object radius can override it when radius-from-size is enabled.
Minimum: A small radius concentrates local bias.
Maximum: A large radius spreads the density bias through more of the source.
Allowed range: 0.001 to 100000.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_prox_density:
Density multiplier at source centres: rho = 1 + (density - 1) times influence. The final requested piece count remains the target.
Minimum: 1 gives no density increase.
Maximum: 100 strongly concentrates the partition near points, with larger pieces farther away.
Allowed range: 1 to 100.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_prox_falloff:
Exponent in exp(-(distance/radius)^falloff). It changes the shape of the density transition, not its peak.
Minimum: 0.25 gives a long soft tail and a less flat centre.
Maximum: 8 gives a flatter centre and a much sharper transition near the radius.
Allowed range: 0.25 to 8.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_rubble:
Amount of small pieces near impact sources; -1 uses the material default.
Minimum: -1 is automatic; 0 adds no rubble population.
Maximum: 1 adds the strongest local rubble population before final count reconciliation.
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_remainder_reach:
How far the local region extends from point sources, as a multiple of their radius, when an intact remainder is requested.
Minimum: 0.1 keeps a very small fractured neighbourhood.
Maximum: 20 lets the local region extend far from each source; irrelevant with Intact Remainder off.
Allowed range: 0.1 to 20.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_stroke_spacing:
Spacing of samples used to add crack-line constraints.
Minimum: 0 computes an automatic spacing from characteristic cell size.
Maximum: Larger positive values place fewer constraints along a stroke and follow it less tightly.
Allowed range: 0 to 10000.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_grain_x:
X component of the local grain axis, normalised with Y and Z.
Minimum: -1 points the X contribution toward negative X.
Maximum: 1 points it toward positive X; the axis controls shape direction, not cell size by itself.
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_grain_y:
Y component of the normalised local grain axis.
Minimum: -1 points toward negative Y.
Maximum: 1 points toward positive Y; combine the three components to choose the grain axis.
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_grain_z:
Z component of the normalised local grain axis.
Minimum: -1 points toward negative Z.
Maximum: 1 points toward positive Z; Wood's stretching and splinter relief use this axis.
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_grain_stretch:
Anisotropic cell stretch along the grain; the partition is built in compressed coordinates and transformed back.
Minimum: 1 gives isotropic cells.
Maximum: 100 permits very long, thin grain-aligned pieces.
Allowed range: 1 to 100.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_splinter:
Amplitude of the additional grain-oriented splinter field.
Minimum: 0 disables splinter relief.
Maximum: 2 gives the strongest grain splinter relief; enough Detail is needed to resolve it.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_glass_ring_grow:
Multiplicative growth of successive ring distances from an impact.
Minimum: 1.15 keeps successive rings close together.
Maximum: 10 rapidly increases spacing between outer rings.
Allowed range: 1.15 to 10.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_glass_branch:
Probability of branching in the planar impact crack network.
Minimum: 0 suppresses optional branching.
Maximum: 1 uses the maximum branching probability.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_glass_wander:
Irregular angular wandering of planar glass cracks.
Minimum: 0 keeps the network relatively regular.
Maximum: 2 gives stronger deviations from ideal spokes and rings.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_glass_hole:
Central opening radius as a fraction of the hit radius in the planar glass network.
Minimum: 0 keeps the impact centre filled with pieces.
Maximum: 1 removes the widest central region supported by the hit radius.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_inner_uv_scale:
World-length scale for UVs on generated inner faces, in centimetres.
Minimum: 0.001 produces many texture repeats over a face.
Maximum: 10000 gives very large texture features and fewer repeats; it does not change geometry.
Allowed range: 0.001 to 10000.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_smooth_angle:
Angle threshold used for shading piece surfaces. It changes normals, not the partition itself.
Minimum: 0 degrees preserves sharp boundaries between differing face normals.
Maximum: 180 degrees permits smoothing across the widest range of angles.
Allowed range: 0 to 180.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_prox_collection:
Collection of impact objects. The host converts their positions, optional display-size radii and strength into point sources.
Low / first state: Empty: no point sources are supplied.
High / other state: Assigned: objects locally bias fracture density; Add Empty creates a point without leaving this workflow.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_prox_use_size:
Uses an Empty's display size and largest object scale to provide its radius, converted to the source's local units. The regular Radius is the fallback for other source cases.
Off: Off uses the shared Radius for points.
On: On permits each Empty to have its own radius; resizing its display or scale changes the influenced region.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_drawing:
Grease Pencil or Curve for through cuts. On a shared drawing, only Draw Through layers are read.
Empty: no through cuts. Assigned: project actual strokes into the object, stopping at earlier crossing cutters. A short contact that does not divide a cell leaves it unchanged.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_surface_drawing:
Grease Pencil or Curve for surface-only cuts. On a shared drawing, only Draw Surface layers are read.
Empty: no surface cuts. Assigned: divide directly touched cells only when a stroke crosses them; deeper cells and incomplete contacts remain unchanged.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_draw_mode:
Choose how a drawn cutting curtain enters Cell Fracture pieces. This selector changes the drawing target, not the seed density.
Through Cut: project along the surface normal through the solid, stopping at an earlier crossing cut.
Surface Cut: split only pieces touched by the stroke; deeper pieces remain intact.
ProjectDamageProps.bevel_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve that marks which edges get worn. Draw close to the edges.
Empty: edges are picked automatically.
Assigned: only edges under your strokes are worn.
ProjectDamageProps.scratch_drawing:
Grease Pencil or curve object with the strokes that guide the scratches. Draw where the object gets scratched. New Drawing creates one, Draw / Edit lets you draw on the object
empty or no drawing: nothing is made from strokes
More strokes: more places get the effect
ProjectDamageProps.bullet_drawing:
Grease Pencil or curve object with the strokes that place the shots (Paint mode). New Drawing creates one, Draw / Edit lets you draw on the object
empty or no drawing: nothing is made from strokes
More strokes: more places get the effect
ProjectDamageProps.ground_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve that shows where the ground cracks. Draw close to the surface.
Empty: cracks are placed automatically.
Assigned: cracks follow your strokes.
ProjectDamageProps.brick_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve that shows where the plaster breaks off the bricks. Draw close to the surface.
Empty: patches are placed automatically.
Assigned: patches follow your strokes.
ProjectDamageProps.fissure_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve that gives the path of the fissure. Draw close to the surface.
Empty: the fissure is placed automatically.
Assigned: the fissure follows your stroke.
ProjectDamageProps.glass_holes_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve with the outlines of holes in the glass. Draw close to the pane.
Empty: holes are placed automatically.
Assigned: holes are knocked out where you drew them.
ProjectDamageProps.glass_impacts_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve with the points where something hit the glass. Draw close to the pane.
Empty: impacts are placed automatically.
Assigned: the glass breaks at your marks.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve that shows where the metal rusts through. Draw close to the surface.
Empty: holes are placed automatically.
Assigned: holes appear along your strokes.
ProjectDamageProps.metal_collection:
Collection supplying this effect's helper objects. Only supported object types are read; the source mesh itself is not used as a helper.
Empty: no collection input.
Assigned: read supported helper objects from that collection.
ProjectDamageProps.metal_crush_collectio:
Collection supplying this effect's helper objects. Only supported object types are read; the source mesh itself is not used as a helper.
Empty: no collection input.
Assigned: read supported helper objects from that collection.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_enable:
Turns worn concrete edges on: a soft worn-off edge with broken stretches.
Off: edges stay sharp.
On: edges are worn and chipped.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_seed:
Seed for repeatable wear patches and bevel variation.
Minimum: 0 selects the first repeatable variant.
Maximum: Other values reroll the pattern; there is no increasing intensity with seed value.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_avoid:
Skip edges that touch an Avoid face.
Off: omit respect avoid while keeping its stored settings.
On: use respect avoid with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_detail:
Increases along-run sampling and cutter-profile segments. Multiplied by Master Quality and clamped natively.
Minimum: 0.05 gives the cheapest supported sampling.
Maximum: 4 resolves finer broken relief and curved profiles, with more Boolean work.
Allowed range: 0.05 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_angle:
Minimum dihedral angle between adjacent face normals for a convex edge to enter the edge-run graph.
Minimum: 1 degree admits very shallow convex changes.
Maximum: 179 degrees admits only extremely sharp folds; ordinary 90-degree box edges are excluded.
Allowed range: 1 to 179.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_drawn_only:
Restricts the edge-run selection to drawn strokes.
Off: Off processes all eligible convex runs.
On: On uses the stroke distance, alignment and coverage tests; a missing valid drawing yields no selected runs.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_paint_radius:
Maximum distance between an edge sample and a drawing segment.
Minimum: A small radius requires close tracing.
Maximum: A larger radius can select neighbouring edges too.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_paint_align:
Maximum angular difference between an edge direction and its nearby stroke direction.
Minimum: 0 degrees requires alignment.
Maximum: 90 degrees permits any direction; proximity and coverage still apply.
Allowed range: 0 to 90.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_paint_cover:
Minimum fraction of samples along an edge that must pass the drawing test.
Minimum: 0 is permissive; any edge reaching this test can pass the fraction check.
Maximum: 1 requires all tested samples to be covered.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_max_turn:
Largest direction change allowed when joining neighbouring edges into one run.
Minimum: 0 joins only straight continuations.
Maximum: 89 degrees joins around much stronger turns, affecting patch continuity.
Allowed range: 0 to 89.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_width:
Width of the swept chamfer along the adjoining faces, capped by local available thickness and Max Share.
Minimum: 0 removes the clean chamfer but can leave damage active.
Maximum: Larger widths expose a broad bevel until local limits stop further growth.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_smoothness:
Rounds the chamfer profile and reduces high-frequency roughness on the broken surface. The chamfer reaches its fully rounded profile at roughly 0.625.
Minimum: 0 gives a straight chamfer and crisp broken relief.
Maximum: 1 gives a rounded bevel and softer damage transitions.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_profile_shape:
Bends the bevel profile toward the original sharp edge, independently of the smoothness-derived rounding.
Minimum: 0 uses the profile determined by Smoothness.
Maximum: 1 gives the strongest bulge toward the original edge.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_uneven:
Slow variation in chamfer width along each run. Its wavelength depends on bevel width and patch length.
Minimum: 0 keeps a constant nominal width.
Maximum: 1 gives the strongest width wandering, still capped by Max Share.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_max_share:
Maximum chamfer or local cut reach as a share of measured available thickness on adjoining faces.
Minimum: 0.01 applies a strict local cap.
Maximum: 0.99 allows almost the full local thickness; it does not increase nominal Width by itself.
Allowed range: 0.01 to 0.99.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_damage:
Multiplies Damage Depth to obtain the break's base depth. Damage Factor must also be nonzero.
Minimum: 0 disables broken stretches even when a chamfer is present.
Maximum: 1 uses the full Damage Depth.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_damage_amount:
Controls bite length inside damaged patches: characteristic length changes from 2.6 to 0.9 times break depth.
Minimum: 0 gives fewer, longer chunks.
Maximum: 1 gives more, shorter chunks; it does not change the total damaged-length fraction.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_damage_factor:
Fraction of each eligible run's length assigned to damaged patches. The patch allocator preserves this length fraction while distributing stretches and gaps.
Minimum: 0 leaves no broken stretches, including in Clean and Narrow presets.
Maximum: 1 assigns the whole eligible run to damage; Amount controls subdivision within it.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_damage_depth:
Base cut depth in centimetres, multiplied by Damage and Master Scale.
Minimum: 0 disables this damage geometry.
Maximum: Larger values permit deeper missing chunks; local geometry still limits the cut.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_patch_length:
Typical length of a contiguous damaged stretch, before placement randomness.
Minimum: 0.1 cm gives many short stretches for a fixed coverage fraction.
Maximum: Larger values combine damaged length into fewer, longer stretches.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_chip_scatter:
Adds scattered chip variation around the broken stretches.
Minimum: 0 keeps damage concentrated in its base profile.
Maximum: 1 gives the strongest scattered chip contribution.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_jagged:
High-frequency radial roughness of break faces and boundaries. Smoothness and Smooth Damage Surface attenuate it.
Minimum: 0 removes this roughness contribution.
Maximum: 1 gives maximum jaggedness before smoothing attenuation.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_placement_rand:
Varies damaged patch lengths, gaps and depths while preserving the requested total damaged-length fraction.
Minimum: 0 gives a regular arrangement.
Maximum: 1 gives the most irregular placement.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_smooth_damage:
Enables a separate relaxation of broken faces, depth transitions and chip shapes.
Off: Off keeps the basic broken relief.
On: On applies Smooth Damage Amount without smoothing the whole source mesh.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_smooth_damage_:
Strength of the separate broken-surface smoothing. It reduces relief octaves and roughness and blends depth steps.
Minimum: 0 leaves the broken profile unchanged by this option.
Maximum: 1 gives the softest broken profile; only active when Smooth Damage Surface is on.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_export_segment:
Also build the broken-off pieces so Fill Segments can make fill objects for Fracture and Quick Physics (a second Boolean per build).
Off: omit pieces for physics while keeping its stored settings.
On: use pieces for physics with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_mask_width:
Width of the exported wear-mask fade around the bevel. This is material-mask data, not a second chamfer.
Minimum: 0 gives no extended fade width.
Maximum: Larger values spread the mask farther onto adjoining surfaces.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_mask_noise:
Irregularity in the exported wear-mask boundary.
Minimum: 0 gives the most regular mask.
Maximum: 1 gives the most irregular supported mask boundary.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_mask_scale:
Spatial size of the wear-mask irregularities.
Minimum: Small values give fine mask breakup.
Maximum: Large values give broad mask breakup; visible only in a shader using the mask.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_up_x:
X component of the local Up vector used to choose the sweep's top/side frame.
Minimum: Negative X reverses that directional contribution.
Maximum: Positive X points the reference toward local positive X; combine with Y and Z.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_up_y:
Y component of the local Up reference vector.
Minimum: Negative Y reverses that contribution.
Maximum: Positive Y points toward local positive Y.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_up_z:
Z component of the local Up reference vector.
Minimum: Negative Z points the reference downward.
Maximum: Positive Z points upward; this orients the frame rather than applying gravity.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.dbevel_preset:
Sets a coordinated group of shape controls. Editing one of those controls changes the selector to Custom.
Low / first state: Clean and Narrow set Damage Factor to zero and produce a chamfer without broken stretches.
High / other state: Heavy, Chipped and Weathered choose different depth, coverage and smoothness combinations; a preset is not a quality level.
ProjectDamageProps.bevel_preset:
Choose Profile Defaults. Custom; Dwarf Wall; Round Top; Flat Top; Dropper; Half Batter; Full Batter; Bull Nose; Channel.
Custom: select this profile defaults variant.
Dwarf Wall: select this profile defaults variant.
Round Top: select this profile defaults variant.
Flat Top: select this profile defaults variant.
Dropper: select this profile defaults variant.
Half Batter: select this profile defaults variant.
Full Batter: select this profile defaults variant.
Bull Nose: select this profile defaults variant.
Channel: select this profile defaults variant.
ProjectDamageProps.blast_collection:
Collection supplying this effect's helper objects. Only supported object types are read; the source mesh itself is not used as a helper.
Empty: no collection input.
Assigned: read supported helper objects from that collection.
ProjectDamageProps.wallpaper_material:
Material for the front of the wallpaper.
Empty: the default wallpaper material is kept.
Assigned: the wallpaper gets this material.
ProjectDamageProps.wallpaper_back_materi:
Material for the back side of the wallpaper, seen where it peels away.
Empty: the default paper back is kept.
Assigned: the back side gets this material.
ProjectDamageProps.wall_material:
Material for the bare wall that shows where the wallpaper is gone.
Empty: the default wall material is kept.
Assigned: the bare wall gets this material.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_enable:
Turns the inner construction on, so that holes show steel bars, bricks or timber inside the wall.
Off: holes are empty inside.
On: the inner construction is built and shown in the holes.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_seed:
On the breaker Empty: the seed of its noise (Add Breaker gives each new breaker its own).
Every number gives another break line.
There is no low or high.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_layout:
Choose Layout. Grid: One mesh layer (wall, slab); Double Grid: A mesh layer behind each face; Column Cage: Corner and side bars with stirrups; Round Cage: Bars on a circle with hoops or a spiral.
Grid: One mesh layer (wall, slab).
Double Grid: A mesh layer behind each face.
Column Cage: Corner and side bars with stirrups.
Round Cage: Bars on a circle with hoops or a spiral.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_axis:
Choose Axis. Auto: Grid: thinnest side is the wall normal. Cage: longest side is the column axis; X; Y; Z.
Auto: Grid: thinnest side is the wall normal. Cage: longest side is the column axis.
X: select this axis variant.
Y: select this axis variant.
Z: select this axis variant.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_side:
Choose Side. + Face: Near the face on the positive side of the axis; - Face: Near the face on the negative side of the axis; Centre: In the middle of the wall.
+ Face: Near the face on the positive side of the axis.
- Face: Near the face on the negative side of the axis.
Centre: In the middle of the wall.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_angle:
Rotation of the reinforcement grid within its placement plane.
Minimum: Rotate or tilt toward the lower end of the permitted angle range.
Maximum: Rotate or tilt toward the upper end; angles are not a damage-strength multiplier.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_cover:
How deep the steel bars sit below the wall surface.
Low: bars show even in shallow damage.
High: bars show only in deep holes.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_spacing_u:
Distance between the steel bars running in the first direction.
Low: a dense grid of bars.
High: a few bars far apart.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_spacing_v:
Distance between the steel bars running in the second direction.
Low: a dense grid of bars.
High: a few bars far apart.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_bars_u:
Enable Bars U for this object.
Off: omit bars u while keeping its stored settings.
On: use bars u with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_bars_v:
Enable Bars V for this object.
Off: omit bars v while keeping its stored settings.
On: use bars v with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_outer:
Choose Outer. U Bars: U bars sit nearer the surface; V Bars: V bars sit nearer the surface.
U Bars: U bars sit nearer the surface.
V Bars: V bars sit nearer the surface.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_amount:
Edge Breakup fold, Plane and Strip only: how strongly the outline of the breaker is broken up (0 to 50 %, default 13 %).
Low (0 %): the ends of the cut are straight and clean.
High (40 %): the ends of the cut are torn and rounded.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_jitter:
How unevenly the bars are spaced.
0: a perfect regular grid.
High: bars sit at uneven distances, like real site work.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_tie_spacing:
Distance between the wire ties that hold the bars together.
Low: ties at almost every crossing.
High: only a few ties.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_tie_radius:
Thickness of the tie wire.
Low: thin wire.
High: thick wire.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_spiral:
Enable Spiral for this object.
Off: omit spiral while keeping its stored settings.
On: use spiral with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_type:
Choose Type. Ribbed: Deformed bar: two longitudinal ribs and inclined crescent ribs; Helical Ribs: Cold-rolled bar with one continuous helical rib; Smooth: Plain round bar, old structures and wire mesh; Twisted Square: Cold-twisted square bar; Strand: 7-wire prestressing strand.
Ribbed: Deformed bar: two longitudinal ribs and inclined crescent ribs.
Helical Ribs: Cold-rolled bar with one continuous helical rib.
Smooth: Plain round bar, old structures and wire mesh.
Twisted Square: Cold-twisted square bar.
Strand: 7-wire prestressing strand.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_radius:
Thickness of the main steel bars.
Low: thin rods.
High: heavy bars.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_scale:
Multiplies the surface noise Strength of every breaker (10 to 400 %, default 100 %). It does not change the size of the cut.
Low (50 %): a smoother break face.
High (200 %): a deeply broken face and a ragged rim.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_rib_height:
Height of the ribs on the steel bars.
0: smooth round bars.
High: strongly ribbed bars.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_rib_pitch:
Distance between the ribs along a bar.
Low: ribs close together.
High: ribs far apart.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_twist_pitch:
How quickly the rib pattern spirals around the bar.
Low: a tight spiral.
High: a long, lazy spiral.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_sides:
How round a bar is, counted in flat sides.
Low: an angular bar, light mesh.
High: a smooth round bar, heavier mesh.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_detail:
Octaves of the noise (1 to 8, default 4).
Low (1): soft shapes only.
High (8): extra fine grain; the change from 4 is small.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_embed:
How far the bars continue into the intact wall around a hole.
Low: bars end right at the edge of the hole.
High: bars run far into the wall, safe for big holes.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_min_exposed:
Shortest visible piece of bar that is still kept.
Low: even tiny stubs are shown.
High: only long visible runs are shown.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_wobble:
Small side-to-side waviness of the bars.
0: perfectly straight bars.
High: visibly crooked bars.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_bow:
Broad curvature along exposed reinforcement runs.
Minimum: Nearly straight exposed bars.
Maximum: Broader curvature of exposed bars without changing their cross-section.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_bend:
How much the broken ends of the bars are bent.
0: straight ends.
High: ends bent far out of line.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_broken:
Share of eligible reinforcement runs with a broken end.
Minimum: Keep more of the original structure intact.
Maximum: Omit or break a larger share of eligible elements.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_trim:
How much is cut off the visible ends of the bars.
0: bars reach across the whole hole.
High: bars are broken short and leave a gap.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_neck:
How much a bar thins toward its broken end.
0: a blunt end with full thickness.
High: the end is pulled thin like stretched steel.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_drop_loose:
Remove unsupported internal fill. Upright bricks must rest on supported bricks, be gripped, hang at most one course or bridge one gap; steel and wood use their anchoring checks. Disable for the previous loose/connectivity behavior.
Off: omit drop loose while keeping its stored settings.
On: use drop loose with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_mode:
On the breaker Empty: Plane (default), Sphere or Strip. With a Cutter object (or a mesh child) the breaker is Custom and Mode is greyed out. The images use a Plane of 120 x 60 cm at the top, a Sphere of 30 cm radius and a Strip of 80 x 60 cm with Thickness 8 cm.
Plane: the top of the wall is broken off along a rough line.
Sphere: a round bite. Strip: a slab between two break faces is removed.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_fit:
Auto selects a fitting strategy; Object Box suits regular walls and columns; Follow Shape follows organic or sculpted forms.
Auto: Object Box for box-like objects (walls, slabs, columns), Follow Shape for everything else.
Object Box: The layout fills the object's bounding box (the original behaviour).
Follow Shape: Statues, sculpts, organic parts: a grid under the damaged surface, or a cage of bars and hoops that follows the body.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_deform:
Overall irregular bending of the visible bars.
0: bars keep their neat shape.
High: bars are twisted and pushed about.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_reach:
How far around a hole the inner construction is built.
Low: only right at the hole.
High: far around the hole, safe but heavier.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_core:
Enable Core for this object.
Off: omit core while keeping its stored settings.
On: use core with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_show_all:
Enable Show All for this object.
Off: omit show all while keeping its stored settings.
On: use show all with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_stroke_radius:
How far from a line you drew the inner construction is built.
Low: a narrow strip along the line.
High: a wide zone around the line.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_stroke_embed:
How far the inner construction continues past the visible damage along a drawn line.
Low: it ends right at the damage.
High: it runs far past the damage.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_fill:
Choose steel reinforcement, a connected brick layer, wooden boards, or a timber stud frame behind a drywall skin (Wood Framing) inside Boolean-damaged regions. All use the same fit/layout and support checks. This is distinct from the Brick Damage effect.
Rebar: Steel reinforcement.
Bricks: One connected brick layer held by the remaining solid.
Wood Planks: Boards with splintered broken ends.
Wood Framing: Timber stud frame behind a drywall skin: studs, plates, noggins, headers, joists and nails. The object is hollowed behind the skin around the breaks.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_brick_length:
Length of the bricks inside the wall.
Low: short bricks.
High: long bricks.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_brick_height:
Height of the bricks inside the wall.
Low: flat bricks.
High: tall blocks.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_brick_depth:
Chip depth as a share of the Edge Damage depth range (default 100 %).
Low (40 %): shallow chips.
High (250 %): deep chips.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_mortar:
Width of the mortar between the bricks.
Low: tight joints.
High: wide joints.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_missing:
Share of construction bricks omitted from the generated layout.
Minimum: Keep more of the original structure intact.
Maximum: Omit or break a larger share of eligible elements.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_brick_broken:
Share of construction bricks generated with broken ends.
Minimum: Keep more of the original structure intact.
Maximum: Omit or break a larger share of eligible elements.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_chamfer:
How much the edges of the bricks are cut off.
0: sharp-edged bricks.
High: worn, rounded-looking bricks.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_brick_jitter:
How much each brick is shifted and varied.
0: perfectly laid bricks.
High: crooked, uneven brickwork.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_plank_width:
Width of the boards inside the wall.
Low: narrow slats.
High: wide boards.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_plank_thickness:
Thickness of the boards inside the wall.
Low: thin slats.
High: thick planks.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_plank_gap:
Space between adjacent Boolean Planks boards.
Minimum: Small or closed gaps between neighbouring elements.
Maximum: Larger visible separation between neighbouring elements.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_plank_dir:
Choose horizontal boards or vertical staves. Vertical boards often reveal more with a horizontal cut.
Horizontal: Boards along the horizontal family.
Vertical: Vertical boards or staves.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_splinter:
How splintered the broken ends of the boards are.
0: clean sawn ends.
High: long torn splinters.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_stud_width:
Width of the upright timbers in the frame.
Low: slim timbers.
High: wide timbers.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_stud_depth:
How deep the upright timbers go into the wall.
Low: shallow battens.
High: deep beams.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_stud_spacing:
Distance between the upright timbers.
Low: timbers close together.
High: timbers far apart.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_joist_depth:
