Depth of the horizontal beams in the frame.
Low: slim beams.
High: deep beams.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_noggin_spacing:
Height between the short horizontal blocks that sit between the uprights.
Low: many rows of blocks.
High: few rows of blocks.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_double_plate:
Double the top plates and the headers over openings.
Off: omit double plate while keeping its stored settings.
On: use double plate with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_skin:
Thickness of the wall facing in front of the frame.
Low: a thin board skin.
High: a thick facing.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_cavity_reach:
How far the hollow space behind the facing opens up around the damage.
Low: the hollow shows only at the hole.
High: the hollow reaches far around the hole.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_paper_tear:
Tearing of the facing paper around the exposed frame.
Minimum: Earlier timing or a shorter allowed duration.
Maximum: Later timing or a longer allowed duration.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_paper_depth:
How deep the torn paper face of the board goes.
0: no torn paper.
High: a deep torn paper edge.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_nails:
How many nails are left sticking out of the frame.
0: no nails.
High: nails at every fixing point.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_nail_length:
Length of the nails that stick out.
Low: short stubs.
High: long nails.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_wood_broken:
Share of timber members snapped in the damaged region.
Minimum: Keep more of the original structure intact.
Maximum: Omit or break a larger share of eligible elements.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_facet_angle:
Angular threshold for splitting construction placement into separate surface facets.
Minimum: Rotate or tilt toward the lower end of the permitted angle range.
Maximum: Rotate or tilt toward the upper end; angles are not a damage-strength multiplier.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_mortar_joints:
Add recessed mortar attached to each Boolean-fill brick. Mortar is trimmed with broken bricks and has its own material slot; some joints are omitted for weathering.
Off: omit mortar joints while keeping its stored settings.
On: use mortar joints with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_mortar_recess:
How deep the mortar sits below the faces of the bricks.
0: joints flush with the bricks.
High: deep grooves between bricks.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_brick_3d:
Replace Boolean fill bricks with detailed library models, scaled and cut to each brick. Mortar is disabled. Dense models can slow Live Update.
Off: omit 3d bricks (experimental) while keeping its stored settings.
On: use 3d bricks (experimental) with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve that shows where the inner construction is needed. Draw close to the surface.
Empty: it is built around the damage automatically.
Assigned: it is built along your strokes.
ProjectDamageProps.surface_rebar_enable:
Enables reinforcement clipped to visible Concrete crater faces. Wood Knife does not generate this grid, even if the toggle remains stored.
Off: Off generates no surface reinforcement.
On: On exposes density, radius, deepness and material controls.
ProjectDamageProps.surface_rebar_amount:
Density of a ray-clipped reinforcement grid. Nominal pitch decreases with the square root of Amount, then is bounded by bar radius and internal sampling limits. Only Concrete craters with enough depth reveal the grid.
Minimum: Zero suppresses the bars.
Maximum: Larger values increase the available bar population within the generated damage.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.surface_rebar_radius:
Cross-section radius of generated reinforcement in centimetres, before effect scaling.
Minimum: A small positive radius makes thin bars.
Maximum: A larger radius makes thicker bars and needs enough exposed space.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.surface_rebar_cover:
Deepness under the original skin, in scaled centimetres. Effective deepness is at least the bar radius; the second grid family is offset by a little more than two radii.
Minimum: Zero puts it near the source skin.
Maximum: Larger deepness places it farther inside; shallow craters may no longer reveal it.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.surface_rebar_materia:
Material for the steel bars that show inside concrete craters.
Empty: the default steel material is used.
Assigned: the bars get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.boolean_quality:
Boolean cutter and fill geometry quality. Lower is faster; higher adds geometry. Does not change other effects.
Minimum: Coarse, faster Boolean cutter and fill geometry.
Maximum: Denser geometry for Boolean Break only, at higher cost.
Allowed range: 5% to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.boolean_frame_amount:
How dense the timber frame inside the wall is.
0: no frame.
High: uprights and blocks sit much closer together.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.boolean_pipe_scale:
Makes the pipes inside the wall bigger or smaller, with their spacing.
Low: thin pipes close together.
High: thick pipes far apart.
Allowed range: 1% to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.boolean_cable_scale:
Makes the cables inside the wall bigger or smaller, with their spacing.
Low: thin cables close together.
High: thick cables far apart.
Allowed range: 1% to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.boolean_plank_amount:
How many of the wooden boards are still there.
0: all boards are gone.
1: every board is present.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_surface_dist:
Warps the relief noise into flowing shapes without changing the patch outline (0 to 4, default 0).
Low (0): the plain noise.
High (3): twisted, streaky relief; the change is subtle.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_surface_roug:
Blend of broad ripples and fine aggregate pits (0 to 100 %, default 45 %).
Low (0 %): a smooth, wavy floor.
High (100 %): a pitted, gritty floor.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_surface_stre:
Multiplies the relief (0 to 400 %, default 100 %).
Low (0 %): a smooth floor; only the terraces remain.
High (300 %): a deeply pitted, broken floor.
Allowed range: 0% to 400%.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_proximity_amoun:
Number of cracks around the points. They are shared between all points.
0: no cracks at all.
High: a dense cluster of cracks around each point.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_placement:
Chooses where the tears come from
Procedural: tears all over the cloth from Interior Tears and Edge Tears
Draw: only the tears you draw, an empty drawing leaves the cloth intact
ProjectDamageProps.plaster_zone_group:
Vertex group that limits the relief. Weight 1 is full relief, 0 is none. Assign Selected and Weight Paint fill it
Empty: the whole mesh gets plaster
A group: plaster only where the weight is above 0
ProjectDamageProps.ground_axis_x:
World up direction for Ground Cracks. Several axes combine into a diagonal; at least one stays enabled.
Off: omit x while keeping its stored settings.
On: use x with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.ground_axis_y:
World up direction for Ground Cracks. Several axes combine into a diagonal; at least one stays enabled.
Off: omit y while keeping its stored settings.
On: use y with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.ground_axis_z:
World up direction for Ground Cracks. Several axes combine into a diagonal; at least one stays enabled.
Off: omit z while keeping its stored settings.
On: use z with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_brick_library:
A .blend file with your own brick models (objects named brick).
Empty: the built-in bricks are used.
Assigned: bricks are taken from your file.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_brick_collectio:
Use mesh objects from this collection and its child collections as custom bricks. Names do not matter. Originals stay untouched. Empty uses bundled brick models.
Empty: no collection input.
Assigned: read supported helper objects from that collection.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_preset:

Custom: Keep the fields as they are.

Double Wall: select this rebar defaults variant.
Column Cage: select this rebar defaults variant.
Round Column: select this rebar defaults variant.

Twisted Square: select this rebar defaults variant.
Prestress Strands: select this rebar defaults variant.

ProjectDamageProps.rebar_material:
Material for the steel bars inside the wall.
Empty: the default steel material is used.
Assigned: the bars get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_axes_bits:
Set rebar_axes_bits for this generated feature.
Minimum: First entry or lowest enabled-axis bit pattern.
Maximum: Later entry or combined enabled-axis bits; this is a selector, not an intensity.
Allowed range: 0 to 7.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_axis_auto:
Grid: the thinnest side is the wall normal. Cage: the longest side is the column axis. Off: pick one or more axes by hand.
Off: omit auto while keeping its stored settings.
On: use auto with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_axes:
The axes that get a layout.
X: select this axes variant.
Y: select this axes variant.
Z: select this axes variant.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_axis_x:
A layout for the X axis (several axes can be on).
Off: omit x while keeping its stored settings.
On: use x with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_axis_y:
A layout for the Y axis (several axes can be on).
Off: omit y while keeping its stored settings.
On: use y with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_axis_z:
A layout for the Z axis (several axes can be on).
Off: omit z while keeping its stored settings.
On: use z with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_cable_material:
Turns the cables on or off.

On: cables loop out of the rim.
ProjectDamageProps.plaster_master_scale:
Scales all sizes of the plaster at once: strokes, ridges, grain and cracks.
Low: small, fine strokes, like a smooth finish.
High: large, coarse strokes.
Allowed range: 0.01% to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.one_material_all:
Show one material input for all generators; nothing changes until Apply.
Off: omit add one material to all while keeping its stored settings.
On: use add one material to all with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.all_generators_materi:
One material to give to every Project Damage generator on the selected objects.
Empty: every generator keeps its own material.
Assigned: all generators use this material.

Remembers the last shared material that was applied. The addon fills it in for you.
Empty: no shared material has been applied.
Assigned: this material is in use for all generators.

ProjectDamageProps.fracture_l1_material:

ProjectDamageProps.fracture_l2_material:

ProjectDamageProps.fracture_l3_material:

ProjectDamageProps.surface_damage_materi:

ProjectDamageProps.buildup_material:

ProjectDamageProps.boolean_break_materia:

ProjectDamageProps.erosion_material:

ProjectDamageProps.rebar_brick_material:
Material for the bricks inside the wall.

ProjectDamageProps.rebar_plank_material:
Material for the boards inside the wall.

ProjectDamageProps.rebar_framing_materia:

ProjectDamageProps.rebar_nail_material:
Material for the nails in the frame.
Empty: the default metal material is kept.
Assigned: the nails get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.bevel_material:
Material for the worn, cut-off edges.

ProjectDamageProps.wear_material:
Material for worn areas.

ProjectDamageProps.scratch_groove_materi:
Material inside the scratch grooves.

ProjectDamageProps.scratch_scuff_materia:
Material for the scuffed area around scratches.
Empty: the default damage material is kept.
Assigned: scuffs get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.heat_char_material:
Material for charred, burnt areas.
Empty: the default material is kept.
Assigned: burnt areas get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.rebar_mortar_material:
Material for the mortar between the bricks inside the wall.

ProjectDamageProps.coating_shell_materia:

ProjectDamageProps.brick_front_material:

Empty: the default brick material is kept.
Assigned: brick faces get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.brick_break_material:
Material for broken bricks.
Empty: the default material is kept.
Assigned: broken brick faces get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.brick_seam_material:
Material for the mortar joints between bricks.
Empty: the default mortar material is kept.
Assigned: the joints get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.brick_behind_material:
Material for what shows behind the bricks.
Empty: the default material is kept.
Assigned: the area behind the bricks gets this material.
ProjectDamageProps.brick_render_material:
Material for the broken edge of the plaster layer.
Empty: the default plaster material is kept.
Assigned: the plaster break gets this material.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_material:
Material for the wooden laths behind the plaster.
Empty: the default wood material is kept.
Assigned: the laths get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.debris_material:
Material for the loose chunks.
Empty: chunks keep the material of the place they came from.
Assigned: all chunks get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.rbf_inner_material:
Material for the new inside faces of broken pieces.
Empty: the default material is kept.
Assigned: the inside faces get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_inner_material:
Material for the new inside faces of broken pieces. Outside faces keep their own material.
Empty: the default material is kept.
Assigned: the inside faces get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.surface_secondary_mat:
Material for the small extra damage around the rim of a crater.
Empty: the same material as the crater is used.
Assigned: the rim damage gets this material.
ProjectDamageProps.pile_material: The material of the piles. It has no effect on the shape, so there is no image.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_rebar_materi:
Material for the steel bars shown in broken concrete.
Empty: the default steel material is used.
Assigned: the bars get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_cavity_smooth:
Smooths the cut floor behind the laths, not the plaster rim (0 to 1, default 0.6). Removes one-cell spikes between the laths.
Low (0): the original, spiky floor.
High (1): a smooth floor.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_rim_smooth:
Smooths grid-scale jaggedness on the plaster and hole walls (0 to 1, default 0.5). Walls still read as sheer.
Low (0): stair-stepped walls.
High (1): cleaner walls; very fine features soften.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_lath_optimize:
Drops lath cross-sections that its neighbours already describe within a tolerance (0 to 1, default 0.5). Fewer polygons on straight runs; warps, bends and splinters above the tolerance stay. It changes the polygon count, not the look, so there is no image.
Low (0): every section kept.
High (1): the lightest mesh.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_wall_slope:
Largest steepness of the broken walls, in degrees from the surface (default 72; 0 or 90 = off). The outline on the surface stays.
Low (30°): wide, gentle walls.
High (90°, off): sheer walls.
Allowed range: 0 to 90.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_cavity_slope:
Largest slope of the floor behind the laths, in degrees (default 40; 0 or 90 = off). The images use Keys 0.6.
Low (15°): low, rounded keys.
High (90°, off): steep, lumpy keys.
Allowed range: 0 to 90.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_hole_noise_scale:
Feature size of the hole outline noise, times the patch size (default 0.3). The images use Hole Size 0.7 with the laths off, so the hole outline shows.
Low (0.1): small notches.
High (1): broad lobes.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_hole_detail:
Weight of the finer octaves of the hole outline (0 to 1, default 0.35). Same images setup.
Low (0): one smooth octave.
High (1): a more ragged outline.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_riven_wave:
How much the laths wave up and down, as a share of their width.
0: straight sawn laths.
High (2): strongly wavy, hand-split laths.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_riven_wave_lengt:
Length of one wave along a lath.
Low: short, crooked wiggles.
High: long, lazy bends.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_riven_width_var:
How much the width changes from lath to lath and along each one.
0: evenly sawn widths.
1: very uneven hand-split widths.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_riven_twist:
The most a lath is twisted along its length, in degrees.
0: flat laths.
High (30): clearly twisted laths.
Allowed range: 0 to 30.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_riven_rough:
How rough the hand-split laths look: uneven corners and a bumpy face.
0: clean rectangular boards.
1: rough, wedge-shaped split boards.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_stud_enable:
Vertical studs behind the laths, seen through the gaps and holes; they go into the separate lath object.
Off: omit studs while keeping its stored settings.
On: use studs with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_stud_spacing:
Distance between the upright timbers behind the laths.
Low: timbers close together.
High: timbers far apart.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_stud_width:
Width of the upright timbers.
Low: slim timbers.
High: wide timbers.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_stud_depth:
How deep the upright timbers go into the wall. They are left out where the wall is too thin.
Low: shallow battens.
High: deep beams.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_board_studs:
Length of one lath, counted in gaps between uprights.
0: endless laths without joints.
High (64): very long laths with rare joints.
Allowed range: 0 to 64.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_joint_bundle:
Rows that break on the same stud before the joint line steps to the next one.
Minimum: Neighbouring rows step their joints more frequently.
Maximum: More rows share one supporting stud before the joint line steps.
Allowed range: 0 to 1000.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_lath_hang:
Chance that a snapped lath held by one nail swings down over a hole.
0: broken laths stay in place.
1: every such lath hangs down.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_noggin_spacing:
Height between the short horizontal blocks that sit between the uprights.
0: no blocks.
High: only a few rows of blocks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_frame_plates:
Bottom and top plates where the damage reaches the lowest / highest point of the object.
Off: omit top and bottom plates while keeping its stored settings.
On: use top and bottom plates with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_double_plate:
Doubled top plate, as in platform framing.
Off: omit double top plate while keeping its stored settings.
On: use double top plate with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_nail_amount:
Chance that a nail is left standing where the laths came off.
0: no nails.
1: a nail at every fixing point.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_nail_length:
How far the nails stick out of the frame.
0: nails are flush.
High (10): long nails sticking far out.
Allowed range: 0 to 10.
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_solid_bevel:
Fabric Solidify only. Rounds the torn rim of every hole on both faces of the cloth
0: sharp, knife-cut rim edges
1: a fully round rim, half the cloth thickness
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_solid_bevel_se:
Fabric Solidify only. Smoothness of the rounded rim, rings per quarter circle
1: a single chamfer
High: a smooth round rim, heavier mesh
Allowed range: 1 to 12.
ProjectDamageProps.fissure_master_scale:
Scales every fissure size (width, depth, slabs, branches) on top of the global Master Scale (1 to 400%, default 20%). Lower it for small objects.
Low (10%): a narrow crack with small slabs.
High (40%): a wide chasm with large, heavy slabs.
Allowed range: 1% to 400%.
ProjectDamageProps.break_variant:
What sits inside the break. All types share the breakers; switching keeps every setting.
Simple: The cut alone: nothing inside the break.
Rebar: Steel bars exposed in the break.
Bricks: A brick layer behind the surface, revealed by the break.
Planks: Wooden boards behind the surface, splintered where broken.
Framing: A timber stud frame behind a drywall skin.
Pipes: Hollow pipes in the wall, bent and broken at the edge of the break.
Cables: Electrical cables in the wall, sagging, torn and hanging out of the break.
ProjectDamageProps.break_objects:
A collection of objects that cut this object, like the Boolean modifier with a collection.
Empty: no collection cuts the object.
Assigned: every mesh in the collection is carved out.
ProjectDamageProps.break_separate:
Every loose part the breakers cut off becomes its own object (origin at its centre of mass, no parent); the main body stays the result. Apply All turns them into ordinary objects.
Off: omit separate fragments while keeping its stored settings.
On: use separate fragments with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.break_separate_min:
Loose parts smaller than this stay attached to the main body instead of becoming separate objects.
0: every loose part becomes its own object.
High: only big parts are separated.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_damage_enable:
Concrete Damage chased along pipes in the wall: the spalls uncover hollow pipes instead of rebar. Shares the Concrete Damage shape, crack and hole settings.
Off: omit pipe damage while keeping its stored settings.
On: use pipe damage with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_break_enable:
internal: Boolean Break type Pipes.
Off: omit pipe break enable while keeping its stored settings.
On: use pipe break enable with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_type:
Material and behaviour of the pipes. Choosing a type also sets its usual diameter, wall and joint spacing. PVC (5 cm): brittle, snaps into a jagged shard edge. Copper (2.2 cm, default): thin, bends easily, torn and squashed ends. Steel (3.4 cm): galvanised, threaded couplings, stiff. Cast Iron (10 cm): thick soil pipe with socket hubs, ragged breaks. Conduit (2.5 cm): corrugated, with wires inside, sags and tears.
The images show the five types in the same chase.
Cast Iron is wider than the chase, so only its hubs and a broken end show.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_material:
Material for the pipes.
Empty: a built-in material that suits the pipe type is used.
Assigned: the pipes get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_layout:
Direction of the runs: Horizontal, Vertical or Both (default).
Horizontal: runs along the stroke.
Vertical: risers crossing the stroke; only short pieces show in the chase.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_count:
Runs per direction (1 to 40, default 2).
Low (1): one run.
High (5): several runs and risers.
Allowed range: 1 to 40.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_bundle:
Pipes laid side by side in one run, like hot and cold water (1 to 6, default 2).
Low (1): single pipes.
High (4): bundles of four.
Allowed range: 1 to 6.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_bundle_gap:
Space between the pipes of one run (default 1.5 cm).
Low (0.5 cm): pipes almost touching.
High (5 cm): pipes spread across the chase.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_diameter:
Outer diameter of a pipe (default 2.2 cm for Copper).
Low (1.2 cm): thin tubes.
High (5 cm): large pipes filling the chase.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_wall:
Wall thickness of the hollow pipe, seen at a broken end (default 0.1 cm). It shows only at the open ends; the close-up looks at the broken ends on the left.
Low (0.05 cm): a thin rim.
High (0.5 cm): a thick rim at the broken end.
Allowed range: 0.005 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_cover:
Concrete in front of the pipes (default 1.5 cm). The chase is cut deeper with it.
Low (0.5 cm): pipes right under the surface.
High (5 cm): a deep chase.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_axis:
Choose Wall Normal. Auto: The thinnest side of the object is the wall normal; X; Y; Z.
Auto: The thinnest side of the object is the wall normal.
X: select this wall normal variant.
Y: select this wall normal variant.
Z: select this wall normal variant.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_side:
Which face the pipes run behind.
+ Face: Just behind the face on the positive side of the axis.
- Face: Just behind the face on the negative side of the axis.
Centre: In the middle of the wall.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_seed:
The Concrete Damage seed: changes the outline and the cracks of the chase, not the pipes.
Every number gives another outline.
There is no low or high.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_elbows:
Chance that a run turns 90 degrees with an elbow (0 to 1, default 0.3).
Low (0): straight runs.
High (1): every run turns.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_joint_spacing:
Joint Spacing: couplings, sockets or hubs along the pipe, in cm (default 80; 0 = no joints). The joints are small next to the chase.
Low (0): plain pipes.
High (20 cm): a joint every 20 cm.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_embed:
How far a pipe piece continues into the concrete that holds it (default 6 cm). The images use Broken 1.
Low (0): nothing holds the snapped pieces, and they fall out of the chase.
High (20 cm): the pieces are held and stay in the chase.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_broken:
Chance that a pipe crossing the damage is snapped, with a gap (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): whole pipes.
High (1): every pipe is snapped.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_bend:
How far broken and free ends bend out of the hole, starting at its edge (0 to 1, default 0.5). The images use Broken 1.
Low (0): the ends stay in line.
High (1): the ends bend out toward the viewer.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_jagged:
How ragged the broken end is (0 to 1, default 0.6). The images use Broken 1, in close-up.
Low (0): a clean cut.
High (1): a slightly torn rim; small at this distance.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_dent:
Squashed spots on metal pipes and flattened broken ends (0 to 1, default 0.4).
Low (0): round pipes.
High (1): a few squashed spots; small at this distance.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_bow:
Pipes spanning the damage bow outward; conduit also sags (0 to 1, default 0.3). The images use Broken 0.
Low (0): straight pipes.
High (1): the pipes bow out a little; in a 6 cm chase the change is small.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_wires:
Wires inside the pipe that hang out of broken ends (off by default; on for Conduit). The images use Broken 1, in close-up.
Off: empty pipes.
On: a bunch of wires sags out of the broken end.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_wire_count:
Number of wires inside each pipe.
Low (1): a single wire.
High (5): a bundle of five wires.
Allowed range: 1 to 5.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_sides:
Segments round the pipe (Sides, 6 to 48, default 16).
Low (6): faceted pipes.
High (32): round pipes, more polygons.
Allowed range: 6 to 48.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_chase_amount:
Runs per direction (1 to 40, default 2).
Low (1): one run.
High (5): several runs and risers.
Allowed range: 0 to 200.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_chase_length_min:
Shortest damaged stretch along a pipe.
Low: some damaged spots are very short.
High: even the shortest damaged stretch is long.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_chase_length_max:
Longest damaged stretch along a pipe.
Low: all damaged spots stay short.
High: some stretches of wall are opened for a long way.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_chase_width:
Width of the wall damage around the pipes, compared with the width of the pipe run.
Low (0.5): a tight slot that barely shows the pipes.
High: a wide broken channel.
Allowed range: 0.5 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_chase_dig:
How deep the damage goes past the cover, as a share of the pipe diameter (default 0.9; 1 uncovers the whole front half).
Low (0.3): the pipes barely break the floor of the chase.
High (2): a deep chase; the pipes lie free in it.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_axes_bits:
Set pipe_axes_bits for this generated feature.
Minimum: First entry or lowest enabled-axis bit pattern.
Maximum: Later entry or combined enabled-axis bits; this is a selector, not an intensity.
Allowed range: 0 to 7.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_axis_auto:
Pick the wall normal by itself (each break or painted area takes its own face). Off: choose the axes.
Off: omit auto while keeping its stored settings.
On: use auto with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_axes:
The axes whose faces get runs.
X: Faces across X.
Y: Faces across Y.
Z: Faces across Z.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_axis_x:
Runs behind the faces across X (click to turn on or off; several can be on).
Off: omit x while keeping its stored settings.
On: use x with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_axis_y:
Runs behind the faces across Y (click to turn on or off; several can be on).
Off: omit y while keeping its stored settings.
On: use y with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_axis_z:
Runs behind the faces across Z (click to turn on or off; several can be on).
Off: omit z while keeping its stored settings.
On: use z with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.pipe_spawn_center:
Placement Logic fold: off follows each painted face; on places the pipes in the middle of the wall.
Off: the pipes lie just behind the painted face.
On: in the middle of the 20 cm wall the chase does not reach them, and no pipes show.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_damage_enable:
Concrete Damage chased along electrical cables in the wall: the spalls uncover cables that sag and hang out of the holes. Shares the Concrete Damage shape, crack and hole settings.
Off: omit cable damage while keeping its stored settings.
On: use cable damage with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_break_enable:
internal: Boolean Break type Cables.
Off: omit cable break enable while keeping its stored settings.
On: use cable break enable with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_type:
Kind of cable; choosing a type also sets its usual diameter, stiffness and strip length. Round Sheathed (default): grey or white cable with three cores. Twin & Earth: flat grey cable, brown and blue cores with a bare earth. Single Wires: loose insulated wires, no sheath. Armored: spiral metal sheath, stiff, ragged metal at a cut. Data: thin blue network cable with four cores.
The images show the five types in close-up.
Single Wires and Data show their coloured cores.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_material:
Material for the outer sheath of the cables.
Empty: a built-in material that suits the cable type is used.
Assigned: the cables get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_layout:
Direction of the runs: Horizontal, Vertical or Both (default).
Horizontal: cables along the stroke only.
Vertical: risers crossing the stroke hang out in long loops.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_count:
Runs per direction (1 to 40, default 2).
Low (1): one run of cables.
High (5): many cables hang from the chase.
Allowed range: 1 to 40.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_bundle:
Cables laid side by side in one run (1 to 12, default 3).
Low (1): single cables.
High (6): thick bundles.
Allowed range: 1 to 12.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_bundle_gap:
Space between the cables of one run (default 3 cm).
Low (0.5 cm): cables together.
High (8 cm): cables spread out.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_diameter:
Outer diameter of a cable, the width of a flat cable (default 1.1 cm).
Low (0.5 cm): thin cables.
High (2.5 cm): thick cables.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_cover:
Plaster or concrete in front of the cables (default 1 cm).
Low (0.3 cm): cables right under the surface.
High (4 cm): a deep chase, fewer loose cables.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_axis:
Choose Wall Normal. Auto: The thinnest side of the object is the wall normal; X; Y; Z.
Auto: The thinnest side of the object is the wall normal.
X: select this wall normal variant.
Y: select this wall normal variant.
Z: select this wall normal variant.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_axes_bits:
Set cable_axes_bits for this generated feature.
Minimum: First entry or lowest enabled-axis bit pattern.
Maximum: Later entry or combined enabled-axis bits; this is a selector, not an intensity.
Allowed range: 0 to 7.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_axis_auto: Placement Logic fold: find the wall normal and the face for every area by itself (on by default). Off: pick the axes by hand. No image.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_axes:
The wall normals the cables are laid for.
X: select this axes variant.
Y: select this axes variant.
Z: select this axes variant.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_axis_x:
Local-space X component of axis. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Off: omit x while keeping its stored settings.
On: use x with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_axis_y:
Local-space Y component of axis. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Off: omit y while keeping its stored settings.
On: use y with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_axis_z:
Local-space Z component of axis. Set all three components together to define a nonzero direction.
Off: omit z while keeping its stored settings.
On: use z with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_side:
Which face the cables run behind: Auto (walls: the + face; slabs and ceilings: the face that points down), + Face, - Face or Centre. With painted damage every area uses the face it was painted on, so Side made no visible difference in our test (no image); it matters for Boolean Break Cables.
Auto, + Face and - Face: the cables run behind the painted face.
Centre: the same result here, because the painted face wins.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_seed:
The cable seed: changes the layout of the runs.
Every number gives another layout.
There is no low or high.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_turns:
Chance that a run turns 90 degrees (0 to 1, default 0.3).
Low (0): straight runs.
High (1): every run turns.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_embed:
How far a cable piece continues into the wall that holds it (default 6 cm).
Low (0): short pieces where a cable leaves the wall.
High (20 cm): longer pieces held in the wall. With Hanging Always the result looked the same from the front, so there is no image.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_cut:
Chance that a cable crossing the damage is torn through (0 to 1, default 0.4). With Hanging Always the loose cables hang down either way, so the change is small here.
Low (0): whole cables, hanging as loops.
High (1): torn cables with stripped ends.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_slack:
Loose cable pulled out of the wall, as a share of the hole width (default 0.15). The images use Cut 0 and Hanging Off.
Low (0): the cables stay tight in the chase.
High (0.6): the cables bulge far out of the chase.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_stiffness:
Soft cables follow gravity in a smooth curve; stiff ones keep straighter (0 to 1, default 0.45; the type sets its usual value). The images use Cut 1.
Low (0): limp cables hanging straight down.
High (1): slightly wider arcs; with Hanging Always the change is small.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_strip:
Sheath stripped back at a cut end, showing the cores (default 4 cm).
Low (1 cm): short bare cores.
High (10 cm): long cores out of the sheath.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_splay:
How far the cores fan out of a cut end (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): the cores stay together.
High (1): the cores spread a little; small at this size.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_fray:
Torn, ragged edge where the sheath ends (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): a clean sheath edge.
High (1): a ragged sheath edge; small at this size.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_sides:
Segments round a cable (Sides, 5 to 32, default 10).
Low (5): faceted cables.
High (24): round cables.
Allowed range: 5 to 32.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_hang:
Off: loose cables sag and droop, torn ends stay short. Horizontal: on horizontal surfaces (a ceiling, a hole through a slab) the loose cables hang down out of the hole. Always (default): loose cables hang out of every hole, on walls too.
Off: short droops in the chase.
Horizontal: on a wall, the same as Off. Always: long loops and ends hang down the wall.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_hang_length:
How far the cables hang below the hole (default 35 cm).
Low (10 cm): short loops.
High (80 cm): cables hang far down.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_hang_ends:
Share of the hanging cables that are torn through and dangle as loose ends; the others hang as loops (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): only loops.
High (1): only dangling ends.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_hang_sway:
Hanging cables drift sideways a little, each its own way (0 to 1, default 0.3).
Low (0): straight down.
High (1): the cables swing out to the sides.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_hang_tilt:
How tilted a surface may be and still count as a ceiling or floor.
Low (0): only perfectly level surfaces.
High (89): almost any slope counts.
Allowed range: 0 degrees to 89 degrees.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_chase_amount:
Runs per direction (1 to 40, default 2).
Low (1): one run of cables.
High (5): many cables hang from the chase.
Allowed range: 0 to 200.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_chase_length_mi:
Shortest damaged stretch along a cable.
Low: some damaged spots are very short.
High: even the shortest damaged stretch is long.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_chase_length_ma:
Longest damaged stretch along a cable.
Low: all damaged spots stay short.
High: some stretches of wall are opened for a long way.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_chase_width:
Width of the wall damage around the cables, compared with the width of the cable run.
Low (0.5): a tight slot that barely shows the cables.
High: a wide broken channel.
Allowed range: 0.5 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.cable_chase_dig:
How deep the damage goes past the cover, as a share of the cable diameter (default 1.2). Above 0.5 the cables come loose.
Low (0.3): the cables stay in the wall; only a short loop shows.
High (2.5): a deep chase; all cables are free and hang down.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_enable:
Small pores, chipped dents and flaked-off cement skin displaced into the surface, before any other damage is cut.
Off: omit concrete pitting while keeping its stored settings.
On: use concrete pitting with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_seed:
Shuffles the pores, flakes and dents without changing their size or amount.
Every number gives a different random arrangement.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_group:
Vertex group painting where the pitting goes (1 = full, 0 = none). Empty = the whole object.
Empty: no vertex-group restriction.
Assigned: use the named group weights on this object.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_zone_feather:
Weights below this fade the relief out softly.
Minimum: A harder transition at low mask weights.
Maximum: A wider smooth fade in the pitting relief near low-weight mask areas.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_avoid:
No pitting on the Avoid faces.
Off: omit avoid selection while keeping its stored settings.
On: use avoid selection with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_strength:
Makes every pore, flake and dent deeper or shallower at once.
0: a flat surface, nothing is pressed in.
High: everything is much deeper.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_thickness_cap:
Limit inward pitting to a fraction of the local wall thickness.
Minimum (0): disable this cap.
Maximum (1): permit depth up to the available wall thickness; other limits still apply.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_edge_length:
Target edge length over the concrete-pitting zone.
Minimum: dense geometry for grain, dents and waviness.
Maximum: coarser, faster geometry with less small relief.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_fine_edge:
Smallest target edge inside pores and flaked patches.
Minimum: resolve smaller pores with more triangles.
Maximum: small pores are left to the baked map instead of geometric holes.
Allowed range: 0.005 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_detail:
Resolution multiplier for pitting: 2 halves the target edge lengths.
Minimum: coarse, fast pitting geometry.
Maximum: finer topology, limited by Max Triangles.
Allowed range: 0.05 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_max_tris:
Triangle budget; the edges grow to fit it on big objects.
Minimum: A strict limit: less generated detail or fewer elements, with lower processing cost.
Maximum: Allow more geometry or elements; updates and memory use can increase.
Allowed range: 10000 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_pore_density:
How many small pores there are on each 10 by 10 cm.
0: no pores.
High: the surface is full of pores.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_pore_size_min:
Smallest pore, in cm.
Low: some pores are pin-pricks.
High: even the smallest pore is clearly visible.
Allowed range: 0.005 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_pore_size_max:
Largest pore, in cm.
Low: all pores stay small.
High: some pores are big holes.
Allowed range: 0.005 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_pore_small_bias:
Bias the pore-size distribution toward the minimum diameter.
Minimum (0): sizes span the range evenly.
Maximum (1): almost all pores are small.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_pore_depth:
How deep a pore is, compared with its width.
0: flat marks.
High (2): deep narrow holes.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_pore_sharp:
Shape of the pore wall and floor.
Minimum (0): soft rounded bowls.
Maximum (1): steep walls and a flatter floor.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_pore_jagged:
How irregular the outline of a pore is.
0: round pores.
High (1.5): ragged, lobed pores.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.5.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_pore_stretch:
Elongation (1 = up to 2.5 : 1).
Minimum: Rounder pores.
Maximum: More elongated pores, up to the supported aspect ratio.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_pore_rim:
Chipped ring around the opening of a pore.
0: a clean opening.
High (2): a wide chipped rim.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_pore_merge:
Share of pores that are really two to four holes run together.
0: every pore is single.
1: all pores are merged groups.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_clustering:
Concentrate pores into bands and patches.
Minimum (0): an even scatter.
Maximum (1): strongly clustered pores with more empty space between gatherings.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_cluster_scale:
Size of the areas where pores gather, in cm.
Low: many small groups.
High: a few large groups.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_flake_enable:
Patches where the cement skin has chipped off down to the sand.
Off: omit flaking while keeping its stored settings.
On: use flaking with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_flake_coverage:
How much of the surface has lost its outer skin.
0: the skin is whole.
1: the skin is gone everywhere.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_flake_scale:
Size of the patches where the skin came off, in cm.
Low: small scabs.
High: large bare patches.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_flake_depth:
Depth of the deepest part of a flaked patch, in cm.
0: no depth.
High: deep patches.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_flake_layers:
Number of steps the skin broke off in.
Low (1): one single step.
High (4): a staircase of four ledges.
Allowed range: 1 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_flake_jagged:
How ragged the outline of a flaked patch is.
0: smooth outlines.
High (2): torn, crumbly outlines.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_flake_rough:
How gritty the floor of a flaked patch is, with sand and small stones.
0: a smooth floor.
High (2): a very rough, stony floor.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_aggregate_size:
Size of the sand grains and small stones on that floor, in cm.
Low: fine sand.
High: coarse gravel.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_flake_pores:
Extra pores inside a flaked patch (x Pores).
Minimum: No extra pores inside the flaked patches.
Maximum: More additional pores within the flaked floor.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_dent_density:
How many shallow dents there are on each 10 by 10 cm.
0: no dents.
High: a hammered-looking surface.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_dent_size_min:
Smallest dent, in cm.
Low: some dents are tiny.
High: even the smallest dent is wide.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_dent_size_max:
Largest dent, in cm.
Low: all dents stay small.
High: some dents are wide.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_dent_depth:
How deep a dent is, compared with its width.
0: no depth.
High (0.5): deep bowl-shaped dents.
Allowed range: 0 to 0.5.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_dent_chip:
Asymmetry of a shallow dent.
Minimum (0): a soft round dish.
Maximum (1): one side breaks off steeply.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_grain:
Height of the fine sandy roughness, in cm.
0: no fine roughness.
High: a coarse sandpaper surface.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_grain_size:
Size of the grains in that roughness, in cm. It fades out where the mesh is too coarse to show it.
Low: very fine grain.
High: bigger bumps.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_undulation:
Height of the broad, gentle waves in the surface, in cm.
0: a flat surface.
High: a clearly uneven, wavy surface.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_undulation_scale:
Length of those gentle waves, in cm.
Low: short ripples.
High: long swells.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_bake_tile:
Width of the area that one baked image covers, in cm.
Low: a small area with very fine detail.
High: a large area with softer detail.
Allowed range: 1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_bake_res:
Pixels across the tile.
1024: select this resolution variant.
2048: select this resolution variant.
4096: select this resolution variant.
8192: select this resolution variant.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_bake_flakes:
Bake the flaked patches too. Off by default: they are the biggest features and the first to make a repeat noticeable.
Off: omit include flaking while keeping its stored settings.
On: use include flaking with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.pits_bake_dir:
Folder where the baked images are saved.
Empty: the default folder is used.
Assigned: images are saved into this folder.
ProjectDamageProps.foam_enable:
Enable this feature for the current source. Disable to omit it without losing its stored settings.
Off: omit expanding foam while keeping its stored settings.
On: use expanding foam with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.weld_enable:
Enable this feature for the current source. Disable to omit it without losing its stored settings.
Off: omit welded edges while keeping its stored settings.
On: use welded edges with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.weld_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve that gives the path of the weld seam. Draw close to the surface.
Empty: the weld is placed automatically.
Assigned: the weld follows your strokes.
ProjectDamageProps.grass_enable:
Enable this feature for the current source. Disable to omit it without losing its stored settings.
Off: omit grass scatter while keeping its stored settings.
On: use grass scatter with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.grass_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve that shows where grass grows. Draw close to the surface.
Empty: grass is placed automatically.
Assigned: grass grows along your strokes.
ProjectDamageProps.gravel_enable:
Enable this feature for the current source. Disable to omit it without losing its stored settings.
Off: omit gravel scatter while keeping its stored settings.
On: use gravel scatter with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.gravel_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve that shows where gravel lies. Draw close to the surface.
Empty: gravel is placed automatically.
Assigned: gravel is scattered along your strokes.
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_tear_style:
Shape family of the procedural tears
Classic: ragged lens-shaped holes that can split into several holes with fabric bridges between them
Realistic: tears that follow the weave, with stepped rims and a fringe along the yarns
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_tear_rip:
Realistic only. Share of rips: straight tears along one yarn, opened by the pulled edges. Only the ratio of the four tear types matters
0: no rips
1: mostly rips
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_tear_corner:
Realistic only. Share of corner (L) tears: a snag on a nail, two legs along warp and weft with a folded flap
0: no corner tears
1: mostly corner tears
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_tear_worn:
Realistic only. Share of worn holes: squarish worn areas (knees, elbows) with yarns still spanning them
0: no worn holes
1: mostly worn holes
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_tear_puncture:
Realistic only. Share of punctures: small holes with short slits along the grain
0: no punctures
1: mostly punctures
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_grain_snap:
Share of tears that run exactly along the warp or the weft. The rest are bias tears at any angle.
Low (0): tears at random angles.
High (1): every tear runs along or across the weave.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_yarn_size:
Width of a yarn bundle, the step size of the torn rim. Smaller is finer and slower.
Low: a finely stepped rim, like thin shirt fabric.
High: a coarse stepped rim, like canvas or burlap.
Allowed range: 0.02 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_flap_lift:
How far the flap of a corner tear is folded back out of the hole.
Low (0): the flap lies in place, the tear is a thin L-shaped line.
High (1): the flap is folded right over and the hole is open.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_tear_preset:
Loads the shape, mix and sizes of a typical cloth look. Edit the values afterwards as you like; Custom keeps your current values.
Old Jeans, Snagged Shirt, Ripped Canvas: from a few worn holes to long rips.
Moth-Eaten, Shredded Rag, Classic Lenses: from many small holes to heavy shredding (second image).
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_surface_deta:
Octaves of the relief noise (1 to 8, default 3). Each octave adds finer grain.
Low (1): soft, large ripples.
High (8): more fine grain on top; the change from 3 is small.
Allowed range: 1 to 8.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_noise_scale:
Size of the wall noise, times the hole size (default 100 %).
Low (40 %): small, busy lumps.
High (300 %): broad, smooth bulges.
Allowed range: 5% to 2000%.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_noise_detail:
Octaves of the noise (1 to 8, default 2).
Low (1): soft lumps only.
High (6): extra fine grain on the lumps.
Allowed range: 1 to 8.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_noise_roughness:
How strong each finer octave is compared with the one before (0 to 0.95, default 0.5). The images use Detail 5.
Low (0.2): the fine octaves almost vanish.
High (0.9): sharp, jagged walls.
Allowed range: 0 to 0.95.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_noise_distortion:
Twists the noise into flowing, less regular shapes (0 to 4, default 0).
Low (0): the plain noise.
High (3): streaky, twisted walls.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_noise_strength:
Depth of the wall noise, times Roughness (default 100 %).
Low (0 %): smooth walls.
High (300 %): deep lumps and ledges.
Allowed range: 0% to 1000%.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_noise_scale:
Size of the noise features (default 10 cm).
Low (2 cm): busy, fine lumps.
High (40 cm): broad, smooth swells.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_noise_detail:
Octaves of the noise (1 to 8, default 4). The change is small.
Low (1): soft lumps only.
High (8): a little more fine grain.
Allowed range: 1 to 8.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_noise_roughness:
How strong each finer octave is compared with the one before (0 to 0.95, default 0.5).
Low (0.2): smooth lumps.
High (0.9): jagged, broken relief.
Allowed range: 0 to 0.95.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_noise_distortion:
Twists the noise into flowing, less regular shapes (0 to 4, default 0).
Low (0): the plain noise.
High (3): twisted, streaky lumps.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.lath_noise_strength:
Peak-to-peak depth of the noise (default 0).
Low (0): the plain cavity.
High (4 cm): a rough, lumpy cavity floor and rim.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.brick_noise_scale:
Size of the noise features (default 10 cm).
Low (3 cm): fine, busy relief.
High (30 cm): broad swells.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.brick_noise_detail:
Octaves of the noise (1 to 8, default 4).
Low (1): soft lumps.
High (8): fine grain on top.
Allowed range: 1 to 8.
ProjectDamageProps.brick_noise_roughness:
Uneven floor on the render (default 0.3). In our Carved close-ups the change was too small to see, so there is no image.
Low (0): a smooth floor.
High (1.5): a bumpy floor.
Allowed range: 0 to 0.95.
ProjectDamageProps.brick_noise_distortio:
Twists the noise into flowing, less regular shapes (0 to 4, default 0). The images were made with Brick Damage and its Back Surface Strength of 2 cm; the noise is the same here.
Low (0): the plain noise.
High (3): twisted relief.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageProps.brick_noise_strength:
Peak-to-peak depth of the noise (default 2 cm here; 0 = the surface as built).
Low (0): a flat back.
High (6 cm): a deeply broken back.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.rusty_master_scale:
Scales hole sizes, crack widths, sheet thickness and drawing distances together, in percent (default 100).
Low (50%): the same layout with clusters half the size.
High (200%): clusters twice the size; neighbouring holes start to merge.
Allowed range: 1% to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.split_effect_zones:
Duplicate boundary vertices so damage groups select exact zones. Geometry stays in place; modifiers may open the seams.
Off: omit split effect zones while keeping its stored settings.
On: use split effect zones with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.hang_master_scale:
Multiplies the opening size range (default 100 %).
Low (50 %): a small hole.
High (200 %): a large hole with a long span of bars.
Allowed range: 1% to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.glass_master_scale:
Scales the openings, cracks, chips and drawing widths together, in percent (default 100). The image uses two hits on the whole pane.
Low (50%): small openings with short cracks.
High (200%): openings twice as large; the cracks reach far over the pane.
Allowed range: 1% to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.brick_back_resolution:
Density of the cutter grid (default 0.5 for this asset). The brick edges are always exact; it changes the render rim and the pocket.
Low (0.25): a coarser render rim.
High (1.5): a finer rim, a heavier mesh and a slower build.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.fract_surface:
How cracks follow the surface.
Classic: Cracks start at sharp edges and stop at edges and folds.
Rounded: Cracks start across the surface, follow curves and soft folds, and stop at sharp creases. Length 0 uses a few network cells.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_enable:
Erodes the object like weathered or broken stone: edges and corners break away first
Off: the object is left untouched
On: every closed piece of the object is eroded
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_seed:
Seed offset for repeatable procedural erosion.
Minimum: 0 gives the first pattern.
Maximum: Other values reroll the pattern, without increasing erosion strength.
Allowed range: 0 to 100000.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_damage:
Changes the volume threshold and, with Round First on, the pre-noise smoothing. Its response is nonlinear.
Minimum: 0% gives the least erosion, but the volume reconstruction can still alter topology and silhouette.
Maximum: 100% gives the strongest erosion and rounding recipe; thin details can disappear.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_noise_type:
Rocky uses hetero-terrain noise, Soft uses fBm, Cracked uses Voronoi edges, Cells uses smooth Voronoi cells.
Low / first state: Rocky and Soft give continuous weathering.
High / other state: Cracked emphasises a crack network; Cells gives pebble-like bites.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_noise_scale:
Frequency of noise in reference space. Larger values mean smaller features, despite the Scale label.
Minimum: 0.01 gives extremely broad variations.
Maximum: 1000 gives extremely fine requested variation; a coarse voxel grid cannot resolve it.
Allowed range: 0.01 to 1000.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_noise_contras:
Brightens the procedural field with a contrast/dodge factor up to 0.25 before the volume threshold. It changes how much of the field survives, rather than adding mesh detail.
Minimum: 0% keeps the base field response.
Maximum: 100% makes the field's transitions more pronounced; it does not refine the grid.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_round_first:
Adds damage-dependent volume smoothing before the noise operation. Even with this off, the base volume filter remains active.
Off: Off retains more of the original angular form.
On: On softens the volume first, increasingly with Damage.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_post_smooth:
Additional volume smoothing after the erosion field has been formed.
Minimum: 0% skips the extra post-smoothing.
Maximum: 100% rounds the eroded result further and can remove small chips.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_voxel_size:
Reference-space voxel size. Physical cell size is approximately Voxel Size times reference size divided by 20. The budget may enlarge it.
Minimum: 0.015 requests very fine sampling and high cost.
Maximum: 10 gives very coarse sampling and can remove the entire small solid; larger values are faster, not higher quality.
Allowed range: 0.015 to 10.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_relative_scal:
Controls automatic component-relative reference size versus an explicit Damage Scale, unless a reference object is assigned.
Off: Off uses the explicit reference size.
On: On gives each component a scale derived from its own largest dimension.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_ref_object:
Reference object used only when Relative Scale is enabled. Its largest world-space dimension is converted to the source reference space.
Low / first state: Empty uses the source or per-component dimensions in Relative Scale mode.
High / other state: Assigned uses the reference dimension while Relative Scale is on; ignored when fixed Damage Scale is selected.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_scale_size:
Explicit reference size in centimetres when Relative Scale is off; Master Scale also multiplies it.
Minimum: 1 cm makes relative features and target edge lengths small.
Maximum: Larger values enlarge the reference-space features; the reference-object field is ignored in this fixed-scale mode.
Allowed range: 1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_thickness_cap:
Positive values restrict erosion depth relative to local thickness; zero is a disabled sentinel.
Minimum: 0 disables the limit.
Maximum: 1 allows the full measured thickness; smaller positive fractions protect thin features more strictly.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_max_voxels:
Budget for all cells in a component's padded volume grid, including smoothing margins. The algorithm increases voxel size by 8% repeatedly until it fits.
Minimum: 100000 forces coarsening on many inputs.
Maximum: A larger budget preserves a finer requested grid at greater memory cost; it does not force fine sampling by itself.
Allowed range: 100000 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_avoid:
Keeps the Avoid faces untouched
Off: Avoid faces erode like the rest
On: Avoid faces stay intact
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_global_coords:
Chooses world-space versus local-space positions when evaluating the erosion field.
Off: Off anchors the pattern to the source's local coordinates.
On: On samples world positions, so transformed objects share a world-space field.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_offset:
Vector translation of the procedural sampling coordinates. Components move the pattern; they are not displacement amounts.
Minimum: Negative offsets move the sample origin in the negative direction.
Maximum: Positive offsets move it in the positive direction; repeatable positions are not ranked by intensity.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_rotation:
Euler rotation of the noise-coordinate frame.
Minimum: Zero uses the original coordinate orientation.
Maximum: Changing any axis rotates the pattern; a full turn returns to the same orientation.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_stretch:
Per-axis scaling of sampling coordinates, changing feature aspect rather than stretching output geometry directly.
Minimum: Small absolute components spread features along that axis.
Maximum: Larger absolute components compress them into finer features; use a nondegenerate vector.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_mask_mode:
None erodes everywhere; Vertex Group treats weight 1 as erodible; Image treats white as protected.
Low / first state: None uses the full geometric influence.
High / other state: Group and Image restrict the field, with opposite white/weight conventions explicitly described below.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_group:
Name of the vertex group used by Vertex Group mode. The host transfers source weights to the volume sampling.
Low / first state: Weight 0 protects the source region.
High / other state: Weight 1 permits full erosion; this is the opposite of white in an image mask.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_mask_image:
Image used in Image mode. The native sampler uses repeating bilinear image sampling and smooths the sampled mask on the voxel grid.
Low / first state: Black permits full erosion with normal mask polarity.
High / other state: White protects the source with normal polarity; Invert swaps these roles.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_mask_uv:
UV layer used to read an image mask when UV rather than box projection is selected.
Low / first state: An empty name falls back to the available active mapping.
High / other state: A named layer provides the image coordinates; a missing or unsuitable UV map prevents the intended mask placement.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_mask_box:
Uses box projection for image masking instead of source UVs.
Off: Off samples the image using the selected UV layer.
On: On projects by position and surface direction; it does not create a UV layer.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_mask_invert:
Reverses image-mask protection before the mask adjustment is applied.
Off: Off: white protects and black erodes.
On: On swaps protected and erodible image values.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_mask_adjust:
Biases the signed protection contribution of the sampled image in the volume threshold, rather than changing image pixels. Invert is applied to the sampled image first.
Minimum: -1 shifts toward less protection and more erosion.
Maximum: 1 shifts toward more protection and less erosion; the image and invert choice still define the original pattern.
Allowed range: -1 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_shade_smooth:
Smooths shading of the reconstructed mesh; it does not add geometry.
Off: Off exposes the reconstructed facets.
On: On interpolates normals for a smoother appearance.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_uv_transfer:
Transfers UV coordinates from the source to the rebuilt surface. New faces do not have the original polygon correspondence.
Off: Off leaves UV transfer disabled.
On: On approximates the original mapping on the new topology; deeply eroded faces can still need Quick UV Map.
ProjectDamageProps.erosion_uv_map:
Name of the source UV map used for optional UV transfer.
Low / first state: Empty uses the host's fallback active UV layer.
High / other state: A valid named map selects that source mapping; it is not a new noise-frequency control.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_enable:
Tears a jagged slit through sheet metal along your Grease Pencil strokes
Off: the metal is intact
On: every stroke becomes a torn, pushed-in slit
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_drawing:
Linked Grease Pencil or supported curve paths, read at the current frame and transformed into source-local space. Use New Drawing to create an input, Draw / Edit to paint, and the trash button to remove it.
Low / first state: Empty supplies no drawing constraint or no drawn damage, according to the placement mode.
High / other state: Assigned visible strokes guide placement; geometry outside their eligible region is not made eligible merely by drawing there.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_seed:
Seed for repeatable notches, wandering and edge blisters.
Minimum: 0 gives the first variant.
Maximum: Other integers change the random variant, not its strength.
Allowed range: 0 to 100000.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_width:
Maximum nominal slit width before taper and the endpoint fade.
Minimum: 0.01 cm gives a narrow slit.
Maximum: Larger values open a wider tear; keep Resolution small enough to represent its width.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_taper:
Reduces width at the start of a stroke relative to its end. Both endpoints also have a separate short fade.
Minimum: 0% keeps the body width approximately even.
Maximum: 100% gives the strongest opening from a narrow start toward a wider end; reversing a stroke reverses the taper.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_jagged:
Amplitude of notches along the tear boundary.
Minimum: 0% gives relatively clean slit edges.
Maximum: 100% gives strongly torn, irregular edges.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_meander:
Lateral wandering of the cut around the drawn centreline.
Minimum: 0% follows the stroke directly.
Maximum: 100% gives the strongest wandering; the drawing remains the broad guide.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_cut_depth:
Depth reached by the slit cutter. It must exceed the relevant panel thickness to cut through.
Minimum: 0.01 cm may make only a shallow cut on thick geometry.
Maximum: A larger depth can cut a thicker sheet; it does not determine the surrounding dent depth.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_dent_depth:
Inward displacement around the tear, modulated along the stroke and tapered at its ends.
Minimum: 0 leaves the surrounding sheet undented.
Maximum: Larger values push the neighbouring sheet inward more strongly.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_dent_width:
Lateral reach of the dent around each stroke.
Minimum: A small width confines deformation near the slit.
Maximum: A large width makes a broad dent without increasing the actual slit width.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_lip_curl:
Extra bending of the torn lips near the opening.
Minimum: 0% gives little additional lip curl.
Maximum: 100% gives the strongest supported curled edge.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_blisters:
Amount of small molten or buckled edge beads.
Minimum: 0% adds none.
Maximum: 100% gives the strongest bead population along the tear.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_blister_siz:
Physical size of edge blisters, in centimetres.
Minimum: Small values give tiny beads that may need fine Resolution.
Maximum: Large values give conspicuous raised lumps.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_heat_spread:
Width of the heat-zone point attribute around the tear. This control writes shader data; it is not a geometry displacement.
Minimum: 0 gives no extended heat zone.
Maximum: A larger value spreads the attribute farther from the tear; the material must read PD_MetalTear Heat.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_scratches:
Amount of fine scratch marks written to the PD_MetalTear Scratches attribute.
Minimum: 0% writes no scratches.
Maximum: 100% gives the strongest scratch coverage; visible only through a shader that reads the attribute.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_detail:
UI label: Resolution. The native parameter is the target triangle-edge length near tears, in centimetres. This is an inverse quality control.
Minimum: 0.01 cm requests very fine local topology and can reach the triangle budget.
Maximum: Larger values make the local mesh coarser and faster; narrow tears may lose shape.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_max_tris:
Budget for local refinement. It limits geometry work; it is not a guaranteed exact output triangle count.
Minimum: 20000 strongly limits refinement on long or multiple strokes.
Maximum: A higher budget allows the requested small edge length over more tear area, using more memory.
Allowed range: 20000 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.metaltear_material:
Material for the torn metal edges.
Empty: the default material is kept.
Assigned: torn edges get this material.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_enable:
Turns the object into hand-modelled clay: soft edges, lumps, thumb presses and smears
Off: the object keeps its shape
On: the whole object is reshaped as clay
ProjectDamageProps.clay_seed:
Seed shared by repeatable clay-noise and hand-mark placement.
Minimum: 0 is the first variant.
Maximum: Other values reroll the placement; they do not increase damage.
Allowed range: 0 to 100000.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_softness:
Repeated alternating smoothing passes round the source, with pass count depending on Softness and sampling density. This is not a bevel modifier.
Minimum: 0% skips the softness passes.
Maximum: 100% gives the strongest rounding; thin or nearby surfaces are still subject to safeguards.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_lumps:
Amplitude of broad normal displacement: nominal amplitude is 1.5% of reference size times Lumps/100.
Minimum: 0% disables broad lumps.
Maximum: 100% uses the full broad-lump amplitude.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_lump_scale:
Frequency multiplier of broad lumps, approximately 3 times this value per reference size. Despite the label, larger values make smaller features.
Minimum: 0.05 gives very broad variations.
Maximum: 50 gives very fine lumps, which require enough Resolution.
Allowed range: 0.05 to 50.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_presses:
Coverage of randomly placed round press marks. Count depends on available area, mark size and an internal cap, rather than being an exact number.
Minimum: 0% adds no round presses.
Maximum: 100% gives dense overlapping presses.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_press_size:
Press radius as a percentage of reference size, with per-mark variation. Smears also derive their width from it.
Minimum: 0.5% makes tiny marks requiring fine Resolution.
Maximum: 50% makes broad marks; fewer fit in the same surface area.
Allowed range: 0.5% to 50%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_press_depth:
Depth relative to each press radius, with random variation. Round marks use a factor of 0.5; smears use 0.35.
Minimum: 0% flattens the indentation contribution.
Maximum: 100% gives the deepest marks allowed by the reference radius and safeguards.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_press_rim:
Raised ring around each indentation.
Minimum: 0% leaves the press without a raised rim.
Maximum: 100% gives the strongest rim buildup.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_fingerprints:
Fine ridges inside hand marks. The implementation fades them out when their wavelength is below roughly two to five mesh edges.
Minimum: 0% disables fingerprints.
Maximum: 100% uses full ridge strength, but coarse Resolution can still make them disappear.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_smears:
Coverage of elongated hand marks. Uses a separate population derived from press size.
Minimum: 0% adds no smears.
Maximum: 100% makes dense elongated marks, overlapping other relief.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_smear_length:
Length-to-width aspect of the elongated marks.
Minimum: 1 makes nearly round marks.
Maximum: 8 makes long streaks; this does not lengthen the whole mesh.
Allowed range: 1 to 8.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_grain:
Amplitude of fine normal displacement, about 0.12% of reference size at full strength.
Minimum: 0% disables this fine grain.
Maximum: 100% gives full fine-grain amplitude, subject to sampling density.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_grain_scale:
Frequency multiplier, approximately 70 times this value per reference size.
Minimum: 0.1 gives coarser grain.
Maximum: 10 gives very fine grain that needs a fine mesh to show.
Allowed range: 0.1 to 10.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_cracks:
Coverage mask for a Voronoi-edge crack field.
Minimum: 0% disables cracks.
Maximum: 100% exposes the widest crack coverage supported by the field.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_crack_width:
Width of the crack profile when cracks are active. The formula includes a nonzero base width.
Minimum: 0% is the narrowest supported crack, not an off switch.
Maximum: 100% gives the widest crack profile; use Cracks = 0 to disable the feature.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_crack_depth:
Depth of the crack profile when cracks are active. It also includes a nonzero base value.
Minimum: 0% gives the shallowest supported groove.
Maximum: 100% gives the deepest supported groove, before protection limits.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_sag:
