Downward sag per connected component, weighted toward its top. The host transforms world gravity into local coordinates.
Minimum: 0% disables sag and the associated base spread.
Maximum: 100% uses the strongest sag, approximately up to 22% of a component's height before safeguards.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_bulge:
Outward spreading near a component's base while sagging. Multiplied by Sag, so it does nothing when Sag is zero.
Minimum: 0% suppresses base spreading.
Maximum: 100% gives the strongest base bulge under nonzero Sag.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_resolution:
Target number of edges across the reference size: edge length is reference size divided by Resolution.
Minimum: 20 gives a coarse mesh that cannot show fine fingerprints.
Maximum: 2000 requests a very fine mesh; Max Triangles can force a coarser result.
Allowed range: 20 to 2000.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_max_tris:
Refinement budget. If the requested mesh is too large, target edge length grows to fit the budget.
Minimum: 5000 keeps the result light but can erase small marks.
Maximum: A higher budget permits finer requested relief, using more time and memory.
Allowed range: 5000 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_thickness_cap:
Caps inward travel using local thickness ray tests, together with curvature and triangle-orientation checks. Zero is disabled.
Minimum: 0 disables the thickness cap.
Maximum: 1 permits the full measured thickness; smaller positive fractions are stricter. This is not an absolute self-intersection guarantee for arbitrary input.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_relative_scale:
Chooses automatic object-relative feature scale versus an explicit reference size. A reference object can provide the reference dimension.
Off: Off uses the explicit scale size when no reference object overrides it.
On: On derives the reference from the object's dimensions, so proportions follow source size.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_ref_object:
Reference object used only when Relative Scale is enabled. Its largest world-space dimension is converted to the source reference space.
Low / first state: Empty uses the source or per-component dimensions in Relative Scale mode.
High / other state: Assigned uses the reference dimension while Relative Scale is on; ignored when fixed Damage Scale is selected.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_scale_size:
Explicit reference size in centimetres when Relative Scale is off; Master Scale also multiplies it.
Minimum: 1 cm makes relative features and target edge lengths small.
Maximum: Larger values enlarge the reference-space features; the reference-object field is ignored in this fixed-scale mode.
Allowed range: 1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_avoid:
Keeps the Avoid faces untouched
Off: Avoid faces turn to clay like the rest
On: Avoid faces keep their original shape
ProjectDamageProps.clay_group:
Optional vertex-group influence interpolated on the source: zero protects, one allows the effect.
Low / first state: Empty imposes no group restriction.
High / other state: Assigned weights blend the effect; unweighted vertices are protected.
ProjectDamageProps.clay_material:
Material for the clay result.
Empty: the default clay material is kept.
Assigned: the clay gets this material.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_mode:
Procedural uses a thresholded multi-frequency field. Draw uses projected closed areas or bands around paths.
Low / first state: Procedural needs no drawing.
High / other state: Draw requires valid projected regions; an empty drawing generates no peeling.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_drawing:
Input paths for the current frame, projected onto the result surface before peeling.
Low / first state: Empty produces no regions in Draw mode.
High / other state: Assigned visible contours or strokes place the peeled patches.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_draw_shape:
Areas uses closed contour interiors; Strokes builds a peeled band around open paths.
Low / first state: Areas is suited to explicit exposed patches.
High / other state: Strokes follows thin damage trails with Stroke Width controlling the band.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_close_strokes:
Closes input paths for the Areas mask.
Off: Off requires the path itself to close.
On: On connects the contour endpoints; only relevant in Areas mode.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_stroke_width:
Width of the peeled band in Strokes mode, in centimetres.
Minimum: 0.1 cm gives a very narrow band needing high Detail.
Maximum: A larger width produces a broad peeled strip; irrelevant in Areas mode.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_paint_snap:
Maximum distance for projecting paths onto the mesh.
Minimum: Small distances reject floating strokes.
Maximum: Large distances accept farther paths and can project onto unintended nearby geometry.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_adaptive:
Refines near detected peeling seeds and restores unaffected original polygons, including their interpolated data.
Off: Off allows refinement over the whole eligible mesh.
On: On concentrates new topology around damage; coarse transition faces can still change to keep the rim connected.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_enable:
Lift the existing coating into attached curled edges, revealing a recessed inner layer.
Off: omit peeling while keeping its stored settings.
On: use peeling with the controls below.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_seed:
Moves the deterministic noise field and varies local curls and small damage.
Minimum: 0 selects the first repeatable pattern.
Maximum: Other integers reroll the pattern; they are not damage-strength values.
Allowed range: 0 to 100000.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_size:
Reference patch size in centimetres, multiplied by Master Scale. It sets procedural wavelength and the physical size of lift, bend, substrate depth and coating thickness.
Minimum: Small values create small patches and proportionally small rims.
Maximum: Large values create broad patches and proportionally larger layer dimensions; in Draw mode it still scales rim geometry.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_amount:
Threshold of the procedural field, not an exact area percentage. Surface orientation and edge protection change measured coverage.
Minimum: 0 disables procedural peeling.
Maximum: 85% exposes a large fraction of eligible surface, but protected edges and other effects remain protected.
Allowed range: 0% to 85%.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_small_damage_:
Adds small attached holes near main peeled boundaries without rerolling the main field.
Minimum: 0% adds no small satellite damage.
Maximum: 100% adds the densest supported local micro-damage; it remains close to main peeled zones.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_ragged:
Strength of higher-frequency contour noise. In Draw mode only a small perturbation is added to the drawing mask.
Minimum: 0% gives smoother field or drawing boundaries.
Maximum: 100% gives stronger jagged boundaries; Detail limits how much is resolved.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_lift:
Maximum nominal rim lift as a percentage of Patch Size. Lift falls quadratically over Bend Width and is reduced by Curl Variation.
Minimum: 0% leaves the rim unlifted while keeping the recessed substrate.
Maximum: 20% gives a strongly raised rim; large lift on small peninsulas can be visually excessive.
Allowed range: 0% to 20%.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_bend:
Width of the attached bend band as a percentage of Patch Size. The algorithm also protects a collar near structural edges.
Minimum: 5% confines bending to a narrow, steep rim.
Maximum: 40% spreads bending across a broad attached band and protects a wider structural collar.
Allowed range: 5% to 40%.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_variation:
Reduces local lift by a noise factor. It does not increase the nominal maximum lift.
Minimum: 0% keeps uniform nominal curl height.
Maximum: 100% gives the strongest variation, including low and highly lifted rim stretches.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_depth:
Substrate recess as a percentage of Patch Size. Local ray tests cap it at 40% of measured wall thickness when an opposing surface is found.
Minimum: 0.1% gives a shallow exposed layer.
Maximum: 8% requests a deep recess; a thin source wall can clamp the actual depth.
Allowed range: 0.1% to 8%.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_thickness:
Thickness of the peeled coating as a percentage of Patch Size, capped to half of local substrate depth.
Minimum: 0.02% gives a thin film.
Maximum: 1% gives a thicker lip unless substrate depth imposes a smaller cap.
Allowed range: 0.02% to 1%.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_detail:
Approximate edges per Patch Size: target edge length is Patch Size divided by Detail and Master Quality.
Minimum: 8 gives coarse contours and bends.
Maximum: 64 resolves fine contours with more faces.
Allowed range: 8 to 64.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_face_budget:
Stops additional splitting when predicted face count would exceed the budget. It is a refinement guard, not a decimator for an already dense input.
Minimum: 10000 can stop refinement early.
Maximum: 2000000 allows much denser local refinement, using more memory.
Allowed range: 10000 to 2e+06.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_group:
Optional vertex group. Weight below about 0.5 protects the surface; higher weights allow the peeling field. This is a thresholded mask, not a simple linear strength multiplier.
Low / first state: Empty applies no group restriction.
High / other state: Assigned groups constrain damage; unweighted vertices remain protected.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_material:
Material for the bare surface that shows where the coating peeled off.
Empty: the built-in bare-surface material is used.
Assigned: the bare surface gets this material.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_back_material:
Material for the underside of the curled coating.
Empty: the underside looks like the front.
Assigned: the underside gets this material.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_wall_type:
Concrete (default): a mineral cavity. Wooden: the surface breaks like a wooden skin over a straight cavity, split along the grain into planks; the Wooden Skin box appears and Wall Soft is hidden.
Concrete: a soft-edged spall with an aggregate floor.
Wooden: sheer, plank-wide steps along the grain round the patch.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_wood_thickne:
Thickness of the splintered wooden skin around a Wooden Wall damage opening.
Minimum: a thin facing with fine splinters.
Maximum: thicker plank ends; keep it consistent with the source wall thickness.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_wood_width:
Wooden only: width of the planks the skin breaks into (default 12 cm). The change is small at the scale of one patch.
Low (5 cm): narrow, closely spaced steps on the rim.
High (30 cm): fewer, wider steps.
Allowed range: 0.2 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_wood_splinte:
Wooden only: how far the planks split along the grain past the patch outline (default 6 cm).
Low (0): the planks end on the patch outline.
High (20 cm): long splinters reach far out above and below the patch.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageProps.concrete_wood_angle:
Wooden only: direction of the grain in degrees (-180 to 180, default 0 = vertical planks).
Low (0°): vertical planks and splinters.
High (90°): horizontal planks; the steps run sideways.
Allowed range: -180 to 180.
ProjectDamageProps.frame_restructure_ang:
Rotation between supporting fragments at which unprotected timber connections may snap.
Minimum: slight rotation can break members.
Maximum: tolerate larger rotations before breaking; protected connections remain continuous.
Allowed range: 1 to 179.
ProjectDamageProps.frame_restructure_min:
Minimum continuous timber connections retained for each fragment pair.
Minimum (0): every eligible member may break.
Maximum: preserve more connections, limited by the number of available members.
Allowed range: 1 to 32.
ProjectDamageProps.frame_restructure_col:
Break or shorten timber that crosses the remaining wall surfaces; keep the original embed at anchors. Protected connections seek a clear route.
Off: omit break on intersection while keeping its stored settings.
On: use break on intersection with the controls below.
ProjectDamageCleanSettings.min_part_perc:
Remove islands smaller than this percentage of the largest island: volume for closed solids, area for open surfaces.
Minimum (0): preserve all nonempty islands.
Maximum: remove progressively larger islands; the largest remains.
Allowed range: 0% to 100%.
ProjectDamageCleanSettings.keep_largest_:
Remove every part except the largest one, whatever its size.
Off: omit keep largest only while keeping its stored settings.
On: use keep largest only with the controls below.
ProjectDamageCleanSettings.report_only:
Count what would be removed without changing the mesh.
Off: omit report only while keeping its stored settings.
On: use report only with the controls below.
ProjectDamageCleanSettings.reference:
The original, undamaged shape that the result is compared with.
Empty: each result is compared with its own source object.
Assigned: this object is used as the original shape.
ProjectDamageCleanSettings.allowance:
How far the result may stick out beyond the original shape before it is trimmed.
0: nothing may stick out at all.
High: bigger bumps are left alone.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCleanSettings.use_reference:
Trim against evaluated source; match ProjectDamage Use Modifiers when enabled.
Off: omit source modifiers while keeping its stored settings.
On: use source modifiers with the controls below.
ProjectDamageCleanSettings.flip_open_sid:
Open references: reverse which side of their normals is trimmed.
Off: omit reverse open surface side while keeping its stored settings.
On: use reverse open surface side with the controls below.
ProjectDamageInputProps.mode:
Choose Mesh Preparation. Auto: Closed solids take the original path; n-gons are triangulated, split vertices welded, open or non-manifold surfaces handled in surface mode; Closed Only: Only triangulate n-gons; anything that is not a closed solid passes through unchanged (the original behaviour); Surface: Always prepare the mesh using Open Mesh Method, then build a temporary solid, apply damage, and remove helper faces.
Auto: Closed solids take the original path; n-gons are triangulated, split vertices welded, open or non-manifold surfaces handled in surface mode.
Closed Only: Only triangulate n-gons; anything that is not a closed solid passes through unchanged (the original behaviour).
Surface: Always prepare the mesh using Open Mesh Method, then build a temporary solid, apply damage, and remove helper faces.
ProjectDamageInputProps.holes:
Choose Open Mesh Method. Auto: Cap small holes to make solid volumes; thicken sheet-like surfaces; Fill Holes: Cap boundary loops when a valid closed volume can be made; Thin Shell: Keep the surface as a thin temporary shell instead of filling holes.
Auto: Cap small holes to make solid volumes; thicken sheet-like surfaces.
Fill Holes: Cap boundary loops when a valid closed volume can be made.
Thin Shell: Keep the surface as a thin temporary shell instead of filling holes.
ProjectDamageInputProps.thickness_logic:
Choose Thickness Logic. Improved: Local glass thickness and smoothed shell offsets; Legacy: Previous glass thickness and raw-normal shell offsets.
Improved: Local glass thickness and smoothed shell offsets.
Legacy: Previous glass thickness and raw-normal shell offsets.
ProjectDamageInputProps.use_modifiers:
Damage the evaluated mesh (with the modifier stack) instead of the base mesh.
Off: omit use modifiers while keeping its stored settings.
On: use use modifiers with the controls below.
ProjectDamageInputProps.weld_distance:
Merge preparation vertices closer than this distance.
Minimum: preserve close but separate vertices.
Maximum: weld wider gaps; large distances can collapse thin details.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageInputProps.surface_thicknes:
Thickness of the temporary solid behind an open source surface.
Minimum: a thin backing that is pierced by shallow cuts.
Maximum: deeper backing, allowing deeper cavities before a through-hole.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageInputProps.surface_flip:
Thicken toward the front instead, so the damage is cut into the surface's back side.
Off: omit damage back side while keeping its stored settings.
On: use damage back side with the controls below.
ProjectDamageInputProps.restore_ngons:
Dissolve untouched triangulated n-gons back into the original faces.
Off: omit restore n-gons while keeping its stored settings.
On: use restore n-gons with the controls below.
ProjectDamageInputProps.transfer_data:
Copy vertex groups and boolean face attributes (Avoid) onto the prepared result.
Off: omit transfer groups and attributes while keeping its stored settings.
On: use transfer groups and attributes with the controls below.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.resolution:
Quality of the branch cross-section: the number of sides of each branch tube is Branch Sides (6) times this share (default 100%). It does not change the growth paths. The image hides the leaves.
Low (25%): three-sided branches, a light mesh.
High (250%): round branches, a heavier mesh. Above about 270% the branch tubes need more than 16 sides and the grow stops with the error "Ivy geometry budget out of supported range", although the slider goes to 300%.
Allowed range: 10% to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.result:
The object that holds the grown ivy. The addon fills it in.
Empty: no ivy has been grown yet.
Assigned: this object is updated when you regrow.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.adhesion_smooth:
Smoothing of the surface directions used to orient the leaves (0 to 5, default 5); 0 uses the older one-sided filter.
Allowed range: 0 to 5.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.leaf_maturity:
How much the leaves gather on older parts of the shoot and where it touches the ground.
0: leaves are spread evenly along the shoot.
1: old parts are leafy, young tips are bare.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.seeds: A collection: every Empty in it starts a root. The + button adds a seed Empty. There is no image.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.guide: A Grease Pencil object whose strokes give the main growth direction, and start the ivy when there are no seeds. New Drawing creates one, Draw / Edit lets you draw, the bin deletes it. While you draw, a Finish Drawing button returns to the object.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.curve: A Curve object: a stem grows exactly along every spline, also in mid-air, and drops hanging tendrils. New Curve creates one, Draw / Edit lets you draw it. With a Curve and no seeds, only the hanging ivy grows. The two settings below are shown only when a Curve is set; their images use a Curve along the top of the wall.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.hang_density:
Chance of a hanging tendril at each growth step along the Curve (0 to 1, default 0.15).
Low (0.05): a few tendrils.
High (0.5): many tendrils; each is shorter, so the curtain looks denser but hangs less low.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.hang_length:
Longest hanging tendril, as a share of the object size; each tendril varies down to 40% of it (0 to 4, default 0.3).
Low (0.1): short fringes along the curve.
High (1): long tendrils hanging down the wall.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.seed:
Shuffles the growth without changing its size.
Every number gives a different plant.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.size:
Growth step (1 to 10, default 3); a larger value covers a larger area. Simple: 3 times Master Scale.
Allowed range: 1 to 10.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.primary_weight:
How strongly a shoot keeps growing in the direction it already has.
0: the shoot forgets its direction at once.
1: long, straight shoots.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.random_weight:
How much a shoot wanders at random.
0: no wandering.
1: tangled, restless shoots.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.gravity_weight:
Pull toward the ground while a shoot floats (0 to 2, default 1). Simple: 2 times Droop.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.adhesion_weight:
How strongly the ivy hugs the surface.
0: shoots drift freely away from the surface.
1: shoots cling tightly and follow every corner.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.guide_weight:
Shown only with a Guide: how strongly the ivy follows the strokes (0 to 2, default 1; side branches half as much per level). Simple: 2 times Guide Strength, or 0 with Follow Guides off.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.guide_radius:
Shown only with a Guide: reach of a stroke, as a share of the object size (0.01 to 1, default 0.15). Simple: 0.05 plus 0.2 times Guide Strength.
Allowed range: 0.01 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.branching_proba:
How often branches split into side shoots (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): one long shoot that wanders without branching.
High (1): a compact bush of short shoots; the same number of points is spent on many branches close to the seed.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.max_float_lengt:
How far a shoot may grow through the air before it dies, as a share of the object size.
0: shoots die as soon as they leave the surface.
1: shoots hang and bridge wide gaps.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.max_adhesion_di:
Reach of the surface adhesion, as a share of the object size (0 to 4, default 0.2). Simple: 0.4 times Cling times Master Scale; this is why Cling 0 stops the growth.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.max_nodes:
Total growth points (100 to 50000, default 4000). Simple: 300 plus 15000 times Amount squared (4050 at the default Amount).
Allowed range: 100 to 50000.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.branch_size:
Branch diameter (0 to 2, default 0.15). Simple: 0.15 times Master Scale times Branch Thickness.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.branch_sides:
Sides of the branch tubes before Resolution (3 to 16, default 6). The core accepts at most 16 sides after Resolution.
Allowed range: 3 to 16.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.uv_scale:
Tiling of the bark texture along and around the branches (0.01 to 100, default 1).
Allowed range: 0.01 to 100.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.leaf_size:
Leaf size, times Master Scale (0 to 5, default 1).
Low (0.5): small leaves; the branches show.
High (2): big leaves that overlap into a solid cover.
Allowed range: 0 to 5.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.leaf_density:
How many leaves grow along the branches (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): bare branches.
High (1): the branches are hidden under leaves.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.leaf_density_mu:
How many leaf candidates are tried per point (1 to 10, default 2). Simple: 1 plus 3 times Leaf Density to the power 1.5, rounded.
Allowed range: 1 to 10.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.leaf_offset:
Random extra stem length, so leaves stand off the branch for a bushier look (0 to 5, default 0).
Allowed range: 0 to 5.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.stem_length:
Length of the small stem joining each leaf to the branch, as a share of the leaf length (0 to 2, default 0.5; 0 = the leaf sits on the branch).
Low (0): leaves pressed against the branches.
High (2): leaves stand off on long stems; the cover looks looser.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.stem_thickness:
Thickness of the leaf stems (0 to 3, default 1; 0 = no stem geometry). Shown only when Stem Length is above 0.
Allowed range: 0 to 3.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.stem_attach:
Where the stalk joins the leaf in your leaf image, measured from the base of the leaf.
0: the stalk joins at the very base.
1: the stalk joins at the tip.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.leaf_uv_directi: Which way the leaf tip points in your leaf image: Up, Right (default), Down or Left. Each leaf is then turned so its tip points along the growth direction, without rotating UVs by hand. It changes only the UVs, not the shape, so there is no image.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.leaf_tilt:
Random tilt of each leaf on two axes, in degrees (0 to 90, default 30): the tip lifts off the surface and the leaf rolls about its length. The stem follows the leaf.
Low (0): leaves lie flat on the surface like scales.
High (90): leaves stand out in every direction; a bushy look.
Allowed range: 0 to 90.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.advanced_contro: Switches the panel to the detailed growth settings below. In Advanced mode the Simple sliders are not used; the detailed values are used as they are. Ivy grown before the Simple controls existed opens in Advanced mode, so it keeps its look.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.master_scale:
Scales the whole ivy: growth step, branch thickness and leaf size together (0.05 to 20, default 1).
Low (0.5): a small, fine-leaved patch.
High (2): big leaves and long steps; the ivy covers much more of the wall.
Allowed range: 0.05 to 20.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.amount:
How much ivy grows: how far it spreads and how many branches it makes (0 to 1, default 0.5). It sets the total number of growth points.
Low (0.2): a small sprig.
High (0.9): a large, dense patch.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.branching_amoun:
How often branches split into side shoots (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): one long shoot that wanders without branching.
High (1): a compact bush of short shoots; the same number of points is spent on many branches close to the seed.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.randomness:
0 grows in long straight runs, 1 wanders in every direction (default 0.5).
Low (0): long straight shoots that climb and run across the whole wall.
High (1): a tight tangle near the seed.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.climb:
How tightly the ivy hugs the surface and how far it reaches for it (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): the shoots do not hold on; they float off, die and almost nothing grows.
High (1): the ivy stays flat on the surface and spreads over the ground and the wall.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.droop:
How much loose shoots hang down, and how soon they give up when they lose the surface (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): shoots may float well off the surface; the ivy climbs high up the wall.
High (1): shoots die as soon as they leave the surface; almost nothing grows.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.branch_thicknes:
Branch thickness, times Master Scale (0 to 5, default 1). The image hides the leaves.
Low (0.3): hair-thin stems.
High (3): thick, woody vines.
Allowed range: 0 to 5.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.simple_leaf_siz:
Leaf size, times Master Scale (0 to 5, default 1).
Low (0.5): small leaves; the branches show.
High (2): big leaves that overlap into a solid cover.
Allowed range: 0 to 5.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.density:
How many leaves grow along the branches (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): bare branches.
High (1): the branches are hidden under leaves.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.follow_guides: Shown only with a Guide in Simple mode. Turn it off to keep the guide but ignore it; there is no separate image.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.guide_strength:
Shown only with a Guide in Simple mode: how strongly, and from how far, the growth is pulled along the strokes (0 to 1, default 0.5). Side branches feel half as much pull per level. The image uses a stroke drawn diagonally up the wall.
Low (0): the guide is ignored; the ivy grows as without it.
High (1): the ivy follows the stroke closely in a narrow band.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.branch_material:
Material for the stems of the ivy.
Empty: the default stem material is kept.
Assigned: the stems get this material.
ProjectDamageIvySettings.leaf_material:
Material for the leaves of the ivy.
Empty: the default leaf material is kept.
Assigned: the leaves get this material.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.enable:
A breach through the wall with the masonry of its thickness exposed.
Off: omit wall hole while keeping its stored settings.
On: use wall hole with the controls below.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.sites:
A collection of empties. Every empty marks one hole on the nearest wall face.
Empty: one hole is made at the 3D cursor.
Assigned: one hole is made at each empty.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.seed:
Shuffles the broken outline and loose bricks without changing the size of the hole.
Every number gives a different random arrangement.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.hole_width:
Width of the hole, in cm.
Low: a narrow gap.
High: a wide breach.
Allowed range: 5 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.hole_heigh:
Height of the hole, in cm.
Low: a low opening.
High: a tall opening.
Allowed range: 5 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.hole_lift:
Moves the hole up or down from its marker, in cm.
Negative: the hole sits below the marker.
Positive: the hole sits above the marker.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.jagged:
How irregular the outline of the hole is.
0: a clean oval.
High (1.5): a wild, lumpy outline.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.5.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.edge_ragge:
How randomly single bricks stick out or are missing along the outline.
0: an even, comb-like stepped edge.
High (3): a ragged, toothy edge.
Allowed range: 0 to 3.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.depth_vari:
How much the edge steps back from one brick layer to the next through the wall.
0: the same outline right through the wall.
1: each layer breaks at a different place.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.brick_leng:
Length of one brick, in cm.
Low: short bricks.
High: long bricks.
Allowed range: 1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.brick_heig:
Height of one brick, in cm.
Low: flat bricks.
High: tall blocks.
Allowed range: 1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.brick_widt:
Width of one brick into the wall, in cm.
Low: thin bricks, more layers through the wall.
High: deep bricks, fewer layers.
Allowed range: 1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.mortar:
Set Mortar (cm) for this generated feature.
Minimum: Tight or closed mortar joints.
Maximum: Wider mortar joints between the bricks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.bond:
Choose Bond. Running: Stretchers, half-brick shift per course; Header Courses: Every second course headers across the wall.
Running: Stretchers, half-brick shift per course.
Header Courses: Every second course headers across the wall.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.joint_dept:
How deep the mortar joints are scraped out around the hole, in cm.
0: joints flush with the bricks.
High: deep grooves between bricks.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.plaster_th:
Thickness of the plaster on the wall, in cm.
0: bare brick wall, no plaster.
High: a thick plaster layer with a clear broken step.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.plaster_ba:
How far the plaster is knocked off beyond the bricks.
Minimum: Plaster loss stays close to the brick opening.
Maximum: Plaster is knocked off farther beyond the brick opening.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.broken_cha:
Set Broken Bricks for this generated feature.
Minimum: Keep more of the original structure intact.
Maximum: Omit or break a larger share of eligible elements.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.rubble_ena:
Enable this feature for the current source. Disable to omit it without losing its stored settings.
Off: omit rubble while keeping its stored settings.
On: use rubble with the controls below.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.rubble_sha:
How many of the knocked-out bricks lie at the foot of the wall.
0: no rubble.
1: every removed brick lies on the ground.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.rubble_spr:
Set Rubble Spread for this generated feature.
Minimum: Rubble collects close to the opening.
Maximum: Rubble is scattered over a broader floor area.
Allowed range: 0.1 to 3.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.rubble_max:
Set Rubble Max for this generated feature.
Minimum: A small number of loose bricks is permitted.
Maximum: Permit more rubble bricks, with more geometry.
Allowed range: 0 to 5000.
ProjectDamageWallHoleSettings.brick_coll:
Your brick objects: they replace the rubble and the rim bricks, fitted to the generated brick bounds.
Empty: no collection input.
Assigned: read supported helper objects from that collection.
ProjectDamageFragmentSettings.origin_to_:
Put each fragment's origin at the centre of its bounds.
Off: omit origin to pieces while keeping its stored settings.
On: use origin to pieces with the controls below.
ProjectDamageFragmentSettings.own_collec:
Put the fragments in a new collection named after the mesh.
Off: omit own collection while keeping its stored settings.
On: use own collection with the controls below.
ProjectDamageFragmentSettings.hide_origi:
Hide the mesh that was split once the fragments exist.
Off: omit hide original while keeping its stored settings.
On: use hide original with the controls below.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.resolution:
Quality of the root cross-section: the number of sides is Sides (8) times this share (default 100%). It does not change the growth paths.
Low (25%): angular roots, a light mesh.
High (200%): round roots. Above about 200% the tubes need more than 16 sides and the grow stops with the error "Roots geometry budget out of supported range", although the slider goes to 300%.
Allowed range: 10% to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.result:
The object that holds the grown roots. The addon fills it in.
Empty: no roots have been grown yet.
Assigned: this object is updated when you regrow.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.seeds: A collection: every Empty in it starts a cluster of roots. The + button adds a seed Empty. There is no image.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.guide: A Grease Pencil or Curve object whose strokes the roots follow, and start from when there are no seeds. New Drawing creates one, Draw / Edit lets you draw, the bin deletes it. While you draw, a Finish Drawing button returns to the object.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.seed:
Shuffles the growth without changing its size.
Every number gives a different root system.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.size:
Growth step (1 to 10, default 3): larger is faster and coarser. Simple: 3 times Master Scale.
Allowed range: 1 to 10.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.roots_per_see:
Main roots radiating evenly around each seed (1 to 32, default 6). Simple: 1 plus 10 times Amount, rounded.
Allowed range: 1 to 32.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.root_length:
Length of a main root, as a share of the object size (0.01 to 4, default 0.5). Simple: 2 times Length squared times Master Scale.
Allowed range: 0.01 to 4.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.length_random:
How much the roots differ in length.
0: all roots are the same length.
1: short and long roots mixed.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.primary_weigh:
How strongly a root keeps growing in the direction it already has.
0: the root forgets its direction at once.
1: long, straight roots.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.random_weight:
How much a root wanders at random.
0: no wandering.
1: twisted, restless roots.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.gravity_weigh:
How much roots run down walls, rocks and slopes; it has no effect on flat ground (0 to 1, default 0.5). The image uses a seed on top of a boulder.
Low (0): the roots spread over the boulder in all directions.
High (1): the roots run straight down the sides of the boulder.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.spread_weight:
How strongly roots fan out away from their seed (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): roots curl around near the base.
High (1): roots run straight outward, like spokes.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.guide_weight:
Shown only with a Guide: how strongly roots follow the strokes (0 to 2, default 1; side roots half as much per level). Simple: 2 times Guide Strength, or 0 with Follow Guides off.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.guide_radius:
Shown only with a Guide: reach of a stroke, as a share of the object size (0.01 to 1, default 0.15). Simple: 0.05 plus 0.2 times Guide Strength.
Allowed range: 0.01 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.branching_pro:
How often roots fork into side roots, and how many generations of side roots grow (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): bare main roots without side roots.
High (1): a dense mat of short side roots near the base.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.branch_angle:
Angle of a side root off its parent, in degrees (5 to 90, default 45).
Allowed range: 5 to 90.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.max_levels:
Generations of side roots (0 to 5, default 3). Simple: 1 plus 4 times Branching, rounded.
Allowed range: 0 to 5.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.child_length:
Length of a side root, as a share of the parent's remaining length (0.05 to 1, default 0.5).
Allowed range: 0.05 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.root_size:
Base thickness of the main roots (0 to 5, default 0.6). Simple: 0.6 times Master Scale times Thickness.
Allowed range: 0 to 5.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.taper:
How fast roots thin out toward the tip (0.1 to 3, default 0.8).
Allowed range: 0.1 to 3.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.tip_radius:
Thickness of a root at its tip, compared with its base.
Low: roots thin out to a fine point.
1: roots stay as thick as at the base.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.child_radius:
Thickness of a side root, as a share of the parent's thickness where it forks (0.1 to 1, default 0.7).
Allowed range: 0.1 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.embed:
How deep roots sink into the surface (0 to 1, default 0.35): 0 lies on top, 1 is fully buried.
Low (0): roots lie on the ground like ropes.
High (1): only the thickest parts near the base show.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.flare:
Share of each main root that rises out of the ground and thickens toward the seed, like the buttress at a trunk (0 to 1, default 0.15).
Low (0): roots stay flat right up to the seed.
High (0.6): the roots swell and rise near the trunk. On this thin post the change is small.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.flatten:
Squashes the root section against the surface (0 to 0.9, default 0.25).
Allowed range: 0 to 0.9.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.sides:
Sides of the root tubes before Resolution (3 to 16, default 8). The core accepts at most 16 sides after Resolution.
Allowed range: 3 to 16.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.uv_scale:
Tiling of the bark texture along and around the roots (0.01 to 100, default 1).
Allowed range: 0.01 to 100.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.max_nodes:
Total growth points (100 to 200000, default 20000). Simple: 5000 plus 30000 times Amount.
Allowed range: 100 to 200000.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.merge_by_dist: Welds the tube seams, the tips and vertices that are closer than Merge Distance, so the roots stay one surface when you displace them (default on). It changes the mesh connections, not the shape, so there is no image.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.merge_distanc:
Shown when Merge by Distance is on: vertices closer than this (world size) are welded (default 0.1 cm). Keep it below the tip thickness unless you want the tips closed to a point. There is no image.
Allowed range: 0 to 10.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.advanced_cont: Switches the panel to the detailed settings below; the Simple sliders are then ignored. Roots grown before the Simple controls existed open in Advanced mode.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.master_scale:
Scales the whole root system: root length, thickness and growth step together (0.05 to 20, default 1).
Low (0.5): a small, fine root system.
High (2): thick roots that reach across the whole ground.
Allowed range: 0.05 to 20.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.amount:
How many main roots start at each seed (1 to 11), and how much may grow in total (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0.1): two main roots.
High (1): eleven main roots, a dense system.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.length_amount:
How far the roots reach from their seed, times Master Scale (0 to 1, default 0.5). The reach grows with the square of the value.
Low (0.25): short stubs around the base.
High (0.8): long roots that spread over the whole ground.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.branching_amo:
How often roots fork into side roots, and how many generations of side roots grow (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): bare main roots without side roots.
High (1): a dense mat of short side roots near the base.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.randomness:
0 grows straight, even roots; 1 wanders and varies the root lengths a lot (default 0.5).
Low (0): straight roots of similar length.
High (1): curly roots; many stay short.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.downhill:
How much roots run down walls, rocks and slopes; it has no effect on flat ground (0 to 1, default 0.5). The image uses a seed on top of a boulder.
Low (0): the roots spread over the boulder in all directions.
High (1): the roots run straight down the sides of the boulder.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.spread_amount:
How strongly roots fan out away from their seed (0 to 1, default 0.5).
Low (0): roots curl around near the base.
High (1): roots run straight outward, like spokes.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.thickness:
Root thickness, times Master Scale (0 to 5, default 1).
Low (0.5): thin, stringy roots.
High (3): heavy, thick roots.
Allowed range: 0 to 5.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.follow_guides: Shown only with a Guide in Simple mode. Turn it off to ignore the guide; there is no separate image.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.guide_strengt:
Shown only with a Guide in Simple mode: how strongly, and from how far, the roots are pulled along the strokes (0 to 1, default 0.5; side roots half as much per level). The image uses a curve drawn from the post toward the front left.
Low (0): the guide is ignored.
High (1): all roots run together along the stroke.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageRootsSettings.root_material:
Material for the roots.
Empty: the default root material is kept.
Assigned: the roots get this material.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.enabled:
Enable enabled for this object.
Off: omit enabled while keeping its stored settings.
On: use enabled with the controls below.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.result:
The object that holds the generated cables. The addon fills it in.
Empty: no cables have been made yet.
Assigned: this object is updated when you rebuild.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.live_updat:
Rebuild the cables while you edit or move the curve, the proximity Empty, the colliders or the damage zones.
Off: omit live update while keeping its stored settings.
On: use live update with the controls below.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.seed:
Shuffles the layout and shape of the cables.
Every number gives a different random arrangement.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.count:
Number of cables, per curve spline or per Empty (1 to 256, default 1).
Low (1): one cable.
High (16): a thick bundle.
Allowed range: 1 to 256.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.clumps:
The cables are split into this many separate groups (1 to 64, default 1; never more than Amount). The images use Amount 12 and Radius 0.25 m.
Low (1): all the cables in one bundle.
High (6): six thin bundles spread over Radius.
Allowed range: 1 to 64.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.noise:
Curve: the clumps and the loose cables meander. Proximity: the dropped cables bend and coil (0 to 1, default 0). The images use Amount 6 in 2 clumps.
Low (0): the cables follow the curve smoothly.
High (1): the clumps wander and cross each other.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.gravity:
0 (default) lays the cables exactly along the curve. Above 0 a rope simulation settles them: they hang between the held points and lie on the colliders. 1 is earth gravity, up to 10 for heavy, fast settling cables. The Physics box replaces the Hanging box when Gravity is above 0.
Low (0): a straight run under the ceiling.
High (1 or 10): the cables hang in loops between the points; 10 looks much the same as 1 once they have settled.
Allowed range: 0 to 10.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.master_sca:
Scales every cable size together: diameter, gaps, strip length, ties, connectors, holes (default 1). The lengths in metres (Radius, Fan Out, coils, dangles) do not change.
Low (0.5): thin cables.
High (3): thick cables; the stripped ends are three times as long.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.radius:
Curve: how far the clumps spread round the curve. Proximity: the cables are dropped within this distance of the Empty (metres, default 0). The images use Amount 9 in 3 clumps.
Low (0): the clumps lie right next to each other.
High (0.4 m): the clumps spread far apart.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.diameter:
Outer diameter of one cable; the width of a flat cable (default 1.1 cm, set by Cable Type).
Low (0.5 cm): thin cables.
High (3 cm): thick cables.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.cable_type: The kind of cable: Round Sheathed (a grey cable with three cores), Twin & Earth (a flat cable, two cores and a bare earth), Single Wires (loose insulated wires, no sheath), Armored (a spiral metal sheath) or Data (a thin blue network cable with four cores). Choosing a type also sets its usual Diameter, Stiffness and Strip Length. The images show the stripped end of each type.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.arrangemen: Side by Side: next to each other, like a flat run on a wall or a tray. Bundle (default): packed in a round bundle. Twisted: a round bundle that turns round its centre.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.gap:
Space between neighbouring cables of a clump (default 0.1 cm).
Low (0): the cables touch.
High (1 cm): a loose bundle with gaps between the cables.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.roll:
Curves only: turns the cables round the curve. Side by Side lies across the curve horizontally; 90 degrees stacks the run upwards, flat against a wall (default 0). The images use Side by Side.
Low (0°): a flat row lying horizontally.
High (90°): the row stands on edge.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.twist:
Twisted only: turns of the bundle per metre (default 2).
Low (0.5): a gentle twist.
High (8): a tight rope.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.noise_leng:
Shown when Noisiness is above 0: the length of one bend (default 40 cm). The images use Noisiness 0.6.
Low (10 cm): short, tight wiggles.
High (150 cm): long, lazy waves.
Allowed range: 1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.length_min:
Shortest cable dropped near the empty.
Low: some cables are short ends.
High: even the shortest cable is long.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.length_max:
Longest cable dropped near the empty.
Low: all cables stay short.
High: some cables run far across the floor.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.sag:
The cables droop between the control points, as a share of the distance between two points (0 to 1, default 0; the Cable Curve tile sets 0.08). Vertical stretches do not sag. The images use a curve with five points.
Low (0): straight from point to point.
High (0.3): deep swags between the points.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.sag_random:
Every stretch between two points sags a little differently (0 to 1, default 0.3). Greyed out when Sag is 0. The images use Sag 0.15.
Low (0): all stretches sag the same.
High (1): some stretches sag much more than others.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.spread:
Shown with Amount above 1 and no ties: loose cables each sag their own way (0 to 1, default 0.3). The images use Sag 0.12 and Amount 6.
Low (0): the cables hang together.
High (1): the cables of a clump hang at different depths.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.diameter_r:
Thinner cables mixed in: each cable gets its own thickness, down to 30 % of Diameter (0 to 1, default 0). The images use Amount 12.
Low (0): all cables the same.
High (1): a mix of thick and thin cables.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.fan_out:
At both ends the cables of a clump spread this far apart, each its own way, like wiring splaying out of a bundle (metres, default 0). The images use Amount 8.
Low (0): a neat bundle to the ends.
High (0.4 m): the cables splay wide apart near the ends.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.coils:
Share of the cables with a loop of spare cable hanging from them (0 to 1, default 0). With Gravity the loops hang and tangle.
Low (0): no loops.
High (1): every cable has a loop.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.coil_radiu:
Shown when Coils is above 0: the size of the loops (default 0.12 m).
Low (0.05 m): small loops.
High (0.3 m): large loops.
Allowed range: 0.005 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.coil_turns:
Shown when Coils is above 0: turns of a loop (1 to 20, default 2).
Low (1): a single loop.
High (5): a coil of several turns.
Allowed range: 1 to 20.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.dangle:
With Gravity only: share of the cables that came loose at one end and hang down from the last point that still holds them (0 to 1, default 0). The images use Gravity 1 and Amount 6.
Low (0): every cable is held at every point.
High (1): every cable hangs down at one end.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.dangle_len:
Shown when Dangling Ends is above 0: how much longer a loose cable is, so it hangs down to the floor (default 1 m).
Low (0.3 m): short ends.
High (2 m): the ends reach the floor and lie on it.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.colliders:
Objects in this collection are solid for the cables: they lie on them, drape over edges and hang off them. The + button puts the other selected objects into it (made if needed). The images use Floor on.
No colliders: the cables fall through the blocks onto the floor.
Floor and blocks as colliders: the cables drape over the blocks.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.use_floor:
An endless floor at Floor Height the cables cannot fall through.
Off: omit floor while keeping its stored settings.
On: use floor with the controls below.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.floor_heig:
Height of the floor the cables fall onto.
Low: the cables land lower.
High: the cables land higher.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.pin: Where the simulated cables are held. Control Points (default): at every control point of the curve, hanging between them; for Proximity, at the start, hanging from the Empty. Ends: at both ends only, the rest drapes over the colliders. Start: at the first point only. Nothing: free, the cables drop and lie on the colliders or the floor.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.slack:
Extra cable between two held points, as a share of their distance (0 and up, default 0.06). More slack hangs lower.
Low (0): the cables are pulled tight under the ceiling.
High (0.3): deep loops between the points.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.stiffness:
Soft cables bend in tight curves and coil; stiff ones keep straighter (0 to 1, default 0.45; set by Cable Type). The images use 4 cables with Noisiness 1.
Low (0.05): the cables flop into soft curves.
High (1): the cables keep their shape; the difference is small when they lie on the floor.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.friction:
How much the cables grip the colliders and each other (0 to 1, default 0.6). The images drop three cables onto a 35° ramp, held nowhere.
Low (0): the cables slide off the ramp onto the floor.
High (0.6 or 1): the cables stay on the ramp.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.steps:
How long the cables may fall and settle, at 60 steps per second (10 to 5000, default 240). The simulation stops early once everything is at rest.
Low (20): the cables are still falling when the simulation stops.
High (1200): the same as the default; the cables were already at rest.
Allowed range: 10 to 5000.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.end_start:
The cable end at the first point.
Capped: The cable ends closed, cut clean.
Stripped: Sheath cut back by Strip Length: the insulated cores fan out and end in bare copper.
Torn: Ragged sheath, cores of uneven length that splay and droop: a cable torn off.
Connector: The cable ends in a plug: a power plug with pins, an RJ45 plug for data cables, a crimp ferrule for single wires.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.end_end:
The cable end at the last point.
Capped: The cable ends closed, cut clean.
Stripped: Sheath cut back by Strip Length: the insulated cores fan out and end in bare copper.
Torn: Ragged sheath, cores of uneven length that splay and droop: a cable torn off.
Connector: The cable ends in a plug: a power plug with pins, an RJ45 plug for data cables, a crimp ferrule for single wires.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.strip:
Stripped or Torn ends: how far the sheath is stripped back, showing the cores (default 4 cm; set by Cable Type).
Low (1 cm): short core ends.
High (12 cm): long cores.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.splay:
Stripped or Torn ends: how far the cores fan out (0 to 1, default 0.4). The images use a 2 cm cable.
Low (0): the cores stay together.
High (1): the cores spread apart.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.fray:
Torn ends only: how ragged the edge of the sheath is (0 to 1, default 0.5). The images use a 2 cm cable.
Low (0): an even cut through the sheath.
High (1): a ragged, uneven sheath edge.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.damage_zon:
A collection of empties or objects that mark where the cables are bitten through.
Empty: the cables stay whole.
Assigned: cables are cut where they pass through these zones.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.damage_eve:
Bite holes along the whole length, not only in the damage zones.
Off: omit everywhere while keeping its stored settings.
On: use everywhere with the controls below.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.damage_amo:
How many holes are bitten into a metre of cable inside a damage zone (0 and up, default 0 = no damage). The other settings appear when it is above 0. The images use Everywhere, a 2 cm cable and Sides 20.
Low (0): no holes.
High (30): the cable is bitten all along.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.damage_siz:
Length of a hole in cable diameters, and how far it reaches round the cable (0.2 and up, default 1.2).
Low (0.6): small bites.
High (3): long gashes that open the cores.
Allowed range: 0.2 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.strands:
How many copper strands of a bitten core stick out of the hole (0 to 1, default 0.6).
Low (0): clean holes.
High (1): many strands.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.strand_len:
How far the strands stick out, in cable diameters (default 1).
Low (0.3): short stubs.
High (3): long whiskers of copper.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.ties:
Bands round every clump every Tie Spacing. A tied clump stays together: it falls and hangs as one, and the Variation box is greyed out. The images use Amount 6.
Off: a loose bundle.
On: black ties every 25 cm.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.tie_spacin:
Distance between two ties (default 25 cm).
Low (10 cm): many ties.
High (60 cm): one tie on this 60 cm cable.
Allowed range: 1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.tie_width:
Width of a tie (default 0.4 cm).
Low (0.2 cm): thin ties.
High (1.5 cm): wide bands.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.clips:
Curves only: a clamp holding every clump at every control point, except at stripped, torn and connector ends. The images show the middle point of the curve.
Off: no clamp.
On: a white clip at the point.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.sides:
Resolution round a cable (4 to 48, default 10). Use 16 or more where holes are bitten.
Low (4): a square-ish cable with hard shading.
High (24): a smooth round cable.
Allowed range: 4 to 48.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.segment:
Resolution along the cables: one ring of vertices every so far (default 1 cm). The images use Noisiness 1 with Noise Length 15 cm on a 2 cm cable.
Low (0.3 cm): smooth bends, about twice the vertices of the default.
High (8 cm): the bends turn into straight pieces.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.use_radius:
Curve: how far the clumps spread round the curve. Proximity: the cables are dropped within this distance of the Empty (metres, default 0). The images use Amount 9 in 3 clumps.
Low (0): the clumps lie right next to each other.
High (0.4 m): the clumps spread far apart.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.use_tilt:
Use Tilt, curves only (on by default): the tilt of the curve points (Ctrl + T in Edit Mode) rolls the cables round the curve, on top of Roll. The images use a Side by Side run of 5 cables with the end point tilted 90°.
Off: a flat row all along.
On: the row turns on edge toward the end.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.uv_scale:
Tiling of the cable texture along the cables (default 1). Material only, no image.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.sheath_mat:
Material for the outer sheath of the cables.
Empty: a built-in material that suits the cable type is used.
Assigned: the sheath gets this material.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.tie_materi:
Material for the cable ties.
Empty: black nylon is used.
Assigned: the ties get this material.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.clip_mater:
Curves only: a clamp holding every clump at every control point, except at stripped, torn and connector ends. The images show the middle point of the curve.
Off: no clamp.
On: a white clip at the point.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.connector_:
Material for the plug bodies.
Empty: grey plastic is used.
Assigned: the plugs get this material.
ProjectDamageCableGenSettings.pin_materi:
Material for the metal pins of the plugs.
Empty: brass is used.
Assigned: the pins get this material.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.source: Cloth Hanging: curtains, swags and corner drapes pinned to the curve. Cloth Along Curve: draped over the curve (a rope or a beam) or crumpled along it. Cloth Around Empties: crumpled sheets and heaps near the Empties.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.empties:
A collection of empties that the sheets of cloth gather around.
Empty: sheets are spread without gathering points.
Assigned: sheets collect near every empty.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.curve:
Source curve or Grease Pencil strokes for Cloth Sheets. Cloth Hanging creates a Bezier curve with automatic handles.
Move Cloth Hanging Curve to reposition the cloth. Edit its points and handles to reshape the hanging rail.
With Live Update enabled, changes recalculate automatically. With it disabled, press Update Cloth Sheets.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.sheet_type: Mixed (default for Along Curve and Around Empties) picks a type for each sheet from the ones the source allows: Curtain, Swag or Corner when hanging, Draped or Crumpled along a curve, Crumpled round Empties. Curtain (default for Cloth Hanging): the top edge is pinned along the curve every Pin Spacing and gathered, with scallops between the pins. Swag: pinned at the two top corners (sometimes also in the middle), a deep swag. Corner: hung by one corner and a point further down the side. A hanging type on another source becomes Draped or Crumpled. The images show Cloth Hanging with 4 sheets.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.amount:
Number of sheets (1 to 200, default 6).
Low (2): two sheets.
High (16): the rail is full and further sheets hang in a second row in front.
Allowed range: 1 to 200.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.noisiness:
Crumple and fine wrinkles (0 to 2, default 0.5). It also waves the hanging sheets a little before the simulation, so they can fold.
Low (0): smooth cloth with only the folds of the simulation.
High (2): a bumpy, crinkled surface.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.gravity:
How strongly the cloth sags and settles, times 9.81 m/s² (0 to 3, default 1). The images use 3 swags.
Low (0.2): the swags stay shallow and the wind lifts them sideways.
High (3): deep, heavy swags.
Allowed range: 0 to 3.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.scale:
Sheet size: the longer side, plus or minus 30 % (default 1.2 m).
Low (0.6 m): small cloths.
High (2 m): long sheets that reach the floor and pile up on it.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.radius:
Around Empties: the sheets and clumps are spread within this distance of the Empties. Along Curve: crumpled sheets land up to half this distance to the side of the curve. Not used by hanging sheets (default 1 m). The images use 8 sheets and Clumps 0.
Low (0.2 m): a single heap at each Empty.
High (2.5 m): the sheets are scattered far over the floor.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.diameter:
Cloth thickness: the Solidify of the result and the distance the cloth keeps from colliders (default 4 mm). The images are close-ups of a sheet over the beam. Very thick values with the default Detail can make the simulation fail: in our test 3 cm crushed the draped sheets into a tangle.
Low (1 mm): thin fabric.
High (12 mm): a thick tarp or felt.
Allowed range: 0.0002 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.clumps:
Number of heaps (0 to 50, default 2; 0 scatters every sheet on its own). About 85 % of the sheets go into a clump. The images use 12 crumpled sheets round two Empties.
Low (0): every sheet lies on its own.
High (5): several separate heaps.
Allowed range: 0 to 50.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.clump_tightne:
How tightly a clump is stacked and folded (0 to 1, default 0.6). The images use 12 crumpled sheets in 2 clumps.
Low (0): a wide, loose heap.
High (1): a slightly more compact heap; the change is small.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.stiffness:
Bending resistance: 0 silk, 1 stiff canvas or tarp (default 0.25). The images use 3 swags.
Low (0): many small, soft folds.
High (1): fewer, rounder folds.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.friction:
How much the cloth grips the colliders (0 to 1, default 0.6). The images drop 4 sheets onto a 30° ramp.
Low (0): the sheets slide down the ramp onto the floor.
High (1): the sheets stay where they land on the slope.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.curve_radius:
Draped sheets: the curve is a rope or beam of this radius that the cloth lies over (default 3 cm). The images use Cloth Along Curve with no beam, Type Draped and 3 sheets; the bar in the images is drawn at the same radius.
Low (1 cm): the sheets hang over a thin rope.
High (20 cm): the sheets wrap round a thick pipe.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.pin_spacing:
Curtain: distance between the pins along the curve (default 35 cm). The images use 3 curtains.
Low (10 cm): pinned all along; many small scallops.
High (100 cm): only the corners hold, so the top edge sags into deep swags.
Allowed range: 0.02 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.detail:
Simulation cell size: the distance between the particles (default 4 cm, at least 0.8 cm). Smaller gives finer folds and is slower.
High value (8 cm): coarse, broad folds.
Low value (2 cm): many fine folds; about four times as many faces and four times the time.
Allowed range: 0.008 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.quality:
Simulation steps of 1/120 s (30 to 2000, default 240). The simulation stops early once the cloth is at rest.
Low (30): the sheets have not finished falling; little sag and fewer folds on the floor.
High (1000): looks about the same as the default here, and took about three and a half times as long.
Allowed range: 30 to 2000.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.colliders:
Every mesh in this collection is a collider the cloth settles on: floors, rubble, furniture, the beam. Empty: a flat floor under the lowest point of the source.
None: the floor is put at the height of the curve, so the sheets lie flat on top of the beam.
Beam, posts and floor: the sheets hang over the beam and fall to the floor.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.damaged:
Ragged, eaten-away edges and holes.
Off: clean rectangular sheets.
On: ragged hems and a few holes.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.tear:
Depth of the ragged edges, deepest along the hem (0 to 3, default 0.5).
Low (0): straight edges.
High (2): deep tears; sheets break into strips at the bottom.
Allowed range: 0 to 3.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.holes:
Holes per square metre (0 to 10, default 0.4), with ragged rims.
Low (0): no holes.
High (3): sheets full of holes.
Allowed range: 0 to 10.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.wind:
Wind pressure while the cloth settles (0 to 3, default 0.3; 0 is still air).
Low (0): the curtains hang straight down.
High (2): the curtains are blown out at an angle.
Allowed range: 0 to 3.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.wind_directio:
The direction the wind blows (default 1, 0.3, 0: mostly along +X). The images use Wind 1.5.
X: the curtains are blown along the rail.
Y: the curtains billow away from the camera; Z (up): they hang almost straight, with the lower part lifted a little.
Allowed range: no fixed minimum to no fixed maximum.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.turbulence:
Gusts: how much the wind wanders in space and time (0 to 2, default 0.6). The images use Wind 1.5.
Low (0): an even push; all curtains lean the same way.
High (2): uneven billows that differ from sheet to sheet.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.self_collisio:
Cloth never passes through cloth: curtains layer instead of overlapping (on by default; off is faster). With it on, hanging sheets are laid one after another along the curve, and when the curve is full the next row hangs in front. The images use 12 curtains.
Off: the sheets are placed at random along the rail and pass through each other.
On: two neat rows of curtains, one in front of the other.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.self_distance:
The gap kept between cloth layers (default 1 cm; never less than twice the Diameter). Greyed out when Self Collision is off. The images use 12 curtains. Large values make the simulation slow, and in our test 5 cm made it fail: the curtains were crushed into balls.
Low (0.3 cm): the layers lie close together.
High (2.5 cm): the two rows stand further apart, with fuller folds.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.smooth:
A Subdivision modifier (level 1) on the result (on by default).
Off: the faces of the simulation grid show at the folds.
On: smooth folds.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.seed:
Shuffles the sizes, kinds, places and damage of the sheets.
Every number gives a different random arrangement.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.material: Your own material for the result. Empty uses "Curtain Material" for Curtain and "Cloth Default Shader" for the other types. Material only, no image.
ProjectDamageInnerRoughLive.smooth:
Changes shading of faces assigned to the inner material only; it does not displace them.
Off: Off retains the inner faces' current shading.
On: On smooths the inner faces while retaining the outer surface's shading and the sharp boundary rim.
ProjectDamageInnerRoughLive.smooth_angle:
Set Inner Smooth Angle for this generated feature.
Minimum: Keep more folds sharp; only nearly coplanar faces share smooth normals.
Maximum: Allow smoothing across larger folds; feature boundaries remain protected.
Allowed range: 0 degrees to 180 degrees.
ProjectDamageInnerRoughLive.enable:
Recuts neighbouring pieces with one shared noisy Boolean grid, independently implemented, inspired by the shared-grid idea in Destruction Tools. Exterior surfaces and wall contact bound the result.
Off: restore plain pieces.
On: build complementary break faces. Use Show / Update for existing pieces.
ProjectDamageInnerRoughLive.resolution:
Cutter grid density relative to Detail Size.
Minimum 5%: coarse, fast cuts.
100%: use Detail Size directly. Higher values add detail and cost; automatic budgets cap the grid to 192 points per direction.
ProjectDamageInnerRoughLive.strength:
Height of the noisy cutting surface in centimetres, following Master Scale.
Minimum 0: no new relief.
Higher values: deeper recesses and larger matching bulges, capped locally to 22% of the smaller interface dimension. No fixed numeric maximum.
ProjectDamageInnerRoughLive.scale:
Size of the broad noise pattern in centimetres, following Master Scale.
Minimum 0.5: small bumps.
Higher values: wider, slower-changing undulations; no fixed numeric maximum.
ProjectDamageInnerRoughLive.detail:
Target spacing of the cutter grid before Resolution is applied.
Minimum 0.1 cm: fine detail, more Boolean work.
Higher values: fewer grid cells and faster cutting; no fixed numeric maximum. The geometry budget can increase spacing automatically.
ProjectDamageInnerRoughLive.seed:
Seed shared by the roughness field on neighbouring pieces.
Minimum: 0 is the first repeatable field.
Maximum: Other values give a different matching field; do not use different seeds for opposite sides of one boundary.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageInnerRoughLive.proxy:
Keep a plain rigid-body mesh with a detailed render child.
Off: replace the visible mesh, keeping a reversible base.
On: simulate the plain parent and display the detailed child; its deformation follows the parent.
ProjectDamageInnerRough.smooth:
Changes shading of faces assigned to the inner material only; it does not displace them.
Off: Off retains the inner faces' current shading.
On: On smooths the inner faces while retaining the outer surface's shading and the sharp boundary rim.
ProjectDamageInnerRough.smooth_angle:
Set Inner Smooth Angle for this generated feature.
Minimum: Keep more folds sharp; only nearly coplanar faces share smooth normals.
Maximum: Allow smoothing across larger folds; feature boundaries remain protected.
Allowed range: 0 degrees to 180 degrees.
