Keep a plain rigid-body mesh with a detailed render child.
Off: replace the visible mesh, keeping a reversible base.
On: simulate the plain parent and display the detailed child; its deformation follows the parent.
PD_RetopoSettings.backend:
Choose Engine. Instant Meshes: Official Instant Meshes binary (BSD), run as a separate process; QuadriFlow: Blender's built-in quad remesher; Voxel: Blender's voxel remesh: even triangles/quads, closes small gaps.
Instant Meshes: Official Instant Meshes binary (BSD), run as a separate process.
QuadriFlow: Blender's built-in quad remesher.
Voxel: Blender's voxel remesh: even triangles/quads, closes small gaps.
PD_RetopoSettings.edge_length:
Target edge length of the new mesh, in object units.
Minimum: Smaller cells or edges: finer, heavier geometry.
Maximum: Larger cells or edges: coarser, faster geometry that may lose small features.
Allowed range: 1e-05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
PD_RetopoSettings.max_faces:
Set Max Faces per Part for this generated feature.
Minimum: A strict limit: less generated detail or fewer elements, with lower processing cost.
Maximum: Allow more geometry or elements; updates and memory use can increase.
Allowed range: 8 to 2.14748e+09.
PD_RetopoSettings.keep_below:
Loose parts (shards, debris) with fewer faces are copied unchanged.
Minimum: Process even small loose parts.
Maximum: Keep more low-face-count shards unchanged during retopology.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
PD_RetopoSettings.fit_surface:
Move new vertices back onto the original surface of their own part.
Off: omit fit to original while keeping its stored settings.
On: use fit to original with the controls below.
PD_RetopoSettings.smooth_angle:
Edges above this angle, and every border between damage regions, are marked sharp.
Minimum: Keep more folds sharp; only nearly coplanar faces share smooth normals.
Maximum: Allow smoothing across larger folds; feature boundaries remain protected.
Allowed range: 0 to 180.
PD_RetopoSettings.crease_angle:
Instant Meshes: dihedral angle above which an edge is followed as a crease.
Minimum: Keep more folds sharp; only nearly coplanar faces share smooth normals.
Maximum: Allow smoothing across larger folds; feature boundaries remain protected.
Allowed range: 0 to 180.
PD_RetopoSettings.smooth_iterations:
How much the new mesh is smoothed after it is rebuilt.
0: no smoothing, all small detail is kept.
High (10): a very even mesh, but fine damage gets softer.
Allowed range: 0 to 10.
PD_RetopoSettings.quad_dominant:
Instant Meshes: allow triangles instead of splitting every face into quads.
Off: omit quad dominant while keeping its stored settings.
On: use quad dominant with the controls below.
PD_RetopoSettings.seed:
Shuffles the layout of the new faces. Try another number if the result has ugly spots.
Every number gives a different layout.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
PD_RetopoSettings.timeout:
Set Timeout (s) for this generated feature.
Minimum: Earlier timing or a shorter allowed duration.
Maximum: Later timing or a longer allowed duration.
Allowed range: 5 to 2.14748e+09.
PD_RetopoSettings.instant_meshes_path:
Where the Instant Meshes program is on your computer.
Empty: the addon looks for it in the usual places.
Assigned: the program is started from this path.
PDPlankProps.mode:
Proximity damages near each object's current position without needing a drag. Pull Pins stores a rest position and uses displacement from it.
Low / first state: Proximity removes a local region and applies downward Bend Depth.
High / other state: Pull Pins bends toward the moved object and opens a tear once movement exceeds Break Distance.
PDPlankProps.auto_smooth:
Sets smooth face shading and marks sharp edges using Smooth Angle.
Off: Off uses flat face shading.
On: On uses angle-limited smooth shading; this does not round the actual board silhouette.
PDPlankProps.smooth_angle:
Angle threshold for sharp-edge marking, only with Auto Smooth enabled.
Minimum: 0 degrees keeps almost all changes of face normal sharp.
Maximum: 180 degrees permits smoothing across the widest angle range.
Allowed range: 0 degrees to 180 degrees.
PDPlankProps.bend_depth:
Downward displacement vector used by Proximity mode, along local negative Z.
Minimum: 0 creates a local missing region without downward bending.
Maximum: Larger values pull the nearby board geometry farther down; hole radius remains separately controlled.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
PDPlankProps.width:
Total span along local X, in Blender scene units.
Minimum: 0.1 gives a very narrow surface.
Maximum: Larger values expand the surface; board count is derived from the transverse span and spacing, capped internally at 400 per layer.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
PDPlankProps.length:
Total span along local Y, in Blender scene units.
Minimum: 0.1 gives a short surface.
Maximum: Larger values expand its Y span; Horizontal swaps which span is along each board.
Allowed range: 0.1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
PDPlankProps.plank_width:
Nominal board width and top-layer spacing. Actual width is limited to the evenly divided span, then reduced by Gap.
Minimum: 0.02 gives narrow, numerous boards.
Maximum: Larger values give wider, fewer boards; the final span is divided evenly rather than leaving a partial board at the edge.
Allowed range: 0.02 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
PDPlankProps.thickness:
Top-board thickness along negative local Z.
Minimum: 0.002 gives thin boards.
Maximum: Larger values make thick closed boards and move the start of the under layer deeper.
Allowed range: 0.002 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
PDPlankProps.gap:
Empty spacing subtracted from each board's available transverse width.
Minimum: 0 makes adjoining boards meet.
Maximum: Larger gaps separate boards; if Gap consumes their available width, those boards are omitted.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
PDPlankProps.horizontal:
Rotates the top-board direction by 90 degrees in the local XY plane.
Off: Off runs top boards along local Y.
On: On runs top boards along local X; the under layer remains perpendicular.
PDPlankProps.under:
Adds a perpendicular layer beneath the top boards. It uses the same damage objects and warp function.
Off: Off emits top boards only.
On: On emits support boards at Under Spacing, starting below the top layer.
PDPlankProps.under_thickness:
Thickness of the support boards, independent of top-board thickness.
Minimum: 0.002 gives thin supports.
Maximum: Larger values give deeper, closed support boards.
Allowed range: 0.002 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
PDPlankProps.under_spacing:
Spacing between support-board centres across their transverse span.
Minimum: 0.05 gives many closely spaced supports.
Maximum: Larger values give fewer supports; their width still derives from Plank Width and Gap.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
PDPlankProps.seed:
Seed for repeatable splinter offsets at board ends around damage.
Minimum: 0 gives the first break variant.
Maximum: Other integers reroll offsets without changing overall width or length.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
PDPlankProps.radius:
Radius of each object's influence. Bending falls as (1 - (distance/radius)^2)^2. Proximity uses 3D distance; Pull Pins measures distance in the XY plane.
Minimum: A small radius affects a tight region.
Maximum: A large radius bends a broad region; the missing core is smaller than the full bending radius.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
PDPlankProps.break_distance:
Minimum pin displacement before Pull Pins removes board cells.
Minimum: A small threshold tears after little motion.
Maximum: A large threshold allows more bending before removal; it is ignored in Proximity mode.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
PDPlankProps.splinters:
Per-strip random offset of the removal test along the board's long axis. This creates unequal broken ends rather than separate splinter objects.
Minimum: 0 makes a comparatively even break across the board width.
Maximum: Larger values create long, irregular surviving tongues and jagged board ends.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
PDPlankProps.resolution:
Number of longitudinal segments per board; each has six transverse subdivisions before top, bottom and side faces are built.
Minimum: 12 gives coarse bending and stepped breaks.
Maximum: 160 gives finer bends and damage boundaries, with more geometry over every generated board.
Allowed range: 12 to 160.
PDPlankProps.live_update:
Rebuilds the generated surface when relevant controls or linked damage objects change.
Off: Off lets you make edits and then press Update.
On: On automatically reconstructs the boards after relevant changes.
PDPlankProps.material:
Material for the top boards.
Empty: the default wood material is used.
Assigned: the top boards get this material.
PDPlankProps.under_material:
Material for the support boards underneath.
Empty: the same material as the top boards is used.
Assigned: the support boards get this material.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.inner_mater:
Material for the new inside faces of the broken pieces.
Empty: inside faces look like the outside.
Assigned: inside faces get this material.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.smooth_inne:
Enable Auto Smooth Inside Faces for this object.
Off: omit auto smooth inside faces while keeping its stored settings.
On: use auto smooth inside faces with the controls below.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.inner_smoot:
Set Inside Smooth Angle for this generated feature.
Minimum: Keep more folds sharp; only nearly coplanar faces share smooth normals.
Maximum: Allow smoothing across larger folds; feature boundaries remain protected.
Allowed range: 0 degrees to 180 degrees.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.fill_depth:
How deep the fill reaches into the damage.
Auto: Lath effects and Stud Framing: the plaster coat in front of the laths or studs. Concrete, Concrete Hit and Brick Damage: the whole cut.
Whole Cut: Everything the damage removed, around the laths, studs, bricks and rebar.
Surface Layer: Only the layer under the surface, Surface Depth deep.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.surface_dep:
Thickness of the surface layer that is turned into loose pieces, in cm.
Low: a thin crust of pieces.
High: a thick layer of pieces.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.fill_cracks:
Cracks that run out of a damaged area are always filled with it. On: cracks that touch no damaged area get thin fill objects of their own too. Off: they stay visible on the filled wall (anything thinner than Damage Debris Min Thickness is dropped).
Off: omit fill lone cracks while keeping its stored settings.
On: use fill lone cracks with the controls below.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.piece_size:
Target size of pieces created from the fill volume. The Amount Budget caps the count.
Minimum: small pieces and a high estimated count.
Maximum: larger pieces and fewer fractures.
Allowed range: 0.5 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.amount_budg:
Cap the total output fragment count for one Fracture operation before size-based generation. Extra disconnected regions are grouped, not discarded.
Minimum (1): at most one output object.
Maximum: permit more fragments, increasing geometry and simulation work.
Allowed range: 1 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.seed:
Seed shared by the roughness field on neighbouring pieces.
Minimum: 0 is the first repeatable field.
Maximum: Other values give a different matching field; do not use different seeds for opposite sides of one boundary.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.brick_morta:
Brick Damage: what happens to the mortar joints.
With Bricks: Each brick keeps half of the joints around it.
Separate Pieces: The bricks and the mortar joints break apart: every brick also drops its bed joint and its head joint as two thin pieces.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.brick_snap:
Chance that a brick breaks in two.
0: all bricks stay whole.
1: every brick is snapped in half.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.hide_fill:
Hide the fill objects once they are fractured.
Off: omit hide fill while keeping its stored settings.
On: use hide fill with the controls below.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.hit_separat:
Concrete Hit: the cracks around the crater cut through, so the impact plates come apart as loose pieces (Piece Gap, Remove Chunks, Min Piece).
Off: omit separate fragments while keeping its stored settings.
On: use separate fragments with the controls below.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.hit_fill_sh:
Number of shards that fill one hole.
Low (2): a couple of big lumps.
High (600): a mass of small shards, slower to simulate.
Allowed range: 2 to 600.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.hit_fill_ce:
Zero spreads the shards evenly; one packs small shards tightly around the impact centre.
Minimum: Spread fill shards evenly across the impact.
Maximum: Pack smaller shards tightly around the impact centre.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.material:
Selects the partition recipe: stretched grain for Wood, an impact network for planar Glass, or material-specific cellular relief for Concrete, Rock and Soil. This is an algorithm selector, not a Blender material slot.
Low / first state: Choose the type that matches the source structure.
High / other state: Changing it also changes automatic roughness, size variation and rubble defaults when those values are -1.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.grain:
Wood: direction of the fibres.
X: Fibres along the object X axis.
Y: Fibres along the object Y axis.
Z: Fibres along the object Z axis (vertical studs and boards).
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.cut_mode:
What breaks the fill objects.
Automatic: The effect's fracture algorithm only.
Drawn Lines: Only the lines drawn with Grease Pencil break the fills.
Both: The fracture algorithm, then the drawn lines cut through its pieces.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.cut_drawing:
A Grease Pencil drawing or curve whose strokes are break lines. Each stroke cuts straight through the wall.
Empty: no drawn break lines are used.
Assigned: the object breaks along your strokes.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.cut_gap:
Width of a drawn fracture line. Follows Master Scale.
Minimum: Small or closed gaps between neighbouring elements.
Maximum: Larger visible separation between neighbouring elements.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.detach_remo:
Bead, Corner Piles and Deposits: once detached, switch the generator off on the wall and update it, so only the loose objects remain (Undo brings it back).
Off: omit remove from wall while keeping its stored settings.
On: use remove from wall with the controls below.
ProjectDamagePhysicsSettings.bullet_piec:
Usual size of a piece in a crater or bullet hole, in cm.
Low: many fine crumbs, slower.
High: a few big pieces.
Allowed range: 0.05 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.collider_objec:
The object the pieces fall onto or bump into.
Empty: no extra collider is set.
Assigned: the pieces collide with this object.
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.start_frame:
Frame where the simulation starts; before it every piece stays in place.
Minimum: Earlier timing or a shorter allowed duration.
Maximum: Later timing or a longer allowed duration.
Allowed range: -2.14748e+09 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.end_frame:
Last simulated frame.
Minimum: Earlier timing or a shorter allowed duration.
Maximum: Later timing or a longer allowed duration.
Allowed range: -2.14748e+09 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.hold:
What keeps the pieces in the wall until they are hit.
Only Hit Pieces: Every piece stands still until a moving collider touches that very piece; pieces knocked loose do not wake the others.
Wake Together: Pieces sleep until something touches them; touching pieces wake together, so one hit can bring down a whole fill.
Fall at Start: Pieces fall as soon as the simulation starts.
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.hit_margin:
Contact tolerance in centimeters for Only Hit Pieces. Applies to the moving collider, Hit Area and shard contact with Chain Reaction.
At zero, release requires contact with the geometry. Higher values also detect near misses within this distance.
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.shape:
Collision shape of the pieces.
Convex Hull: Fast and stable; the pieces are near convex.
Mesh: Exact shape; slower.
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.density:
How heavy the material is, in kg per cubic metre (concrete 2400, brick 1900, plaster 1200, glass 2500).
Low: light pieces that are easily thrown about.
High: heavy pieces that fall hard and barely move.
Allowed range: 1 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.friction:
Surface friction used by the rigid-body simulation.
Minimum (0): pieces slide easily.
Maximum: resist sliding more strongly; this does not glue pieces together.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.bounce:
Rigid-body restitution.
Minimum (0): impacts lose their bounce.
Maximum (1): highly elastic collisions with strong rebound.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.wall_collider:
The damaged wall (the result) becomes a fixed Mesh collider the pieces rest against.
Off: omit wall is collider while keeping its stored settings.
On: use wall is collider with the controls below.
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.collider_shape:
Collision shape of the colliders.
Mesh: Exact shape.
Convex Hull: Fast; for convex colliders.
ProjectDamageDevState.edit_layout:
Rename and hide controls, pin/reorder quick controls and reorder/hide Add tiles; changes are saved on this computer.
Off: omit edit ui layout while keeping its stored settings.
On: use edit ui layout with the controls below.
ProjectDamageDevState.effect_label:
A new name to show for the selected effect.
Empty: the original name is shown.
Assigned: your name is shown instead.
ProjectDamageDevState.field_label:
A new label to show for the chosen setting.
Empty: the original label is shown.
Assigned: your label is shown instead.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.mask_group:
A vertex group: only edges whose two vertices weigh at least Threshold get a weld. Empty: every matching edge. Paint Mask creates the group and opens Weight Paint; Edit Mask opens Edit Mode, where Assign to Weld Mask adds the selected vertices; Finish Mask returns to Object Mode. The image uses a group on the front corner of the rib.
No mask: the rib corners and the pipe get welds.
Mask: only the front corner of the rib is welded; the pipe has none.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.mask_threshold:
How strongly an area must be painted in the mask group to count for the weld.
Low: even lightly painted areas count.
High: only fully painted areas count.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.edges_enable:
Turns the corner welds on or off (default on). The image also has a drawn weld on the plate.
Off: only the drawn weld is left.
On: the inside corners of the rib and the pipe get fillet welds.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.edge_type:
Which corners get a weld: Inside Corners (concave, fillet welds; default), Outside Corners (beads wrapped over convex edges) or Both.
Inside Corners: the rib and the pipe are welded to the plate.
Outside Corners and Both: every convex edge of the plate, the rib and the pipe top gets a bead too.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.angle:
Corners sharper than this, in degrees, get a weld (1 to 179, default 30). The corners in the image are all 90 degrees.
Low (30 or 89 degrees): the 90 degree corners are welded.
High (91 degrees): the 90 degree corners no longer count; no weld is made.
Allowed range: 1 to 179.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.strokes_enable:
Turns the drawn beads on or off (default on). The image uses a flat 40 x 30 cm plate with one S-shaped curve drawn 2 mm above it.
Off: no weld; the plate has no corners to weld.
On: a bead along the stroke.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.width:
Distance between the two toes of the bead (default 1.2 cm).
Low (0.6 cm): a thin bead.
High (3 cm): a wide bead with more spatter round it.
Allowed range: 0.0001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.height:
Height of the crown above the plates (default 4 mm).
Low (1.5 mm): a flat bead.
High (12 mm): a tall bead standing out of the corner.
Allowed range: 0.0001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.pitch:
Distance between the ripples along the bead (default 3 mm).
Low (1.5 mm): fine, close ripples.
High (10 mm): few, wide ripples.
Allowed range: 0.0001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.ripple_height:
Depth of the ripples, as a share of the bead height (0 to 1, default 0.25).
Low (0): a smooth bead.
High (1): deep scallops, like a stack of coins.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.curvature:
How much the ripples bend into arcs that trail at the toes (0 to 3, default 0.6).
Low (0): straight ripples across the bead.
High (2.5): strongly curved, V-shaped ripples.
Allowed range: 0 to 3.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.wobble:
The welder's hand: width, line, height and ripples vary, and spatter drops are thrown onto the plates (0 to 2, default 0.5; no spatter at 0).
Low (0): a perfectly even bead without spatter.
High (2): an uneven, lumpy bead with spatter.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.sides:
Number of sides round the bead tube (6 to 48, default 16).
Low (6): a faceted, angular bead.
High (48): a smooth section; little difference above 16.
Allowed range: 6 to 48.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.detail:
Sample step along and round the bead (0.01 to 4, default 1). Higher values give a finer, heavier mesh.
Low (0.2): a coarse bead; the ripples are lost.
High (3): finer ripples and toes; the mesh is heavier.
Allowed range: 0.01 to 4.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.uv_scale:
Scale of the bead UV map "UVMap" (U along the bead in Width units, V across). It changes only the texture, not the geometry; no image.
Allowed range: 0.01 to 100.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.seed:
Shuffles the wobble, ripples and spatter of the weld without changing their size.
Every number gives a different random arrangement.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageWeldSettings.material:
Material for the weld seam.
Empty: the default weld material is used.
Assigned: the weld gets this material.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.master_scale:
Scales blade length, width, pile height and the edge, cavity and stroke radii together; the densities change so the spacing between blades scales too (default 100%, multiplies the global Master Scale).
Low (50%): short, fine blades, packed more densely.
High (200%): long, broad blades, spaced further apart.
Allowed range: 0.01% to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.kind: Dry: straw, thin, long, curled, with many broken pieces, lying flat. Fresh: green blades, wider (about 1.6 times) and straighter, with fewer broken pieces and the tips lifted a little. Without a material of your own, each type gets its own default material.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.slope_limit:
Faces steeper than this, in degrees, get no grass (0 to 89, default 35), so walls stay clean. The image uses a piece of ground whose back half is a 30 degree ramp.
Low (20): only the flat front half has grass.
High (35 or 60): the ramp gets grass too.
Allowed range: 0 to 89.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.base_density:
Blades per square metre everywhere on the ground (default 300).
Low (0): grass only near edges and in hollows.
High (1500): an even cover of blades over the whole ground.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.edge_density:
Extra blades per square metre at the foot of walls and kerbs and along crack and chip rims (default 2500).
Low (0): no extra grass at edges.
High (10000): thick lines of grass along the kerb, the groove and the pit rims.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.edge_radius:
How far from an edge the extra Edge Density reaches; it fades out toward this distance (default 6 cm).
Low (2 cm): a thin line hugging the edge.
High (20 cm): a wide band of grass along the edges.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.edge_angle:
Corners sharper than this, in degrees, count as edges (1 to 179, default 25). The image is a close-up of a pit.
Low (10): even soft bends count as edges.
High (100): the 90 degree pit and groove rims no longer count, so the extra grass along them is gone.
Allowed range: 1 to 179.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.cavity_densit:
Extra blades per square metre in cracks, pits and hollows; the more enclosed the spot, the more grass (default 3000). The image is a close-up of a pit.
Low (0): no extra grass in hollows.
High (12000): the pit and the corner along the kerb fill with grass.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.cavity_radius:
How far around a point the cavity test looks for enclosing walls (default 8 cm).
Low (3 cm): only the tightest spots count as hollows.
High (25 cm): larger, shallower hollows also gather grass.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.stroke_mode: Overlay: grass grows only along the strokes; the automatic densities are ignored. Add: the strokes add grass where the field is thinner than Stroke Density; the rest stays.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.stroke_densit:
Blades per square metre along the strokes (default 2500). The image uses Overlay.
Low (500): a sparse trail.
High (10000): a dense band of grass.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.stroke_radius:
How far from the stroke the grass reaches (default 8 cm). The image uses Overlay.
Low (3 cm): a thin line of grass.
High (20 cm): a wide band.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.max_shards:
Upper limit of the number of blades (default 60000). It is multiplied by the global Master Quality of the object. The test ground has about 9000 blades.
Low (1000): the scatter stops early, so the grass is thin everywhere.
High (60000): no limit for this object; all blades the densities ask for are made.
Allowed range: 100 to 2e+06.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.length_min:
Shortest blade (default 3 cm). Each blade gets a length between Length Min and Length Max (Dry grass favours short blades); a share of the blades is then broken shorter.
Low (1 cm): many short bits.
High (10 cm): all blades are long.
Allowed range: 0.0005 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.length_max:
Longest blade (default 14 cm). If it is below Length Min, the two are swapped.
Low (6 cm): short, even blades.
High (30 cm): long straws among the short ones.
Allowed range: 0.0005 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.width:
Width of a blade at its base; each blade varies around it (default 0.36 cm). Fresh blades are 1.6 times wider.
Low (0.15 cm): hair-thin blades.
High (1 cm): broad, leaf-like blades.
Allowed range: 0.0001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.pile_height:
How high blades heap where the grass is dense (default 0.6 cm).
Low (0): every blade lies on the ground.
High (4 cm): blades lift off the ground in the dense spots and stack up. The change is subtle in a still image.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.segments:
Number of segments along a blade (2 to 8, default 4). More segments make the bends smoother.
Low (2): stiff blades with one bend.
High (8): smoothly curved blades, more polygons.
Allowed range: 2 to 8.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.seed:
Shuffles where the blades stand and how they look.
Every number gives a different random arrangement.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageGrassSettings.material:
Material for the grass.
Empty: the default grass material is used.
Assigned: the grass gets this material.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.master_scale:
Multiplies Size Min and Size Max together (default 1). Unlike Grass Scatter it is a plain factor, and it does not change the density or where the stones lie.
Low (0.5): fine grit.
High (2): coarse stones on the same spots.
Allowed range: 0.01 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.rock_subdivi:
Smooths each stone with Loop subdivision (0 to 2, default 0). 0 keeps the angular stones; each level gives four times as many faces.
Low (0): faceted, angular stones.
High (2): round, pebble-like stones. Subdivision also shrinks every stone, and because part of each stone is sunk into the ground, small stones sink below the surface and seem to vanish.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.slope_limit:
Faces steeper than this, in degrees, get no gravel (0 to 89, default 35). The image uses a ground with a 30 degree ramp at the back.
Low (20): only the flat half has gravel.
High (35 or 60): the ramp gets gravel too.
Allowed range: 0 to 89.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.base_density:
Stones per square metre everywhere on the ground (default 150).
Low (0): stones only near edges and in hollows.
High (1000): an even, dense cover.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.edge_density:
Extra stones per square metre at the foot of walls and kerbs and along crack and chip rims (default 900).
Low (0): no extra stones at edges.
High (5000): lines of grit along the groove and around the pits.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.edge_radius:
How far from an edge the extra Edge Density reaches (default 6 cm).
Low (2 cm): stones only right at the edge.
High (20 cm): a wide band of stones along the edges.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.edge_angle:
Corners sharper than this, in degrees, count as edges (1 to 179, default 25).
Low (10): soft bends count as edges too.
High (100): the 90 degree kerb, groove and pit rims no longer count, so fewer stones gather along them.
Allowed range: 1 to 179.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.cavity_densi:
Extra stones per square metre in cracks, pits and hollows (default 1500). The image is a close-up of a pit.
Low (0): no extra stones in hollows.
High (8000): the pit fills with stones.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.cavity_radiu:
How far around a point the cavity test looks for enclosing walls (default 8 cm).
Low (3 cm): only tight spots count as hollows.
High (25 cm): larger hollows gather stones too.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.stroke_mode: Overlay: gravel lies only along the strokes. Add: the strokes add gravel where the field is thinner than Stroke Density; the rest stays.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.stroke_densi:
Stones per square metre along the strokes (default 1500). The image uses Overlay.
Low (300): a sparse trail.
High (8000): a dense path of grit.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.stroke_radiu:
How far from the stroke the stones reach (default 8 cm). The image uses Overlay.
Low (3 cm): a thin line.
High (20 cm): a wide band.
Allowed range: 0.001 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.max_stones:
Upper limit of the number of stones (default 40000), multiplied by the global Master Quality of the object.
Low (500): the scatter stops early and the gravel is thin.
High (40000): no limit on this object; the change from 3000 is small.
Allowed range: 100 to 2e+06.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.size_min:
Smallest stone (default 0.4 cm, times Master Scale).
Low (0.2 cm): many fine grains.
High (1.2 cm): all stones are clearly visible.
Allowed range: 0.0005 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.size_max:
Largest stone (default 2.5 cm, times Master Scale).
Low (1 cm): fine, even grit.
High (6 cm): a few big stones among the grit.
Allowed range: 0.0005 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.size_skew:
How the sizes are spread between Size Min and Size Max (0.2 to 8, default 2.5). Above 1 there are many small stones and few big ones.
Low (0.5): most stones are near Size Max.
High (8): almost all stones are near Size Min.
Allowed range: 0.2 to 8.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.flatness:
Height of a stone as a share of its width (0.1 to 1.5, default 0.55).
Low (0.2): flat chips.
High (1.2): tall, chunky stones.
Allowed range: 0.1 to 1.5.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.angularity:
How much the corners of each stone are pushed in and out (0 to 0.9, default 0.35).
Low (0): even, rounded polyhedra.
High (0.9): sharp, irregular shards.
Allowed range: 0 to 0.9.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.embed:
Share of the height sunk into the ground (0 to 0.9, default 0.3).
Low (0): the stones sit on top of the ground.
High (0.9): only the tips of the stones show.
Allowed range: 0 to 0.9.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.sorting:
Stones get finer where debris gathers, so cracks and pits fill with grit (0 to 0.9, default 0.6).
Low (0): the same size mix everywhere.
High (0.9): only small grit along edges and in hollows. The change shows mainly in those spots.
Allowed range: 0 to 0.9.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.pile_height:
How high stones stack where they gather (default 0.4 cm).
Low (0): every stone lies on the ground.
High (3 cm): stones in dense spots lift and stack. The change is small in open ground.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.seed:
Shuffles where the stones lie and how they look.
Every number gives a different random arrangement.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageGravelSettings.material:
Material for the gravel.
Empty: the default stone material is used.
Assigned: the gravel gets this material.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.placement:
Gaps (default): foam in the narrow gaps of the mesh itself; Max Gap, Min Gap, Samples and Min Openness are shown. Draw: foam along your drawing; the Drawing field, the Add New / Draw, Update and delete buttons and Width are shown.
Gaps: both seams of the boards are filled.
Draw: only the drawn wavy path gets foam; the seams stay empty.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.drawing: Draw mode only. The Grease Pencil object (or a curve object) whose strokes are the foam path. Add New makes a Grease Pencil object "<object>_FoamDrawing", parented to the source, and starts drawing; Draw continues drawing on it; Update leaves drawing and rebuilds the foam; the trash button deletes the drawing. The strokes are read when you leave Draw mode, not while you draw. No image: this is a drawing tool.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.width:
Draw mode only. Bead width of the drawn foam (default 3 cm). Blob size and spacing scale with it.
Low (1.5 cm): a thin, even bead.
High (8 cm): a thick, lumpy rope with large lobes.
Allowed range: 0.002 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.max_gap:
Gaps mode. Gaps up to this wide get foam (default 2 cm). The foam size follows the gap width, not this value.
Low (1.2 cm): only the 1 cm horizontal seam is filled; the 1.5 cm vertical seam is too wide.
High (5 cm): every gap up to 5 cm is filled; here the result is the same as at 2 cm because both seams are narrower.
Allowed range: 0.0005 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.min_gap:
Gaps mode. Gaps narrower than this get no foam (default 0, which also fills surfaces that touch). If Min Gap is above Max Gap, the two are swapped.
Low (0): both seams are filled.
High (1.2 cm): the 1 cm seam is skipped; at 1.8 cm both seams are skipped and no foam is made.
Allowed range: 0 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.samples:
Gaps mode. Surface samples per square metre used to find the gaps (default 40000). More samples find narrow or small gaps more reliably and cost more time.
Low (2000): too few points land in the horizontal seam; the bead breaks into separate lumps.
High (300000): about the same as the default here; raise it only for small or very narrow gaps.
Allowed range: 100 to no fixed maximum. The slider range is a working range, not a hard maximum.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.spacing:
Distance between blobs along the seam, times the gap width (0.2 to 4, default 0.9).
Low (0.4): many overlapping blobs; a smooth, even bead.
High (2.5): fewer blobs; the bead narrows between them into a chain of lumps.
Allowed range: 0.2 to 4.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.min_openness:
Gaps mode. Points deeper in the slit than this openness get no foam, because it would be hidden (0 to 0.6, default 0.08). At the mouth about half of the rays escape.
Low (0): foam is made deep in the gap as well; the visible result hardly changes.
High (0.4): almost every point counts as too deep, and no foam is made.
Allowed range: 0 to 0.6.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.blob_size:
Size of each blob, times the gap width (0.2 to 5, default 1.6).
Low (0.6): a thin line of foam that barely leaves the seam.
High (3.5): a fat bead several times wider than the seam.
Allowed range: 0.2 to 5.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.bulge:
How much the foam swells out of the mouth of the gap (0 to 4, default 1.2).
Low (0): the foam stays almost flush with the boards.
High (3): a thick, rounded bead that stands well out of the seam.
Allowed range: 0 to 4.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.lumpiness:
Noise and small bubble dents on the skin of the foam (0 to 3, default 1).
Low (0): smooth, rounded lobes.
High (3): a rough, crumbly surface.
Allowed range: 0 to 3.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.sag:
On vertical seams the foam sags under its weight: lower and fatter toward the bottom (0 to 3, default 0.6). The image shows the whole vertical seam.
Low (0): the bead keeps the same thickness all the way down.
High (3): the lower lumps get somewhat fatter. The effect is small on a seam this short.
Allowed range: 0 to 3.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.max_blobs:
Upper limit on the number of blobs over the whole object (10 to 500000, default 20000). It keeps very long or dense seams from becoming too heavy.
Low (40): the blobs run out; the bead becomes thin and broken.
High (20000): no limit is reached on these boards (about 220 blobs).
Allowed range: 10 to 500000.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.seed:
Shuffles the lumps, lobes and drips of the foam without changing their size.
Every number gives a different random arrangement.
There is no low or high here, only different variants.
Allowed range: 0 to 2.14748e+09.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.material:
Material for the foam.
Empty: the default foam material is used.
Assigned: the foam gets this material.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.style:
Choose Style.
Foam: One continuous skin with merged lobes, overflow, drips and cuts.
Beads: Separate lumpy beads (the first Foam version).
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.spread:
How far the foam overflows onto the faces round the gap (0 to 3, default 1).
Low (0): the foam stays in a narrow band over the seam.
High (3): the foam spreads wide over the boards on both sides.
Allowed range: 0 to 3.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.cauliflower:
Bulbous lobes grown out of the bead, and smaller lobes out of those (0 to 3, default 1).
Low (0): a plain sausage-like bead with only small lumps.
High (3): large bulbous lobes, typical of foam that kept expanding.
Allowed range: 0 to 3.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.drips:
Share of the bead that runs down a wall below a seam, or hangs as teardrops from a ceiling seam (0 to 1, default 0.35). The image shows the horizontal seam.
Low (0): no drips; the bead ends cleanly.
High (1): drips hang from the whole length of the seam.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.drip_length:
Length of the drips, times the bead radius (0 to 10, default 2.5). Shown only when Drips is above 0. The image uses Drips 1.
Low (0.5): short stubs under the bead.
High (8): the runs break up into separate drops lower down the wall, below the bead.
Allowed range: 0 to 10.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.coverage:
Share of the seam that gets foam (0 to 1, default 1). 1 gives a continuous bead; lower values leave patches of the seam empty.
Low (0.3): only short pieces of bead are left, with long empty stretches.
High (1): one continuous bead.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.trim:
Share of the bead cut flush with a knife, showing the open cells inside (0 to 1, default 0). The cut faces are marked in the foam_cut attribute for the material.
Low (0): no cuts; the bead is as it expanded.
High (1): the whole bead is cut flat, level with the boards; at 0.5 about half of it.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.resolution:
Mesh cell size, times the bead radius (0.04 to 0.6, default 0.14). Smaller values give a finer and heavier mesh. Master Quality refines it further.
High value (0.4): a coarse mesh; lumps and lobes are smoothed away.
Low value (0.06): finer detail than the default; the mesh is several times heavier.
Allowed range: 0.04 to 0.6.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.look:
Choose Look.
Fresh: Pale cream, just cured.
Cured: Typical yellow polyurethane foam.
Aged: Yellowed to orange-brown by sunlight.
White: Off-white foam.
Grey: Grey foam.
Fire-Rated: Red-pink fire-rated foam.
Custom: Your Color and Age.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.color:
Foam colour in the procedural material.
Minimum: Dark or black foam at low RGB values.
Maximum: Bright or white foam at high RGB values; choose the hue with the colour picker.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageFoamSettings.age:
UV yellowing toward orange-brown, stronger on exposed lobes.
Minimum: Fresh, pale foam.
Maximum: Stronger orange-brown ageing, especially on exposed lobes.
Allowed range: 0 to 1.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_draw_tool:
Choose what you want to draw.
Draw Cut splits existing cells along the stroke; Guidance concentrates smaller cells around a separate drawing.
Switching this tool only changes the drawing controls. Existing cut and guidance drawings can work together.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_cut_extend:
Legacy saved setting, no longer used.
Both values preserve finite stroke ends. A stroke must divide a cell before any cut is accepted.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_guidance_drawin:
Primary density layer, evaluated before both cut layers. Smaller cells gather near these strokes; it does not create an exact seam.
Empty: ordinary Cell Fracture distribution. Assigned: use visible Guidance layers at the current frame, within Projection Distance. Through and Surface drawings remain active.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_guidance_amount:
Maximum additional seeds placed around all Guidance strokes, on top of the normal Pieces setting. Clipping, merging or insufficient room can yield fewer pieces.
Minimum 0: disable added guidance seeds.
Maximum 2000: up to 2000 extra seeds; more pieces need more time and memory.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_guidance_radius:
Radius of the surface band in which extra guidance seeds are sampled, in centimeters before Master Scale.
Minimum 0.001 cm: a very narrow band near the line.
Maximum 100000 cm: a very broad area; use realistic values relative to the object size.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_guidance_depth:
How far the density guide reaches inward from the drawn surface, in centimeters before Master Scale.
0: reach the opposite surface. Small positive values concentrate seeds in a shallow layer.
Maximum 100000 cm: full available thickness. Planar fracture always spans the thickness; choose Volume for separate depth layers.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_guidance_fallof:
Concentration of extra seeds within Guidance Radius. Does not change the amount budget.
Minimum 0.25: spread seeds toward the outside of the band.
Maximum 8: concentrate them very tightly at the drawn line.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_guidance_distan:
Maximum gap between a Guidance stroke and the source surface, in centimeters before Master Scale. Farther strokes are ignored.
Minimum 0.001 cm: require almost exact surface contact.
Maximum 100000 cm: accept very distant drawings; normally use a small tolerance.
ProjectDamageProps.cellf_curve_type:
Select the active drawing layer; the other layers remain active.
Guidance: primary layer, adds local seeds before cutting.
Knife Through: projects through depth and stops at earlier crossing cuts.
Knife Surface: only directly touched pieces. Connect two boundaries, or a boundary to a nearby existing cutting stroke; short incomplete strokes are ignored.
ProjectDamageInnerRough.noise_detail:
Number of additional FBM noise layers on the cutter.
Minimum 0: broad single-layer bumps.
Maximum 8: eight smaller noise layers; fine layers need adequate Resolution.
ProjectDamageInnerRough.noise_roughness:
Relative amplitude of each smaller noise layer.
Minimum 0: only the broad pattern.
Maximum 1: fine layers have equal amplitude before normalization.
ProjectDamageInnerRoughLive.noise_detail:
Number of additional FBM noise layers on the cutter.
Minimum 0: broad single-layer bumps.
Maximum 8: eight smaller noise layers; fine layers need adequate Resolution.
ProjectDamageInnerRoughLive.noise_roughn:
Relative amplitude of each smaller noise layer.
Minimum 0: only the broad pattern.
Maximum 1: fine layers have equal amplitude before normalization.
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.material_prese:
Sets density, friction and bounce. Concrete: 2400 kg/m³, 0.65 friction, 0.05 bounce. Wood: 650 kg/m³, 0.5 friction, 0.15 bounce.
Changing the material does not change gravity or free-fall acceleration. Enable / Update Physics applies the chosen values.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_resolution:
Local mesh density around peeled areas. 50% is the fast default; 100% matches the former Detail 24. Master Quality multiplies this setting.
Minimum: 1% gives coarse contours and bends.
Maximum: 400% resolves finer edges but increases time and memory. Face Budget limits refinement; added coating and substrate faces can exceed that budget.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_wrap_edges:
Let patches, cuts and flaps continue over sharp edges and corners.
Off: peeling stops short of sharp edges and they stay intact.
On: the coating peels around edges and corners. Open borders, other effects and very sharp folds stay protected.
ProjectDamageProps.peeling_damage_factor:
How far the damage has gone.
Low: a network of thin cracks with slightly raised plate edges; no paint is lost.
Middle: some plates curl more and a few flake off.
1: full peeling, as set by the other controls.
Low values need a fine mesh: raise Face Budget or Resolution if cracks look broken.
ProjectDamageProps.boolean_wood_deepness:
Depth of the Boolean wooden layer below the source surface, before Scale and Master Scale. Default: 12 cm.
Minimum (0 cm): place boards immediately behind the surface.
Maximum (50 cm): place them deeper; the source must have enough thickness. Applies to Boolean Planks and Laths.
ProjectDamageClothSettings.live_update:
Automatically recalculate Cloth Sheets when its settings, assigned curve, source empties or colliders change.
Off: keep the current cloth until you press Update Cloth Sheets.
On (default): recalculate after the last edit; moving Cloth Hanging Curve repositions the cloth. Material changes update shading without rerunning the simulation.
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.live_updat:
Rebuilds the torn sheet by itself every time you change a setting or move a Blast Point
Off: nothing changes until you press Update. Good for heavy scenes
On: every change is shown right away, but each change costs a rebuild
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.seed:
Shuffles where the damage lands and how it looks, without changing its amount or size
Every number gives a different random arrangement
There is no low or high here, only different variants. More damage comes from the other sliders
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.resolution:
How fine the mesh of the torn sheet is, in percent of the normal detail. Changes smoothness and speed, not the size of the damage
Low (5%): coarse, faceted shapes that build very fast. Good while you are still trying things out
High (400%): very fine edges and small details, but a heavy mesh and slow updates

Size of one mesh cell. This is the same control as Resolution in percent, shown as a length
Low: tiny cells, fine detail, slow and heavy
High: big cells, rough shapes, fast
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.max_verts:
Safety limit for the size of the mesh. If the mesh would go over it, the detail is lowered by itself
Low: the mesh always stays light, but fine detail is lost on big objects
High: big objects keep fine detail, but the mesh can get very heavy
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.uv_scale:
How many times the texture repeats per metre of the surface
Low: the texture is stretched large, few repeats
High: the texture is small and repeats many times
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.mode:
Chooses what gets torn
New Sheet: a fresh metal sheet is built from nothing, using Width and Height
On an Object: the same damage is cut into your own object. The original is hidden and the result follows it when you edit it
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.source:
The object that gets the damage in On an Object mode. Its size is used, its position in the scene is not
Empty: nothing is built in On an Object mode
Picked: that object is copied, torn and kept up to date
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.hide_sourc:
Hides your original object so only the torn copy is seen
Off: the original stays visible and overlaps the torn copy
On: the original is hidden in the viewport and in renders
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.width:
Size of the new sheet from left to right
Low: a narrow strip of metal
High: a wide panel
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.height:
Size of the new sheet from bottom to top
Low: a short strip of metal
High: a tall panel
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.thickness:
How thick the metal is
0: paper-thin, a single surface with no edge thickness. Lightest mesh
High: a thick plate with visible cut edges
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.corrugatio:
Turns the flat sheet into wavy roofing metal. This is the height of the waves
0: a flat sheet
High: deep, strong waves

Distance from one wave top to the next on a corrugated sheet
Low: many narrow waves close together
High: few wide waves

Shape of the waves on a corrugated sheet
Off: soft rounded waves, like classic roofing sheet
On: flat-topped boxy ribs, like trapezoid cladding
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.bend:
Bends the whole sheet into an arc, like a panel wrapped around a barrel
0: the sheet stays straight. Below zero it bends the other way
High: a tight curl with a small radius
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.bend_angle:
Turns the direction in which the sheet is bent
0: the bend runs along the sheet
High: the bend is rotated across the sheet, up to a full turn
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.warp:
Gentle unevenness of the whole sheet, so it does not look machine-flat
0: perfectly flat
High: a visibly wobbly, buckled sheet
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.warp_scale:
Size of the soft waves made by Warp
Low: many small ripples
High: a few broad, lazy waves
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.blasts:
How many blast holes are placed at random. Blast Points you add by hand come on top of this number
0: no random holes, only your Blast Points
High: the sheet is riddled with blast holes
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.blast_size:
Smallest blast hole, measured as the length of its torn petals. Each hole picks a size between Size Min and Size Max
Low: some holes are small stars
High: even the smallest hole is big

Largest blast hole, measured as the length of its torn petals
Low: no hole grows big
High: some holes become huge torn stars
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.blast_side:
Which way the torn metal petals are pushed out. Works for random holes and for Blast Points
Out of the Front: petals curl toward the front of the sheet, as if hit from behind
Out of the Back: petals curl toward the back, as if hit from the front
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.petals_min:
Fewest metal petals a blast hole can have. Each hole picks a number between Petals Min and Petals Max
Low (3): some holes open as a simple three-point star
High: every hole has many narrow petals
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.petals_max:
Most metal petals a blast hole can have
Low: holes stay simple, with a few wide petals
High: some holes split into many thin strips
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.hole_size:
How much of the centre is blown away completely, compared with the petal length
0: no open hole, the petals meet in the middle
High (0.9): a big open hole with short stubs of petals around it
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.petal_gap:
How far the petals are pulled apart from each other at the hole
0: petals touch along their tears
High: wide gaps between thin petals
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.petal_curl:
How far the petals roll back away from the blast
0: petals stay flat in the sheet. Around 0.5 they stand straight up
High: petals roll all the way back onto the sheet
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.curl_rando:
Lets each petal curl by its own amount
0: all petals curl the same, looks neat
High: some petals barely lift while others roll right over
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.petal_twis:
Twists each petal around its own length, like a wrung strip
0: petals are not twisted
High: strongly twisted, chaotic petals
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.petal_crum:
Folds along the petals and crushed petal tips
0: smooth, clean petals
High: heavily creased petals with crumpled ends
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.slit_rando:
How uneven the tears are: different petal lengths, angles and curved rips
0: a regular, even star
High: a messy, lopsided hole
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.jagged:
Roughness of every torn edge
0: clean, knife-cut edges
High: very ragged, saw-toothed edges
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.bulge:
Pushes the metal around a hole outward, as the blast would. Measured against the petal length
0: the sheet stays flat around the hole
High: a tall dome around each hole
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.bulge_radi:
How far from the hole the bulge spreads, counted in petal lengths
Low: a tight bump right at the hole
High: a wide, gentle swelling over a large area
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.punctures:
Number of small shrapnel holes, each with a few tiny petals
0: no small holes
High: the sheet is peppered with shrapnel holes
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.puncture_s:
Smallest shrapnel hole. Each one picks a size between Size Min and Size Max
Low: pin-prick holes are possible
High: even the smallest puncture is clearly visible

Largest shrapnel hole
Low: all punctures stay tiny
High: some punctures become small blast holes
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.tears:
Number of long rips in the sheet, with their lips bent open
0: no rips
High: the sheet is slashed many times
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.tear_lengt:
Shortest rip. Each rip picks a length between Length Min and Length Max
Low: short nicks are possible
High: every rip is long

Longest rip
Low: only short rips
High: some rips run across much of the sheet
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.tear_width:
How wide a rip gapes at its widest point
0: a closed crack, barely visible
High: a wide open gash
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.tear_open:
How far the two lips of a rip are bent outward
0: lips stay flat in the sheet
High: lips are folded right out
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.dents:
Number of dents hammered into the sheet at random
0: no dents
High: a badly battered sheet
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.dent_size_:
Smallest dent. Each dent picks a size between Size Min and Size Max
Low: small dings are possible
High: every dent is wide

Largest dent
Low: only small dings
High: some dents are big hollows
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.dent_depth:
How deep a dent is compared with its width
0: dents are invisible
High: deep bowls
ProjectDamageMetalGenSettings.dent_sharp:
Shape of the dent
0: a soft round bowl, like a push from a ball

How many times the texture repeats per metre of the surface

High: the texture is small and repeats many times

ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.board:

Custom: you set the three sizes yourself
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.length:
Length of the board along the wood fibres
Low: a short stub
High: a long board
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.width:
Width of the board
Low: a narrow strip
High: a wide plank
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.thickness:
Thickness of the board
Low: a thin slat
High: a heavy beam
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.layers:
How many fibre layers the board has through its thickness. Each layer snaps at its own place

High: the broken end is stepped in many thin ragged layers

ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.break_angle:

ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.break_gap:

High: the pieces are clearly separated
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.break_jag:

ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.splinter_wi:
Narrowest splinter. Each splinter picks a width between Width Min and Width Max

High: every splinter is a thick stake

Widest splinter
Low: only thin slivers
High: some broad chunks stick out
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.splinter_le:
Length of the short splinters
Low: short stubby teeth
High: even the short splinters are long

Length of the long splinters
Low: no splinter sticks out far
High: some very long spears stick out of the break
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.long_share:
How many of the splinters are long ones
0: only short splinters, a blunt break
1: almost all splinters are long, a wild shattered break
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.tip_shape:
Shape of the splinter tips
0: blunt, squared-off tips
1: needle-sharp tips
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.splinter_li:
Splinters peel away from the board: top layers lift up, bottom layers hang down
0: splinters stay in line with the board
High: splinters fan out strongly
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.splinter_sw:
Splinters bend sideways
0: all splinters point straight along the fibres
High: splinters lean left and right in a messy way
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.splinter_ga:
Width of the cracks between neighbouring splinters
0: splinters sit tight together
High: clear open gaps between splinters
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.crack_depth:
How far the cracks between splinters run back into the solid board
0: cracks stop right at the break
High: long cracks run deep into the board
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.layer_shift:
How differently the fibre layers break from one another
0: all layers break at the same place
1: every layer breaks at its own place, a ragged stepped end
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.splits:
Number of long splits along the fibres, where the board forks

High: the board is split into several long fingers
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.split_lengt:
How far a split runs back from the end, compared with the piece length

High (0.95): the split runs almost the whole piece
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.split_open:
How far a split gapes at the end of the board

High: the two halves spread wide apart
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.split_jag:
Torn fibres along the walls of a split
0: smooth split walls
High: rough, stringy split walls
ProjectDamageWoodGenSettings.grain_rough:
Small fibre teeth on all torn edges that run along the wood
0: clean edges
High: strongly frayed, hairy edges

High: large slabs, few of them
ProjectDamageTileGenSettings.tile_height:
Height of one tile

High: tall tiles
ProjectDamageTileGenSettings.tile_thickn:

High: chunky floor tiles

ProjectDamageTileGenSettings.corner_radi:

High: clearly rounded corners

How the tiles are laid

How many damage zones are placed at random. Impact Points you add by hand come on top of this number

ProjectDamageTileGenSettings.missing:
How many tiles are knocked off completely in the middle of a zone

1: the centre of every zone is stripped bare

How many tiles in a zone came loose and sit crooked

1: most tiles in a zone are tilted

ProjectDamageTileGenSettings.crack_lengt:

Width of the cracks that cut through tiles

ProjectDamageTileGenSettings.crack_jag:

High: ragged, chipped crack edges

High: pieces are clearly shifted and stepped
ProjectDamageTileGenSettings.piece_tilt:

High: pieces are strongly tipped
ProjectDamageTileGenSettings.chips:
Chipped tile edges and corners inside the damage zones
0: no chips
High: almost every edge in a zone is chipped
ProjectDamageTileGenSettings.chip_size:

High: big broken-off corners
ProjectDamageTileGenSettings.chip_depth:
How deep a chip goes, compared with the tile thickness

High (0.9): chips go almost through the tile
ProjectDamageTileGenSettings.scatter_chi:

ProjectDamageErosionGenSettings.size_z:

High: a tall shape

ProjectDamageErosionGenSettings.block_wi:

ProjectDamageErosionGenSettings.block_he:

ProjectDamageErosionGenSettings.pit_dept:
