Higher: the throw direction turns around the crater, 360 is a full turn
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.irregular:
Roughness of the crater outline and its floor
0: a clean round bowl
High: a ragged outline and a rubble-filled floor
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.clods:
Lumps of soil lying on the thrown-out blanket
0: smooth soil
High: very lumpy, cloddy soil
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.clod_size:
Size of the soil lumps
Low: fine crumbs
High: big clods
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.pavement:
What covers the ground
Bare Ground: soil only, no hard surface
Asphalt: one layer that breaks into plates. Concrete Slabs: square slabs with joints
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.pavement_:
Thickness of the asphalt or concrete layer
Low: a thin skin that breaks into thin flakes
High: thick heavy plates
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.hole_size:
How far out the hard surface is ripped away completely, compared with the crater radius
Low (0.3): the surface survives almost to the centre
High: bare soil far beyond the crater rim
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.plate_siz:
Size of the broken plates around the rim. Plates get bigger further out
Low: small rubble-like pieces
High: big slabs
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.crack_wid:
Width of the cracks between plates
0: closed hairline cracks
High: wide open gaps
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.crack_rea:
How far out the surface is broken into plates, compared with the crater radius
Low (0.5): only a narrow ring is broken
High: plates are broken far away from the crater
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.radial_cr:
Number of long cracks running outward beyond the broken zone
0: no long cracks
High: many long cracks in all directions
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.crack_len:
Length of those long cracks, compared with the crater radius
0: no long cracks
High: cracks run far across the ground
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.plate_til:
How strongly the plates at the rim are pushed up and tilted, in degrees
0: plates stay flat
High (60): plates stand up steeply
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.slab_size:
Size of one concrete slab, which sets where the joints are
Low: many small slabs
High: a few large slabs
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.debris:
Number of loose pieces thrown around: stones, clods and bits of pavement
0: no loose pieces
High: debris everywhere, heavier mesh
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.debris_si:
Size of the largest loose pieces
Low: only gravel
High: big chunks among the debris
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.debris_sp:
How far the loose pieces are thrown, compared with the crater radius
0: pieces stay at the rim
High: pieces fly far from the crater
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.debris_in:
How many of the loose pieces fell back into the crater
0: the crater floor is clear
1: all pieces lie inside the crater
ProjectDamageCraterGenSettings.scorch:
Burnt, blackened ground around the crater. It is stored for the material to use
0: no burn mark
High: a strong, wide burn mark
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.width:
Width of the paper sheet, in cm
Low: a narrow strip of paper
High: a wide sheet or poster
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.height:
Height of the paper sheet, in cm
Low: a short slip
High: a tall sheet or poster
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.resolution:
Size of one mesh cell of the paper, in cm. Changes how fine the tears and creases can be, not their size
Low: tiny cells, crisp fine tears and creases, slow and heavy
High: big cells, soft blurry creases, fast
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.thickness:
Thickness of the paper, in cm
0: a single thin surface, lightest mesh
High: thick card with a back side and visible edges
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.quads:
Keeps a tidy square grid in the untouched middle of the sheet
Off: the whole sheet is made of triangles
On: square cells away from tears, triangles only near torn borders
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.seed:
Shuffles wrinkles, holes and torn edges without changing their amount or size
Every number gives a different random arrangement
There is no low or high here, only different variants
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.max_verts:
Safety limit for the size of the paper mesh
Low: the mesh stays light, but fine tears and creases get rougher
High: fine detail is kept, but the mesh can get very heavy
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.edge_rough:
Unevenness of the outer border of the sheet where it is not torn
0: perfectly straight machine-cut borders
1: wobbly, hand-cut looking borders
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.crumple_stren:
How hard the paper was crumpled
0: no random creases at all
High (3): a sheet that was squeezed into a ball and opened again
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.crumple_size:
Distance between the big creases, in cm
Low: many small creases close together
High: a few large folds
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.crumple_detai:
How much fine wrinkling sits on top of the big folds
0: only big folds
1: lots of small wrinkles everywhere
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.crumple_sharp:
Shape of the creases
0: soft rounded wrinkles, like damp paper
1: sharp fold lines with flat facets between them, like dry paper
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.waviness:
Broad lazy waves across the whole sheet
0: the sheet lies flat
1: a strongly wavy sheet
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.wave_size:
Length of those broad waves, in cm
Low: many short waves
High: one or two long swells
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.folds_x:
Number of straight folds across the sheet, spaced from left to right
0: no folds
High: the sheet is folded like a fan
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.folds_y:
Number of straight folds across the sheet, spaced from bottom to top
0: no folds
High: the sheet is folded like a fan
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.fold_depth:
How far the straight folds stick up and down, in cm
0: the folds are flat and invisible
High: deep zigzag folds
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.torn_width:
How far a torn edge may wander away from the line where the paper was meant to tear, in cm
0: tears follow their line exactly, almost like a cut
High: tears stray far and look wild
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.torn_scale:
Size of the big lumps along a tear, in cm
Low: fine, nervous tear lines
High: big sweeping curves
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.tongues:
Long pointed strips of paper left behind along a tear
0: no strips, an even tear
1: many long strips
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.tongue_stretc:
How long those strips are compared with their width
Low (1): short stubby points
High (8): long thin ribbons
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.tongue_angle:
The direction the paper was pulled when it tore. The strips point this way
0: pulled along the sheet
Turning the angle turns the strips around, a full turn brings them back
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.tongue_angle_:
How much the pull direction changes along a tear
0: all strips point the same way
1: strips point in mixed directions
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.torn_detail:
Small teeth and fibres on torn edges
0: smooth torn edges
1: fuzzy, fibrous torn edges
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.flakes:
Small loose bits of paper kept near the tears
0: no loose bits
1: all loose bits are kept
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.peel_width:
Width of the strip along tears where the printed top layer has peeled off, in cm. It is stored for the material to use
0: no peeled strip
High: a wide white strip along every tear
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.rag_size:
Size of the bumps along the rims of holes, in cm
Low: fine, busy rims
High: big, slow curves
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.jagged:
How strongly the rims of holes jump in and out
0: smooth rims
1: sharply jagged rims
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.fiber:
Fine fibre fuzz on the rims of holes
0: clean rims
1: hairy, fibrous rims
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.roundness:
Softens the outline of holes
0: angular, torn-looking holes
1: rounded, worn-looking holes
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.tear_gap:
Distance between torn pieces that are kept, in cm
0: pieces sit as close as possible, the tear is a thin line
High: pieces are pulled well apart
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.keep_pieces:
What happens to the parts that are torn off
Off: only the largest piece of the sheet is kept
On: every torn-off piece that is big enough is kept too
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.min_piece:
Throws away torn pieces that are too small, compared with the largest piece
0: even the tiniest scraps are kept
1: only pieces as big as the largest one are kept
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.edge_curl:
Lifts torn edges up from the sheet
0: torn edges lie flat
1: torn edges curl up strongly
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.curl_width:
How far in from a torn edge the lifting reaches, in cm
Low: only the very rim lifts
High: a wide band lifts
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.edge_dist_max:
How far from edges and tears the distance information for the material reaches, in cm
Low: only a thin line along edges can be shaded differently
High: a wide band along edges can be shaded differently
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.hole_amount:
Number of holes made at random inside the sheet
0: no random holes
High: a sheet full of holes
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.hole_size_min:
Smallest random hole, in cm. Each hole picks a size between Minimum and Maximum
Low: tiny holes are possible
High: every hole is big
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.hole_size_max:
Largest random hole, in cm
Low: all holes stay small
High: some holes are very big
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.hole_irregula:
How lumpy the outline of random holes is
0: round holes
1: blobby, uneven holes
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.hole_elongati:
How much random holes are stretched
0: round holes
1: long slot-like holes
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.hole_margin:
Keeps random holes away from the border of the sheet, in cm
0: holes may touch the border
High: holes stay in the middle
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.corner_tears:
How many corners of the sheet are torn off
0: all four corners are whole
4: every corner is torn off
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.corner_size_m:
Smallest torn-off corner, in cm
Low: tiny corner tips may go missing
High: every torn corner is large

Largest torn-off corner, in cm
Low: only small corner tips are lost
High: some corners lose a big triangle
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.edge_bites:
Number of pieces ripped out of the border of the sheet
0: the border is whole
High: the border is full of ripped-out notches
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.bite_size_min:
Narrowest piece ripped out of the border, in cm
Low: small nicks are possible
High: every bite is wide
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.bite_size_max:
Widest piece ripped out of the border, in cm
Low: all bites stay small
High: some bites are very wide
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.bite_depth:
How deep a bite reaches into the sheet, compared with its width
0: shallow scallops
1: bites as deep as they are wide
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.stroke_hole_w:
Width of the gash cut along a line you draw on the Hole layer, in cm
0: a thin slit
High: a wide ripped-open gash
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.tear_snap:
If a drawn tear ends this close to the border, it is carried on to the border so the piece comes off, in cm
0: tears stop exactly where your stroke stops
High: tears that end far from the border are still carried to it
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.close_share:
How willingly an almost-closed drawn outline is treated as a closed loop
0: only outlines you really closed count as loops
1: even wide-open strokes are closed into loops
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.paint_only:
What happens to the random holes and tears when you have drawn your own
Off: your drawing is added on top of the random damage
On: once the drawing has usable strokes, only the drawing is used
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.drawing:
Grease Pencil object with your strokes. Lines on the Tear layer tear the paper, lines on the Hole layer cut holes
Empty: only the random damage is used
Picked: the paper is torn and cut where you drew
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.smooth:
Shading of the sheet
Off: every face is shown flat, a faceted look
On: the sheet is shaded smooth and only sharp creases stay crisp
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.front_materia:
Material for the front of the paper
Empty: the built-in paper material is used
Picked: your material is used on the front
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.back_material:
Material for the back of the paper
Empty: the built-in paper material is used
Picked: your material is used on the back
ProjectDamagePaperSettings.edge_material:
Material for the thin edge walls of the paper, visible when Thickness is above zero
Empty: the built-in paper material is used
Picked: your material is used on the edges
ProjectDamageProps.paper_generator_enabl:
Turns this object into an editable sheet of paper that can be crumpled, folded and torn
Off: no paper is generated
On: the paper sheet is built with the settings below
ProjectDamageProps.fabric_fibre_model:
How the loose threads at torn cloth edges are built
Loose Fibres: separate fringe threads and hanging strands, the older look
Woven Fibres: threads stay connected in a criss-cross weave and follow the outline of the tear
ProjectDamageProps.wallpaper_finder:
An Empty that tells the wallpaper which wall to cover. Put it close to that wall
Empty field: every suitable wall is covered
Picked: only the wall face next to the Empty gets wallpaper
ProjectDamageProps.wallpaper_tear_diagon:
Lets each tear have its own slope instead of all tears sharing one
0%: every tear uses the Tear Diagonal value
100%: each tear picks its own slope, from level to steep
ProjectDamageProps.wallpaper_tear_from_t:
Lets tears start at different heights on each strip
0%: every tear starts where Tear From Top says
100%: some tears start at the top and others lower down
ProjectDamageProps.wallpaper_flap_curl_f:
Lets each hanging flap curl and fold by its own amount
0%: all flaps use the set curl and fold
100%: every flap is different, from flat to fully rolled
ProjectDamageProps.wallpaper_flap_wave_r:
Lets each hanging flap be more or less wavy than the others
0%: all flaps use the Flap Wave value
100%: every flap is different, from smooth to very wavy
ProjectDamageProps.draft_enable:
Works with a lighter, faster preview while you are still adjusting things. The final quality is not touched
Off: the preview is built at full Master Quality
On: the preview uses Draft Quality. Apply All still builds the final result at full quality
ProjectDamageProps.draft_quality:
How detailed the fast preview is while Draft Mode is on
Low (10%): very rough but very fast preview
High (400%): a preview finer than the final setting, slow and memory-hungry
ProjectDamageProps.chip_seed:
Shuffles where edge chips sit and how they look, without changing their amount or size
Every number gives a different random arrangement. 0 keeps the original pattern
There is no low or high here, only different variants
ProjectDamageProps.surf_seed:
Shuffles where surface damage sits and how it looks, without changing its amount or size
Every number gives a different random arrangement. 0 keeps the original pattern
There is no low or high here, only different variants
ProjectDamageProps.fract_paint_scale:
Overall size of the cracks grown from your drawn strokes: their width, depth and side branches together
Low (10%): thin, shallow cracks with short branches
High (400%): wide, deep cracks with long branches
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_paint_amount:
Number of side cracks that grow out of your drawn strokes
0: only the drawn cracks, no branches
High: many branches, a dense crack web
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_paint_amount:
Number of small cracks that grow out of the side cracks
0: no small cracks
High: a fine web of small cracks
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_paint_length:
Shortest side crack, in cm. Each one picks a length between Length Min and Length Max. A border or another crack can stop it sooner
Low: some side cracks are short stubs
High: every side crack is long

Longest side crack, in cm. A border or another crack can stop it sooner
0: a short automatic length is used
High: side cracks can run far across the surface
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l2_paint_distor:
How crooked the side cracks are. Your drawn cracks do not change
0%: straight side cracks
100%: strongly winding, irregular side cracks

Distance between the bends of the side cracks, in cm. Only matters when Distortion is above zero
Low: many small, quick turns
High: wide, slow curves
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_paint_length:
Shortest small crack, in cm. Each one picks a length between Length Min and Length Max. A border or another crack can stop it sooner
Low: some small cracks are tiny stubs
High: every small crack is long

Longest small crack, in cm. A border or another crack can stop it sooner
0: a short automatic length is used
High: small cracks can run far
ProjectDamageProps.fract_l3_paint_distor:
How crooked the small cracks are. Your drawn cracks do not change
0%: straight small cracks
100%: strongly winding, irregular small cracks

Distance between the bends of the small cracks, in cm. Only matters when Distortion is above zero
Low: many small, quick turns
High: wide, slow curves
ProjectDamagePreferences.default_view_mo:
How the list of effects is shown when you add one
Compact: one small thumbnail viewer, then Apply
Full Preview: a full grid of preview pictures
ProjectDamagePreferences.auto_setup_reba:
When you add a Boolean asset, fits its inner layer (rebar, bricks, boards) to openings that already exist
Off: you place and fit the inner layer yourself
On: the inner layer is fitted to existing openings for you
ProjectDamagePreferences.cache_intermedi:
Remembers half-finished results so the next update does not start from zero. The final look is the same either way
Off: less memory used, but every update recalculates everything
On: faster repeated updates, at the cost of more memory
ProjectDamagePreferences.incremental_upd:
Recalculates only the effect you just changed and reuses the rest. Needs Cache Intermediate Geometry
Off: every change rebuilds all effects on the object
On: only the changed effect is rebuilt, much faster on objects with several effects
ProjectDamagePreferences.save_all_mesh_s:
Keeps hidden backup copies of the object each time you press Apply
Off: only the very first mesh is kept, the scene stays light
On: a hidden copy of every earlier stage is kept, safer but the file grows
ProjectDamagePreferences.low_details_mod:
Starts every new effect at low detail so weak computers stay responsive. Effects you already have are not changed
Off: new effects start at normal detail
On: new effects start at 20% detail and bigger cells
ProjectDamagePreferences.background_cpu_:
How much computer power the background calculation may take while you keep working. The result looks the same either way
Low (10%): Blender stays smooth, the calculation takes much longer
High (100%): the calculation finishes fastest, Blender may feel slower meanwhile
ProjectDamagePreferences.fracture_surfac:
Experimental. Uses a smoothed copy of the surface to steer cracks and surface effects, so bevels and bumps do not throw them off. Your mesh is not changed
Off: the original behaviour
On: cracks and surface effects follow the smoothed guide
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.hit_area:
A sphere Empty that sets pieces free when it reaches them, used with Only Hit Pieces. Move, scale or animate it. It does not push anything by itself
Empty field: no pieces are released by a hit area
Picked: pieces the sphere touches are released
ProjectDamageQuickPhysics.chain_reaction:
With Only Hit Pieces: pieces that are already flying can knock their neighbours loose
Off: only pieces touched by the Hit Area are released
On: moving pieces release the held pieces they bump into, so the break spreads
ProjectDamagePreparation.thickness:
Thickness given to the working copy of a thin or open object so it can be damaged as a solid. Your original stays as it is
Low: a thin shell
High: a deep, solid body
ProjectDamageCollider.object:
An object the falling pieces should bump into. Pick it with the eyedropper
Empty: this slot does nothing
Picked: the object becomes a solid obstacle for the pieces
ProjectDamageCollider.motion:
Tells the simulation whether this obstacle moves
Auto: it is worked out from the animation on the object. Static: a fixed obstacle that never moves
Animated: the obstacle follows its animation and pushes the pieces
ProjectDamageProximityPoint.obj:
An object or Empty that causes damage where it touches the source
Empty: this row does nothing
Picked: damage appears around that object
ProjectDamageProximityPoint.enabled:
Switches this damage point on or off without removing it
Off: the point is ignored
On: the point causes damage
ProjectDamageProximityPoint.use_size:
Where the size of the damage around this point comes from
Off: the Radius field is used
On: the display size and scale of the Empty are used, so scaling the Empty resizes the damage
ProjectDamageProximityPoint.radius:
Size of the damage around this point, in cm. The object must touch the source inside this distance
Low: a small local opening
High: a wide opening
